hmmc-elite.lens: manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The model gives 28.0/31.1 K with PCM and 30.0/35.0 K with the same paste, against 34.4/44.2 K. The cut in the maximum is the most robust gain. The like-for-like mean margin is only 4.4 K, which sits inside the +/-25 % model band. About 3.3 K of that margin comes from the 1.0 mm tied base, and the process to build that base is unproven (see fatal flaws). With a 2 mm base, the same-paste average is about 33.3 K, roughly parity.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The robust core misses Tcase 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with liquid metal (93 C). The P core reaches 84 C only behind <=33 um loop filtration. At 38-45 W/cm2 Rubin-class flux, the average is 1-2 K worse than a split-flow plate with a pad; it wins only on max dT and dP. The proposal admits this. Also, G-RUB shows the '350 W/cm2 real 2027-28 package' is a 2029+ stress case, not Rubin Ultra (~87 W/cm2 die average).

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: This is the best-argued part: 6 kPa port-to-port, an inertial orifice comb that keeps uniformity independent of flow, and coupling classes stated explicitly (UQD12-class at 15 kW, UQD08 for Rubin). Marked down because the proposal breaks its own velocity rule: ports run 2.2 m/s at 150 % flow and 3.0 m/s at the advertised 36 LPM point. The comb also sits at the slot bottom, so its jets hit the fins after 1.5 mm, against the physics rule of placing it at the slot top. The momentum coefficient theta_c is still unmeasured.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: The manifold tiles while flow length stays at 4 mm, so large packages and wafer-scale tiling are physically sound. Reaching 30 kW needs liquid metal or the filtration-gated P core, plus 20 mm ports. Mass (2.3 kg at 148 mm) and diffusion-bond press force (proportional to area) both scale badly with footprint.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: The joining process of record, a one-shot 850-950 C / 5-10 MPa diffusion bond of six layers, cannot coexist with 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins. The fins creep or collapse at about 0.86 Tm, and the 82 %-open plenum leaves fin tips under the slots with no path for bonding pressure. Cover spans over troughs and loops sag. The tip-bond quality cannot be inspected in production, and furnace capacity, copper cost and yield are all understated. A staged braze/TLP-plus-weld route probably exists, but it is not the one costed or scheduled.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Strengths: all-Cu wetted path with no filler, slot-end bleeds, hierarchical passage widths, explicit MAWP/proof/burst and an OCP test matrix. Weaknesses: the tie stress is about 3-6x higher than claimed, so the burst margin is unproven. The per-plate threaded screen is a field-service item, and its dP signature cannot be seen in a 72-plate rack. Comb jets hit annealed fin tips. The ENi wetted-path option is impossible at bonding temperature, and the plate is 2.3 kg and 21-23 mm tall.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The base concepts are expired art (Harpole, Cooligy, Walpole), and the design avoids the single-slot Split-Flow claims, so FTO at concept level is good. The planned claims look weak. A heat-map-programmed orifice comb is anticipated by Cooligy hot-spot art, Corintis and PKU's 2025 jet-enhanced manifold work, and it edges toward JetCool. A tied plate-fin sandwich is old brazed-HX art. The baseline is itself an etched, diffusion-bonded laminate, so the live Mikros/Jabil families must be cleared now, not 'only if a full-laminate SKU proceeds'.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: M15-18 to a qualified product assumes the one-shot bond works out of the box and that 2-3 furnaces are installed in 9-12 months. Redeveloping the joint (fin-safe braze/TLP plus a welded cover), proving tie-bond burst margin, and buying 4-8 hot presses push this to about M20-26. The plan depends on a single novel process for every SKU.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The product family is broad and coherent: GPU, bare-die, micro-channel lid core, CPU/NVSwitch, wafer-scale, de-rated 800 VDC power shelves, and optics/RF in DI water or PAO. The proposal correctly admits that SiC traction and EV are an aluminium/licensing play, not this copper plate. The power-electronics SKU is de-rated (0.2 mm gaps) and cost-led, so the elite core adds little there.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: The honesty is real: a same-paste row, a 'where it does not win' list, the reconstruction caveat on dP, and +/-25 % stated. But the structural and process claims are asserted, not derived. The 24x stiffness and 15 MPa tie stress come from a different geometry (1 mm fins, 85 % web bond). The proposal relies on C-scan of the tip bond and on an ENi option before bonding, and its stack-up height and block thickness do not add up. The 350 W/cm2 case is labelled a real 2027-28 package.

fatal_flaws: The joining process of record cannot work as specified. It is a one-shot vacuum diffusion bond of all six layers at 850-950 C, 5-10 MPa, for 1-4 h, applied to a skived field of 0.10 mm fins, 0.15 mm gaps and 2.0 mm height (40 % solid). The fin columns would carry p_b/0.40 = 12-25 MPa at about 0.86 Tm, where annealed OFE Cu has a hot yield of roughly 10-15 MPa and creeps fast. The fins would upset, lean and close the 0.15 mm gaps. Lowering the pressure to protect the fins leaves the +/-20-50 um skive tip-height scatter unbonded. Published diffusion-bonding practice for microchannel heat exchangers and reactors shows exactly this trade-off: channel collapse at high p/T, unbonded leaking regions at low p/T, and deformation of unsupported regions (USPTO 7,900,811; 3D InCites Aug 2026 joining-process article).

The stack gives the press no load path to most fin tips. The 1.5 mm plenum is 3.3/4.0 = 82 % open, so uniaxial press load reaches the grate and fin tips only under the 0.7 mm plenum walls. Fin tips under the open slots get no contact pressure and will not diffusion-bond. Under the walls, tip contact stress is about p_b/(0.175 x 0.4 x 0.5), roughly 28x nominal, which crushes them. The 2.5 mm cover over 5.5 mm post spans and over the 10 x 15 / 10 x 22.5 mm perimeter loops also sags at 900 C. The claimed >=50 % fin-tip bond fraction cannot be reached by this process, and the 1.0 mm base and the >=3 MPa burst rating both depend on it.

The tie-stress calculation, and with it the burst margin, is wrong. Even where tips are bonded, those under the open plenum cannot carry tie load: the grate sees fluid at p on both faces and has no solid path upward. The base load can only reach the cover through the 0.7 mm plenum walls at 4 mm pitch. That gives an effective tie fraction of <=17.5 %, or 8.75 % if the grate is 50 % open under the walls. Tie stress at the 3 MPa design burst is then 43-86 MPa, not 15 MPa. This is at or above annealed yield (70 MPa), and with Kt 2.5 it approaches UTS at the 4.5 MPa first-article burst target.

The critical-to-quality feature cannot be inspected in production. C-scan cannot image a fin-tip/grate interface 3 mm deep through a forest of 0.1 mm fins, nor through a 14 mm block full of voids. CT cannot see kissing (touching but unbonded) interfaces. 100 % He leak testing does not detect internal inlet-to-outlet bypass from unbonded plenum walls. The structural integrity of a 10-year pressure vessel would rest on proof testing and destructive lot sampling alone.

There is no route to a nickel-plated wetted path. The 'ENi applied to layers before bonding' option is metallurgically impossible: electroless Ni-P is essentially BNi-6 braze (eutectic ~875-880 C), so it liquates at the 850-950 C bond temperature and wicks into 0.15 mm gaps. Pure electrolytic Ni interdiffuses with Cu and blocks Cu-Cu bonding. If NVIDIA, Group-A or hyperscaler wetted-material practice requires Ni-plated copper (the research calls it de facto practice), the architecture has no way to supply it.

The '10-year drop-in' claim rests on a per-plate field-service item. The integrated threaded-plug 50 um screen becomes the loop's finest filter. Physics shows a 5 cm2 50 um cartridge reaches 50 % blockage in about 13 days at 1e-4 particles/mL above its rating, so service life is set by loop cleanliness the vendor does not control. Its '+2 kPa dP signature' is not observable against a 30-100 kPa branch with 72-150 plates per rack unless every plate has a sensor, which the proposal's own IP section steers away from. A sealed threaded port in annealed copper is also an elastomer-sealed leak path, contradicting the 'no polymer' claim.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Orifice-comb metering: make every branch inertial (comb ~2.2 of 2.4 kPa) so slot-to-slot uniformity does not change with flow, and zone the flow by hole count (die about 92 %, HBM about 6 %). One etched artwork per package is cheap and fast to re-spin. Put the comb at the slot top, at least 4-8 hole diameters away from the fins, as the physics rule says.

Centre-fed, centre-collected 'bow-tie' troughs fed from both ends, with in-plane perimeter loops for horizontal ports. This is a real height-reduction device versus the ~30 mm stacked-header design H, provided the slot-depth and trough arithmetic is fixed.

A tied sandwich achieved by a fin-safe process. Braze or Ag/Sn TLP-bond the fin tips to a grate that is solid under the plenum walls, at low fixture pressure (<0.5 MPa) and <=800 C. Then braze the plenum, comb and block, and laser- or EB-weld the cover. This keeps the 1.0 mm base, zero pressure bow and uniform bond line, and removes the hot-press bottleneck.

Hierarchical passage widths (each stage >2x the next), 0.6 mm slot-end bleeds into the outlet, and port-adjacent channels and slot ends kept outside the die footprint. A 50 um absolute last-chance screen at the tray inlet or UQD (one serviceable element per tray) rather than in each plate.

Interface tiering as a product structure: PCM pad for drop-in, liquid metal on 3-5 um electrolytic Ni on the contact face only (no Au), and direct-to-die stepped pedestal as Tier 3. Plus a hard rule of no grease on lids of 100 mm or more.
A stepped HBM pedestal machined after joining, combined with zoned feeding, with HBM never downstream of a die.

A disclosure package as a competitive weapon: an OCP v1.0.0-format report, dP at 6 or more points at three boundaries (port-to-port, with stubs, with a named UQD pair), an independent-lab repeat, and the coupling class stated with every dP number.
Serialised 100 % flow/dP signature test at the factory (6.0 +/- 0.6 kPa at 18 LPM, 45 C) as an outgoing quality control check.

The risk-retirement experiment set: water-table test of one slot pair for theta_c, bonded coupons for burst and tie bond, a dosed fouling rig behind 50/33/25 um screens, and TTV-A parity plus TTV-B zoned tests.
The honesty format: a same-paste like-for-like row, an explicit 'where it does not win' list, and a 'claims to avoid externally' list.
numbers_disputed: Tie stress at 3 MPa burst, claimed '15 MPa (SF 4.7 on yield)'. Corrected: about 43 MPa if the grate is solid under the 0.7 mm plenum walls (17.5 % effective tie), or about 86 MPa with a 50 %-open grate under the walls (8.75 %). Both are at or near annealed yield at the design burst. Basis: 3 x 0.25 / (0.1 x f_eff). Tips under the open plenum cannot transmit tension because the grate there has p on both faces.

Plate height, claimed 21.1 mm. Corrected: about 23 mm. Basis: 21.1 = 3.0 + 0.5 + 1.5 + 0.4 + (6.5 + 0.7 + 6.0) + 2.5 uses the 6.5 mm inlet slot depth, but the outlet slots are 8.4 mm deep (+1.9 mm). The listed 11.5 mm block cannot hold 6.5-8.4 mm pockets plus a 0.7 mm floor plus a 6 mm trough (13.2-15.1 mm). It only works if the outlet slots are made shallower.

Factory cost at 100k/yr, claimed US$190 (15 kW class) / US$135 (Rubin class). Corrected: about US$240-290 / US$160-190. Basis: LME copper is US$14.4-14.7k/t (Cochilco 1 Sep 2026; Westmetall 8 Sep 2026). Adding an OFE premium on ~3.5-4 kg buy weight gives ~US$45-50 net, not US$24. Yield/overhead should be 18-25 % rather than 12 % for a non-reworkable bonded stack at ramp. The staged braze-plus-weld route adds a step. The research canonical estimate puts a full etched + diffusion-bonded core at +US$40-80 over a US$100 plate.

Diffusion-bond capacity, claimed '2-3 furnaces, US$3-6 M per 100k/yr, 9-12 months'. Corrected: about 4-8 vacuum hot presses, US$10-25 M, 12-18 months. Basis: at 5-10 MPa a 148 x 152 mm plate needs 110-225 kN. A 200-plate batch means 20-high stacked columns holding ~500 kg of copper with height tolerances to equalise. Realistic loads are 30-80 plates per 16-24 h cycle, not 50-200 per 8-12 h.

'Velocities <=1.5 m/s at 150 % rated flow, no orifice >1.8 m/s'. Corrected: 16 mm ports run 2.24 m/s at 27 LPM (1.49 m/s at 18 LPM). At the advertised 36 LPM point, ports run 2.98 m/s and comb jets 2.4 m/s, hitting annealed fin tips about 4 hole diameters downstream, inside the laminar jet core (Re ~420).

'Real 2027-28 package, 4 dies of 26 x 33 mm at 350 W/cm2 (12.85 kW)'. Corrected: per the Rubin envelope gap report, Rubin Ultra is about 3.6 kW, roughly 87 W/cm2 die average, with 300-350 W/cm2 only as local hot spots. The 93 C (robust core, liquid metal) and 84 C (P core) results should be labelled a 2029+ stress case.

'Stack 24x stiffer, mount + thermal bow 4-25 + 6 um over 50 mm'. Corrected: unverified for this geometry. These figures were computed for 1.0 mm fins with 85 % web-bonded tips and a 1.75 mm manifold. With 2.0 mm fins, core shear stiffness across the fins falls about 4x (G_c proportional to 1/H^2), and the effective tie is <=17.5 %. The bow is probably still within 25-50 um thanks to the 14 mm block, but it must be recomputed.

C-scan acceptance, claimed 'tip-bond fraction >=50 %, reject <30 %'. Corrected: not measurable non-destructively in the finished part. Only proof testing plus before/after flatness change plus destructive sectioning per lot are realistic.

Screen service life, claimed '0.6-1.2x a skived plate, 10-year drop-in'. Corrected: the service interval is set by the particle load passing the CDU filter. A 12 cm2 50 um screen reaches about 50 % blockage in roughly 30 days at 1e-4 particles/mL above its rating (scaled from the physics 5 cm2 / 13-day result). This is a maintenance item, not maintenance-free.
Time to qualified product, claimed M15-18. Corrected: about M20-26, allowing for joining-process redevelopment, tie-bond burst proof and hot-press capex lead time.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The 28.0/31.1 K (PCM) and 30.0/35.0 K (same paste) figures come from a 1-D plug-flow model that assumes every parcel runs the full 4 mm through the full 2.0 mm fin. The drawn geometry (3.3 mm slot openings, a 0.7 mm wall between them, land/H = 0.35) does not do that. My 2-D Hele-Shaw conjugate cell model adds +4 K (lower bound, fluid forced well-mixed) to +12.6 K (Darcy) to caloric+conv+base, so like-for-like the plate is at best at parity with CoolIT on average and PCM lands at ~32-41 K; the max win over 44.2 K probably survives.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: By its own numbers the robust core misses 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with liquid metal (93 C), and the same in-gap bypass (+18 K Darcy upper bound in the 4.3 mm-slot die zone) pushes that to ~100-110 C. At 38-45 W/cm2 GPU flux the isothermal-cell caloric penalty makes the average dT worse than split-flow (conceded). Only direct-to-die, or the P core behind 33 um filtration, approaches the target.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: A low plate dP (~6-7 kPa, 86 % inertial and port-dominated) is physically robust, and the proposal correctly states that couplings dominate the loop. Several things are unproven: the Q/2 both-end trough feed (the perimeter-loop path has ~3x the loss coefficient of the direct path, so the split is ~62/38), a branch-to-header-head ratio only 6.5 nominal (~4 with an unequal split or a Cd 0.75 comb), a comb moved to the slot bottom against the physics rule (1.2 m/s jets hit fin tips after only ~4 d), and flow distribution inside the fin gaps. UQD12 is not a confirmed OCP size.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Tiling the trough manifold while holding a 4 mm flow length is a sound scaling idea, and dP at 36 LPM (17.6-23.6 kPa) stays reasonable. Q capacity (21.6 kW PCM, 29.7 kW LM at 1.2 LPM/kW) falls to roughly 17-24 kW once the in-gap penalty is applied. Ports exceed the proposal's own 1.5 m/s rule above ~18 LPM unless 20 mm, and skiving width caps the field at 100-250 mm.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: The one-shot vacuum diffusion bond at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa puts 25-50 MPa on the fins, because only ~20 % of the field area carries load (0.4 solid x 0.5 bonded). That is above copper's hot flow stress, so 0.1 x 2.0 mm skived fins will creep or crush, or else the tips do not bond. In practice the tied sandwich needs the braze fallback, with Ag filler wicking risk in 0.15 mm gaps. The US$190 (100k) cost is plausible only on that route; the 6-layer stack also needs <10 um per-layer flatness, and a 50-200-plate furnace batch is optimistic.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Strong deployability thinking: a 0.15 mm floor behind an integrated 50 um absolute screen with a dP signature, bleed orifices, an all-Cu wetted path and a thorough OCP-format qualification plan. But the burst safety factor is overstated: only the grate bars under the 0.7 mm plenum walls (~12.5 % of fin-tip length) are in the load path, so tie stress at the 3 MPa design burst is ~60 MPa, not 15. Near-base dead zones in the gaps are settling sites. Horizontal 3/4-in ports do not fit inside a 21 mm body, and 2.3 kg is heavy.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The avoid list is sensible and leans on expired Harpole/Cooligy art. However, the project's own FTO gap report says multiple slots are not a safe design-around of an open-ended Split-Flow claim; it recommends segmented fins and no field-end collection, which this design does not adopt, and puts expiry at Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031, not ~Aug 2028. Claimed novelties such as power-map comb density sit close to expired Cooligy US 7,104,312 and to Corintis, so defensibility is weak.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: Conventional processes and a sensible experiment order (the water-table test first) help. The in-gap flow problem forces a manifold/grate redesign plus CFD before any credible claim, and the bonding route will likely change, so qualification at M15-18 is optimistic and could slip past the Rubin Ultra window.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family is well reasoned: GPU, bare-die, micro-channel lid, CPU/switch, wafer-scale and optics, with a de-rated power-electronics variant. For cost-led 5-30 W/cm2 power electronics a multi-layer bonded HMMC is overkill, and traction is rightly framed as a licensing play rather than a product.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: Unusually candid about where it loses: same-paste margin, GPU-class average, 350 W/cm2 miss, and a dP win measured only against a reconstruction. Yet the core claim rests on a model the physics team itself said needs CFD at land/H = 1.7, while this geometry is at 0.35, and the text asserts 'every parcel wets 4 mm of fin at inlet temperature'. There are arithmetic slips: block 11.5 vs 13.2 mm, 11.4 vs ~35 holes per cm of slot, and the tie stress.

fatal_flaws: Fin-level flow geometry breaks the thermal basis. Inlet and outlet openings are 3.3 mm wide (4.3 mm in the die zone), separated by only a 0.7 mm wall, over 2.0 mm deep, 0.15 mm gaps (land/H = 0.35); flow in a 0.15 mm gap is Hele-Shaw-like. My 2-D Darcy plus two-equation conjugate cell model (appendix/judge_hmmc/heleshaw.py) reproduces the 1-D answer within 0.4 K when the fluid is forced well-mixed with narrow openings. For the drawn geometry it finds ~70 % of the flow short-circuiting through the upper half of the fin under the wall, and caloric+conv+base rising from 21.0 K (1-D) to 33.6 K at 128 W/cm2 (+4.0 K even with perfect z-mixing). Inertia (reduced Re ~1) can only partly offset this. As drawn, the same-paste case is at best parity with CoolIT (34-42 vs 34.4 K), PCM is ~32-41 K rather than 28, and the 350 W/cm2 die zone is +18 K worse (Darcy). The physics team flagged this as unresolved, needing CFD, at land/H = 1.7; the proposal is at 0.35 and never addresses it.

The tied sandwich cannot be made as specified. One-shot diffusion bonding at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa loads the 0.1 mm skived fins at 25-50 MPa (only 0.4 solid x 0.5 bonded of the area carries load), above copper's hot flow stress, so fins creep or crush, or the tips stay unbonded. Everything resting on the fin-tip ties (1.0 mm base, zero pressure bow, uniform bond line for PCM/LM, burst margin, 'no braze, no dissimilar metal') then depends on the braze fallback, with Ag filler in the wetted path and capillary wicking into 0.15 mm gaps.

The mission claim 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' is indefensible even on the proposal's own numbers. It loses on average dT at GPU-class flux (18.4 vs 16.1 K at 2.3 kW), misses 85 C at 350 W/cm2 with the deployable core (93 C), only matches the 4 kW plate with PCM, and is heavier (2.3 kg) and about as tall. With the in-gap penalty, even the 15 kW like-for-like average win disappears.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: An orifice comb that makes every branch inertial, so the branch-to-header-head ratio and uniformity are flow-independent, with zoning by hole-density artwork alone (one plate family, any power map). Put the comb at the slot top, or have the jets impinge on solid land, so jets decay before reaching the fins.

Fix the bypass by redrawing the grate and plenum as a single land layer with narrow (~0.8 mm) fin-level openings, >= 3 mm land and 1.5 mm fins. My cell model puts this at +2.6 K over 1-D (vs +12.6 K as drawn), giving PCM ~31.5 K average. It also raises the bonded tip fraction in the load path from ~12 % to ~80 %, and descent velocity stays at ~0.43 m/s, under the 0.5 m/s cap.

An integrated 50 um absolute last-chance screen, with plate dP as its clogging signature, slot-end bleed orifices, and the rule that the channel gap is >= 3x the absolute rating of the last filter (0.15 mm drop-in floor, 0.10 mm only behind <= 33 um loops).
A tiered interface strategy on one core: PCM pad for drop-in, liquid metal on Ni-faced lids for OEMs, stepped pedestal for direct-to-die; never grease on 100+ mm lids.
A stepped HBM pedestal machined after bonding, with HBM never downstream of a die, and the across-die case gradient specified as a product metric.
In-plane both-end-fed header troughs with horizontal ports to cut height, provided the perimeter-loop and direct paths are hydraulically balanced (restrictor or symmetric H-routing).
A disclosure strategy that turns CoolIT's opacity into a weapon: OCP v1.0 format, a 6-point dP curve with a named coupling boundary, three TIMs with D5470, and an independent lab repeat.
numbers_disputed: Average case-to-inlet dT, Tier 1 PCM, 28.0 K: as drawn ~32-41 K (1-D 21.0 K caloric+conv+base becomes 25.0 K with z-mixing / 33.6 K Darcy, plus 7.1 K TIM). About 31.5 K if the fin-level openings are narrowed to 0.8 mm with 3.2 mm land and 1.5 mm fins (24.4 + 7.1 K). Basis: 2-D Hele-Shaw conjugate cell model, appendix/judge_hmmc/heleshaw.py.
Same-paste like-for-like average, 30.0 K: ~34-42.6 K as drawn and ~33.4 K with the opening fix, i.e. parity with CoolIT's 34.4 K, not -13 %.

Max dT with PCM, 31.1 K: ~37-44 K as drawn, ~35 K with the fix. The extra comes from the case sawtooth (2.3 K pk-pk at 128 W/cm2 in the cell model, not < 0.5 K) and a trough-split asymmetry (+0.5-1 K).
Sawtooth at the case < 0.5 K: 2.3 K pk-pk at 128 W/cm2 and 7.4 K pk-pk at 350 W/cm2 for the drawn 3.3/0.7 mm (4.3/0.7 mm) openings. The < 0.5 K value assumed 1-D plug flow along the full cell.

Real package, robust core with liquid metal, 93 C: ~102-111 C as drawn (die-zone cell penalty +17.9 K Darcy, +6.6 K with z-mixing) and ~96-99 C with the fix. The P core's 84 C becomes ~90 C. The 85 C target is met only by direct-to-die.
Q capacity at Tcase,max <= 85 C, 21.6 kW (PCM) / 29.7 kW (LM): ~17-18 kW / ~24 kW once the corrected convective penalty is scaled with flux.

Tie stress at the 3 MPa design burst, 15 MPa (SF 4.7 on yield): ~60 MPa, SF ~1 on annealed OFE yield. The grate bars run in y, parallel to the plenum walls, so only the bar under each 0.7 mm wall (0.5 of every 4 mm, ~12.5 % of fin-tip length) is in the load path: 3 MPa x 0.25 x 4 mm^2 / (0.1 x 0.5 mm^2). Burst is probably still UTS-limited (SF ~3.7).

Troughs+loops+tees 0.61 kPa: ~1.2-2 kPa. The perimeter-loop path has K ~4-5 (tee branch, two machined corners, trough entry) against ~1.4 for the direct path, so the split is ~62/38, not Q/2. The near-end trough head rises to ~600 Pa and the branch-to-head ratio falls from 6.5 to ~4 (global max/min ~1.15-1.2, flow hot spot ~2-2.5 K rather than 1.5 K). Total plate dP ~7 kPa, still inside the <= 8 kPa claim.

Comb dP 2.2 kPa: it assumes K = 3.0 (Cd 0.58). For 0.4 mm thick etched plate with 0.5 mm holes (t/d = 0.8), Cd is ~0.7-0.8, giving 1.3-1.6 kPa, which erodes the uniformity margin further. The hole Re of ~450 means the comb is not purely inertial either.

Die-zone comb density, 11.4 holes per cm of slot in 3 rows: the script multiplies holes/cm2 by 0.33 cm instead of the 1.0 cm inlet pitch. 1182 holes over 34.3 cm2 at 10 mm pitch needs ~35 holes per cm, i.e. >= 4 rows at ~1.1 mm pitch.

Manifold block 11.5 mm: the stack sum needs 13.2 mm (6.5 pocket + 0.7 floor + 6.0 trough) to reach the stated 21.1 mm. The 8.4 mm outlet pockets cannot pass under the 6 mm inlet trough, so they are limited to ~6.5 mm there.

Diffusion-bond feasibility, 5-10 MPa at 850-950 C: fin contact stress is 25-50 MPa, above copper's hot flow stress (~10-30 MPa at low strain rates), so the fins creep. Bonding the tips needs a braze or low-temperature bonding process.

Split-Flow patent expiry ~Aug 2028: the project's FTO gap report bounds it at Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031, and finds multi-slot layouts are not a safe design-around. The planned M15-18 launch (early-mid 2028) falls inside the risk window.

UQD12-class (3/4 in) coupling at ~5 kPa per pair: not confirmed to exist in OCP UQD v2.0.0 (gap-hydraulic report). Horizontal 3/4-in fittings (G3/4 major diameter 26.4 mm) do not fit inside a 21 mm-tall body without bosses.

hmmc-elite.lens: strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The model gives a real win on max dT and uniformity: max-avg drops from about 10 K to about 3 K. Like-for-like with the same TIM, though, the mean gain is only -4.5 K (30.0 vs 34.4 K), and the proposal's own Monte Carlo P90 for that case is 37 K, which is worse than CoolIT. The 28 K headline compares our PCM against CoolIT's paste; an OEM testing to the OCP spec with one recommended TIM will reject that comparison.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: Zoning by comb artwork is a strong, cheap lever: the modelled hot die is about 26 K cooler than a split-flow plate. But the deployable R core misses 85 C even with liquid metal (93 C), and only the filtration-gated P core or direct-to-die gets there. The GPU-class runs use 38-45 W/cm2 spread uniformly over the lid, against the programme's own 90-120 W/cm2 die-average figures. That is why they concede a worse mean dT, and with Tier-1 PCM the design only matches CoolIT's 4 kW plate.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 6 kPa port-to-port with an inertial comb gives uniformity that does not depend on flow. The dP claims honestly name the coupling class, and the plate works with negative-pressure loops. The win is measured against a reconstructed benchmark (CoolIT publishes no dP), and UQD12-class couplings are not one of the OCP UQD v2.0 sizes (02-08), so the 15 kW SKU is not truly drop-in at the tray.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length stays at 4 mm while the tiled header manifold scales. Modelled Q capacity is 21.6 kW with PCM and 29.7 kW with liquid metal, and there is a credible wafer-scale tiling path. At 30 kW+ the ports must grow to 20-30 mm to hold 1.5 m/s, and demand for a 30 kW single plate is speculative given the OCP white paper's ~4 kW single-phase boundary figure.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: A 6-layer one-shot copper diffusion bond is outside the Group-A process base (skive plus FSW, laser or braze), so the Nvidia volume channel would have to adopt a new process. At the stated 2-3 furnaces per 100k/yr, Nvidia-relevant scale (100k plates a month) needs about 25-35 furnaces. Bond pressure on 0.10 x 2 mm fins through about 20 % tip contact at 850-950 C risks crushing them, the braze fallback 'stop-off on the fin tips' gives up the tie, and the US$190/135 cost and 2.3/1.1 kg mass are optimistic or uncompetitive.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The fouling engineering is careful: a 0.15 mm floor behind an integrated 50 um screen, a dP signature, bleed orifices, an all-copper wetted path, leak-before-break and a full OCP-format test matrix. Against that, the per-plate serviceable screen plug adds a joint and a server-level service task operators dislike, laminar 0.08 m/s channels have no self-cleaning, Tier 2 and 3 are not drop-in, and UQD12-class tray couplings are not standard.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The FTO section repeats the superseded 'avoid a single central slot' design-around, yet continuous skived fins with interior inlet slots splitting flow both ways may meet an open-ended split-flow claim. It also omits US 12,101,906, gives the expiry as ~Aug 2028 when the window runs to mid-2031, and under-weights Mikros/Jabil even though this design is a diffusion-bonded laminate with normal-flow feed. The claims it proposes are narrow numeric or implementation claims built on expired Harpole, Cooligy and Valenzuela art, and JetCool-family disclosures of hot-spot-matched nozzle density already pre-empt claim (1).

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: Qualified product at M15-18 means early to mid 2028, which misses Rubin Ultra (2H 2027, design freeze already past), so the 'RU micro-channel-lid bid' at M10-14 is not realistic and Feynman-era revenue lands around 2029. The five de-risking experiments are well chosen and cheap, but launch falls inside the live Split-Flow window, and furnace capacity plus single-process dependence add 9-12 months.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family is broad: GPU, CPU/switch, direct-to-die, lid core, wafer-scale, optics and an 800 VDC derivative, with one etched artwork per package. The power-electronics leg is thin, though: 5-30 W/cm2 shelves do not need HMMC, a diffusion-bonded copper plate is over-specified for cost-led PE, and the proposal itself admits SiC traction is only a licensing play on aluminium loops.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: Unusually candid: it has a 'where it does not win' section, P10-P90 ranges and a claims-to-avoid list. Against that, the conservative same-paste claim (<=34/40 K) contradicts its own P90 (37/42 K), and the GPU cases use the wrong flux. It also says the interface gain is architecture-specific even though the physics synthesis says CoolIT's plate must also be tied, its IP text ignores the gap report, and the CoolIT mass and height figures (1.5 kg, 25 mm) have no basis; photogrammetry gives a 24-25 mm bar width, not height.

fatal_flaws: The 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' claim fails on the proposal's own numbers, so it cannot be defended. Mass is worse (2.3 kg vs a ~1.5 kg estimate) and cost is higher than a skived plate. GPU-class average dT is worse per its own model, and Tier-1 PCM does not clearly beat CoolIT's 4 kW plate (0.215 vs <=0.225 cm2K/W). With the same paste, the mean dT P90 is 37 K, above CoolIT's measured 34.4 K. Under the OCP Cold Plate Test Spec (one recommended TIM for both plates), the architecture-attributable win is -4.5 K mean / ~-9 K max, not the 28 K-vs-34.4 K headline.

The FTO posture rests on a design-around that the programme's own gap report already marked as unsafe. HMMC-E uses continuous 108 mm skived fins, and every interior inlet slot splits flow in opposing directions. Under 'comprising/an = one or more', adding slots does not avoid an open-ended split-flow claim. CoolIT actively asserts this family: it sued Asetek on US 8,746,330 in D. Del. 1:14-cv-00725, and three Split-Flow patents were headed to a 2023 trial. The family's expiry window (Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031 with PTA) overlaps the planned M15-18 launch, and US 12,101,906 is not even listed. The cheap fix is to segment the fins at each outlet slot and keep all outlets interior, documented against Cooligy US 6,986,382 and Harpole US 5,088,005, then run a claim chart before US sales. Without that fix, US sales before roughly 2029-31 are exposed.

The joining route undermines both the volume channel and the 1.0 mm base claim. Group-A houses, who hold more than 80 % of Nvidia plates and buy centrally at ~US$400, do not run multi-layer copper diffusion-bond lines. Nvidia scale (100k plates a month) implies about 25-35 furnaces at the proposal's own rate. In the one-shot bond, the 0.10 x 2.0 mm fins carry the 5-10 MPa stack load through about 20 % tip contact (40 % fin fraction x 50 % grate), roughly 25-50 MPa locally at 850-950 C, which is above hot copper's flow stress, so creep or buckling is likely. The stated fallback (braze 'with stop-off on the fin tips') gives up the tie. The plate would then need a thicker base, losing about 3 K of the margin, and the burst case would have to be redone.

There is no durable moat. Every core concept (manifold microchannel, interwoven slots, hot-spot-weighted feed, normal-flow laminates) is expired art. The six proposed claims are narrow numeric or implementation claims (>=50 % tip bond, <=1.0 mm base, <=21 mm height, bow-tie troughs) that any Group-A house can design around once Split-Flow expires. JetCool-family patents US 11,191,184 and US 11,277,937 already disclose nozzle density matched to hot spots (assignee to verify), which pre-empts claim (1). They also put the comb, which sits beside interleaved return openings in the same plate, into JetCool claim-review territory, which the proposal never flags.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Orifice-comb metering at each slot top: it makes every branch inertial, so flow uniformity does not depend on flow, and it zones the package (die block 92 % / HBM 6 % / margin 2 %) by phototool artwork alone. The result is package-specific SKUs at about US$0.5-3k tooling and a 2-week lead time, a real commercial lever against Group-A lead times.

Transparency play inside CoolIT's own spec: a full OCP v1.0.0 report with the 6-point dP curve at three named boundaries (port-to-port, with stubs, with a named UQD pair), three plates x three assemblies, ASTM D5470 at clamp pressure, and an independent national-lab repeat. CoolIT discloses one flow point and no dP.

A fouling-gated SKU split: an R core with 0.15 mm gaps behind an integrated 50 um absolute screen for the 10-year drop-in product, and a P core with 0.10 mm gaps only for loops filtered to <=33 um. The plate dP doubles as a screen-health signature, and slot-end bleed orifices are added. This turns the loop-cleanliness risk into a spec line.

Tied sandwich (fin tips bonded to the manifold web): zero pressure bow, a stiffer stack, and burst governed by the perimeter land, which is what allows a thin base and a uniform bond line. Graft it with a laser/FSW or braze route that keeps the tie.

Tiered interface strategy with explicit rules: PCM for drop-in, liquid metal on a 3-5 um Ni face for OEM co-design, a stepped pedestal for direct-to-die, and 'never grease on 100+ mm lids'. Pair it with the zoning rule 'HBM never downstream of a die' and a machined stepped HBM pedestal.

In-plane, both-end-fed header troughs with perimeter loops: they cut the manifold stack from ~30 mm to 21 mm (18 mm and 15.6 mm variants) with horizontal ports, while keeping branch dP >= 6x header head.

Coupling class named inside every dP claim, plus a scorecard split into conservative/nominal/stretch with a 'claims to avoid externally' list. This is good claim-defensibility hygiene for OEM and hyperscaler reviews.
numbers_disputed: Conservative same-paste like-for-like '<= 34 / 40 K' (Section 11): the proposal's own Monte Carlo row 'HMMC-E/R same paste 30.0 (26-37) / 35.0 (31-42)' puts the P90 at 37 K avg / 42 K max. The conservative like-for-like mean is therefore about parity with CoolIT's 34.4 K, not a win.

Split-Flow expiry '~Aug 2028': the correct window is 11 Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031. '330 pendency was 2,129 days, so up to 1,034 days of B-delay PTA is possible, and the continuations '284/'513 are tied by terminal disclaimer (gap-splitflow-continuation-claims-fto.md). Likewise 'plus CA/CN/TW/EP counterparts' should read 'probably none for the 2008 family' (KB-L): the exposure is US importation, not Asian manufacture.

GPU-class cases 'Rubin 2.3 kW, 60 cm2' (38 W/cm2) and 'Rubin Ultra 3.6 kW, 80 cm2' (45 W/cm2): the programme's chip-roadmap research gives die-average ~115-120 W/cm2 for Rubin (2 dies, ~16.5 cm2) and ~90-100 W/cm2 for Rubin Ultra (~33 cm2). The concession that the HMMC average is '1-2 K worse at GPU class' is an artefact of a flux 2-3x too low. Re-run with a die map under the lid; the HMMC probably wins on the mean there too.

Interface gain attributed to the architecture ('legitimately part of the architecture'): SYNTHESIS-physics section 3.5 states that CoolIT's real plate must already have tied fins or posts to pass 1.5 MPa, so PCM's -1.9 K TIM gain and ~-2 K lower scatter are available to CoolIT too. CoolIT with PCM ≈ 32.5 K avg / ~40 K max, so the defensible Tier-1 margin is -4.5 K mean (-14 %) and -9 K max (-23 %), not -6.4 / -13.1 K.

Tier-1 unit resistance 0.219 cm2K/W case-to-inlet presented as 'elite': converted to case-to-mean-fluid ((28.0-6.3)/128) it is ≈0.17 cm2K/W, inside the conventional-skived band of 0.14-0.22 (gap-competitor-plate-datasheets). Only liquid metal (≈0.13) or P core plus LM (≈0.11) leaves that band, and none reaches the ≤0.09 that would clearly beat incumbents.

Factory cost US$190 (15 kW-class) / US$135 (Rubin-class) at 100k/yr: the US$34 CNC block assumes about 3 m of 3.3 mm slot in ~5 min, i.e. 10 m/min in OFE copper at 2xD depth, which is unrealistic. manufacturing-cost.md prices a full diffusion-bonded laminate at +US$40-80 over a ~US$105 skived plate. A better estimate is US$145-185 (Rubin-class) and US$230-300 (15 kW-class) at 100k, until an RFQ confirms.

Bond capacity '2-3 furnaces per 100k/yr (US$3-6 M)': that is correct for 100k/yr, but the Nvidia-relevant scale (>=100k plates a month, market-business.md) implies about 25-35 furnaces and roughly US$40-70 M of capex. The proposal never confronts this.

'Rubin-Ultra micro-channel-lid proposal' at M10-14 (Aug-Dec 2027): platform design freeze comes ~12 months before ramp (market-business.md 6.3), so Rubin Ultra (2H 2027) is already closed. The realistic first platform is Feynman (2028), with first volume revenue around 2029.

CoolIT plate 'height ~25 mm with bar / mass ~1.5 kg est.': nothing in the evidence supports this. The photogrammetry (gap-coolit-15kw-ttv-footprint) gives a 140-145 mm body and a 24-25 mm bar width, not height. Drop the comparison or measure it, because it is used to excuse HMMC-E's 21 mm / 2.3 kg.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The term budget matches SYNTHESIS-physics HMMC-R line for line: isothermal caloric 7.6 K at NTU 1.25, h_eff 127 kW/m2K (Nu about 7, so not an optimistic h), a deployable 0.15 mm gap and a 1 mm base. 28 K average is defensible. The 31.6 K maximum rests on an along-slot uniformity of +/-10-12 % that the project's own maldistribution map does not support (+/-20-30 % is the physics-consistent value). The PCM value of 0.055 also assumes a 1.6-2.4 kN clamp. Physics-consistent result is about 28.3/33 K with PCM and about 30.5/37 K with the same paste, which still clearly beats 34.4/44.2 K.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: By its own numbers the drop-in robust core misses T_case 85 C at 350 W/cm2: 107 C with PCM, 93 C with liquid metal. Reaching the line needs the 0.10 mm core behind 25 um loops, or direct-to-die. On uniform 1-3.6 kW TTVs at 1.2 LPM/kW the average is 0.4-2.4 K worse than the split-flow reconstruction, because the isothermal cell saturates at NTU 4-5. The Rubin-Ultra figures (71 C, and CoolIT '~85 C est.') are linear flux scalings with no model basis.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: Good: couplings are treated correctly (UQD08 pair about 25 kPa dominates; three dP boundaries reported), and the U-header ratio of 7.8 meets the >=6 rule. Bad: the along-slot ratio is 2.3-3.6 against the >=15 rule, and slots are fed off-centre from a single 1.2 x 12 mm slit whose 1.3 kPa jet sits only 10 mm above fin tips with a 0.27 kPa branch. The outlet-slit loss is omitted (true plate dP about 7.4-9 kPa, not 6.3). Along-slot uniformity gets worse at 2x flow (ratio about 1.8), contrary to the 'unchanged at 36 LPM' claim.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: The flow length stays 4 mm at any size, and the model gives 38.8/43.1 K at 30 kW on 150 cm2 versus 50/61.7 K for split-flow, at a third of the dP. However, 36 LPM needs 20 mm ports and dual QDs (a UQD08 pair is 78-139 kPa at 36 LPM). Along-slot maldistribution grows with flow, slots longer than 110 mm need extra header pairs, and straight through-slots allow only 1-D zoning.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: All processes are incumbent, but the comb as specified cannot be built. Gang-slitting closed-end 108 mm through-slots in a 10 mm plate gives 137-149 mm top-face openings (saw run-out) inside a 125 mm outline, which severs the frame and opens 27 external leak paths. The fix is end-milling 54 slot ends, a laminated comb, or blind slots cut from below, and it adds cost. The process also stacks risks: 1 x 10 mm OFE webs, 0.10 mm skived fins at aspect ratio 20, and Ag-eutectic bonding of 0.1 mm fin tips held to a +/-20 um plane. Factory cost is 38 % above the incumbent and probably understated by US$10-25.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The fouling strategy follows the physics rules exactly: 0.15 mm gap, 50 um absolute screen of 12 cm2 or more, 4 % dead-end bleed, dP taps. The OCP v1.0.0 qualification matrix is strong. Against that: only 25 % of each fin tip is tied (below the 30 % floor) and the stated tie SF of 5.6 is really about 1.4 on yield at 2 MPa. The plate is 33 mm tall and 1.8 kg, and the PCM clamp needs 1.6-2.4 kN while bow was checked at 300 N. The plate screen becomes the loop's filter and needs field service.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The plate has continuous skived channels, inlet slots between channel ends that split flow in two directions, and outlet slots at the channel ends. The FTO gap report names exactly these features as possibly reading on the Split-Flow continuation family (expiry Aug 2028 to about 2031), and it recommends segmented fins and no end outlets. The proposal still says it 'reads on nothing live'. Its own claims are narrow construction and process claims sitting on expired Harpole/Cooligy art.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The supply chain is conventional and the plan is credible: braze coupons and flow rig in months 1-3, TTV in months 3-5, PO in months 12-18, with the right experiments first. Open risks: fin-tip braze yield, a comb redesign, and a likely Rev B third laminate if the flow rig confirms the along-slot problem. Nvidia's centralised Group-A purchasing limits the near-term sockets.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family is coherent and covers GPU, CPU, switch/CPO, 800 VDC power shelves in the same PG25 loop, an aluminium EV variant and laser diodes. At low-flux uniform power-module loads, the isothermal-cell averaging penalty and the 33 mm height erode the advantage. The aluminium EV line is effectively a separate product.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: The proposal is unusually candid: it lists where it loses, gives P90 and like-for-like paste rows, and a claims-to-avoid list. It also contains several errors and contradictions: slots called 'centre-fed' when they cannot be, +/-10-12 % at ratio 3.5 against the report map of 1.46 max/min, a tie-stress figure with the bonded fraction applied twice, a missing outlet-slit loss, base ripple estimated with 3 mm solid Cu, bow checked at 300 N against a 2 kN clamp, an impossible gang-slit geometry, and an IP statement more confident than the FTO report.

fatal_flaws: The comb cannot be built as written. Gang-slitting 27 closed-end, 108 mm long through-slots in a 10 mm plate within a 125 mm outline is geometrically impossible: for any arbor-mountable saw (D 45-80 mm, 10.5 mm plunge) a 108 mm opening at the fin face needs a 137-149 mm opening at the top face. The slots would breach the comb end faces, severing the frame and the mounting ears and leaving 27 external leak paths. The '2-3 min, US$13 gang-slit comb, any machine shop' route and the US$145 cost are therefore not defensible. It needs end-milled slot ends (54 plunges), a stacked stamped-lamination comb, or blind slots cut from below with an integral slitted ceiling.

The mission requires beating CoolIT in every measurable aspect, and by the proposal's own admission it does not. It is worse on factory cost (US$145 vs about US$105, +38 %), height (33 vs 15-20 mm), mass (1.8 vs about 1.5 kg) and filler-free construction (Ag-Cu eutectic in the wetted path). It also loses the average dT on uniform 1-3.6 kW GPU TTVs at 1.2 LPM/kW (+0.4 to +2.4 K). The robust drop-in core also misses T_case <= 85 C at 350 W/cm2 (93 C even with liquid metal).

The nominal hot-spot claim breaks the project's own manifold rule, so it cannot be defended as nominal. The along-slot branch/dynamic-head ratio is 3.6 even if the slot were centre-fed, and 2.3-2.8 for the real off-centre single-slit feed, against the rule of >= 15. The manifold-maldistribution map gives max/min 1.46 at ratio 3.5, i.e. about +/-20 % or worse, not the +/-10-12 % carried in the 31.6 K figure. On top of that, the 1.6 m/s slit jet (about 0.9-1.3 kPa dynamic head) lands 10 mm above fin tips that have a 0.27 kPa laminar branch, which is not analysed at all.

The tied-sandwich premise behind the 1.0 mm base is weaker than stated. Only 25 % of each fin tip sits under a web, which is below the 30 % minimum in base-stress-stiffness. The true local fin-tip/bond stress at the 2.0 MPa design burst is 10p x Kt 2.5 = 50 MPa, an SF of about 1.4 against annealed 70 MPa yield, not 5.6. At the 4.5 MPa sample-burst target the tips yield, and any voiding in the 0.1 mm-wide Ag-eutectic tip bonds pushes the design below SF 1 on yield at design burst.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: A stamped (or laser-cut) selector floor with one metering slit per slot. Slit width programs the zone flow at near-zero tooling cost and makes the slot-to-slot branch inertial, so header uniformity holds as flow scales. Graft it with a distributed multi-hole orifice strip (the Rev B), not a single slit, so the jet decays before it reaches the fins.

A single vacuum-braze cycle with fin tips tied to manifold webs, then a post-braze fly-cut of the die face. A 2.8 mm blank skived to a 2.0 mm base is cut back to 1.0 mm; the cut absorbs braze distortion and sets <= 15-20 um flatness, so a 1 mm base becomes manufacturable with skiving.

Production test hooks: 100 % dP-vs-flow slope testing at three flows to catch inter-slot cross-leaks and blocked regions, dP tap ports on the header bar, and C-SAM plus burst sampling of the tie bonds.

A serviceable 50 um absolute pleated cartridge in the inlet boss, a dead-end bleed notch at every slot end, and an all-Cu wetted path. Together these turn the fouling report's rules into a concrete package for a 0.15 mm channel.

The reporting discipline: a like-for-like same-paste row, a P90 conservative row, flow-equivalence (0.72 LPM/kW for 34.4 K) and equal-pumping-power curves, three dP boundaries per OCP v1.0.0, and an explicit list of claims to avoid.
A HBM stepped pedestal machined into the die-side face at the same fly-cut operation.
The header sizing rule (branch dP >= 6x header dynamic head) applied explicitly and re-checked at 2x flow.
numbers_disputed: Maximum dT, Tier 1 nominal: 31.6 K claimed; physics-consistent value 32.6-33.5 K. Basis: along-slot ratio 2.3-3.6 (rule >= 15) maps to +/-20-30 % long-wave maldistribution, giving a 2.3-2.8 K flow term (hotspot-smoothing) plus about 0.9 K ripple plus 1.5 K PCM scatter. The average rises about 0.3-0.45 K, to 28.3-28.5 K.

Along-slot uniformity: +/-10-12 % claimed; +/-20-30 % expected. manifold-maldistribution gives CC max/min 1.46 at ratio 3.5. The real feed is 5-16 mm off-centre, because inlet and outlet headers sit side by side and each slit lies under its own header, which cuts the ratio to 2.3-2.8. The 'centre-fed' label in the L3 row is geometrically impossible.
Global max/min: about 1.07 claimed; about 1.5-1.8 expected (slot-to-slot about 1.07 times along-slot about 1.4-1.7).

Plate dP port-to-port at 18 LPM: 6.3 kPa claimed; at least 7.4 kPa, likely 8-9 kPa. The 14 outlet slits (1.2 x 12 mm at 1.49 m/s, 1.1 kPa dynamic head) add 1.7-2.2 kPa and are omitted; the 2.5 kPa metering figure covers only the inlet slits. At 36 LPM expect about 29-33 kPa, not 24.6.

'Uniformity unchanged at 36 LPM': true only slot-to-slot. The along-slot level has a laminar branch scaling with Q against a dynamic head scaling with Q^2, so the ratio falls from 3.6 to about 1.8 at 36 LPM.

Fin-tip tie safety factor: SF 5.6 vs yield at 2 MPa claimed; about 1.4 actual. Local stress is 10p x 2.5 = 50 MPa; the quoted 12.5 MPa applies the 25 % bonded fraction twice. At the 4.5 MPa sample-burst target the local stress is 112 MPa, above the 70 MPa annealed yield.

Base ripple at 8 mm period: about 0.7 K pk-pk claimed; about 1.9 K pk-pk (about 0.9 K max-avg). Basis: the Fourier attenuation used 3 mm of solid Cu, but the 2 mm fin layer is only 40 % Cu, so the effective thickness is about 1.8 mm.

PCM TIM term 7.1 K (0.055 cm2K/W at 20-30 psi): that pressure is 1.6-2.4 kN on 117 cm2 (1.4-2.1 kN on a 100 cm2 lid), versus the 300 N used in the bow check and 0.3-1 kN typical retention. At 4-12 psi and 40-50 um bond line, PTM7950-class pads are about 0.07-0.08 cm2K/W, i.e. 9-10 K. That gives a Tier 1 average of about 30-31 K, not 28.
Comb cost US$13 and 2-3 min at 100k/yr: add US$10-25 and 10+ min for end-milling 54 slot ends or for a laminated comb. Factory cost is then about US$155-170, not US$145.
Q capacity at T_case <= 85 C: 21.2 kW claimed; about 20.4 kW with the corrected hot-spot term (allowed 27.9 K over flux terms of 20.5 K at 15 kW).

Rubin-Ultra-class CoolIT-like '~85 C (est.)' at 120 W/cm2 and '~105 C' at 200 W/cm2: no model basis. CrossComb's 71 C is a linear flux scaling of the 350 W/cm2 fit that ignores the 300-350 W/cm2 patches it cites.

'Stack ~24x stiffer' and 'mount bow 4-25 um': both are taken from base-stress-stiffness, which assumed 85 % of each fin tip bonded and a 300 N load. Neither was recomputed for 25 % tie fraction, 10 mm webs at 25 % solidity, or the 1.6-2.4 kN PCM clamp. Scaled linearly, bow at 2 kN is about 27-167 um.

conventional-cost.lens: Manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility (process chain, yields, tolerances, cost basis, fouling/filtration, materials, burst/proof, service life, MGX/NVL height and mass fit, qualification burden)

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: 28.0/31.6 K with PCM and 30.0/35.5 K with CoolIT's paste match the physics-synthesis HMMC-R rows. The P90 of about 32/36 K still beats 34.4/44.2 K. The max is about 1-2 K optimistic because along-slot flow is ±20-25%, not the claimed ±10-12%, and the like-for-like mean margin is only -13%.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The robust core with liquid metal reaches 93 C on the 350 W/cm2 package and misses the 85 C line. Getting there needs the filtration-gated 0.10 mm core or direct-to-die. On uniform GPU TTVs at 1.2 LPM/kW the average is 1-2 K worse than split-flow (worse still at NVIDIA's 0.75-1.0 LPM/kW), and the plate wins only when zoned to the dies.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 6.3 kPa is credible (design H 5.0 kPa plus metering slits), and the inertial slot-to-slot metering is sound. The proposal also names the UQD08 pair as the dominant loop loss. Against that: the along-slot ratio of 3.5-5 is far below the rule of 15; the side-by-side 25 + 30 mm headers feed each slot about 15 mm off-centre, so it is not actually centre-fed; and slit jets (3.2 m/s) and ports (3.0 m/s) exceed copper velocity guidance at 36 LPM.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length that stays fixed as the plate grows, plus tiled header pairs, is a real scaling path. 30 kW needs liquid metal or bigger ports and headers, which means a taller bar. 16 mm ports already hit 3 m/s at 36 LPM, and a 250 cm2 plate at 60 LPM is 67 kPa port-to-port.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Each process exists on its own, but the make-or-break single-cycle, four-part Ag-Cu eutectic braze of 0.10 mm fin tips is not a volume process. It needs a 1.6-3.1 kN stack load per plate (diffusion-bond-class tooling) against a ±40 µm part-plane stack-up, and unmasked slot walls would take about 4-5 g of Ag that drains into the fin entrances. The comb as written (closed-end through-slots by gang slitting) cannot be cut, and cost is understated by US$25-45: 2026 copper, twice the skive strokes, braze fixtures, early yield.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The 0.15 mm floor, all-copper wetted path, tied zero-bow sandwich and full OCP/PPAP plan are right. But the 12 cm2 screen in a 16 mm port does not fit hydraulically, will blind in weeks to months by the programme's own loading numbers, cannot be serviced in a 1U tray, and has no sensing. Height (33 mm plus stubs) and mass (1.8 kg) against 1U NVL trays are unverified, bare copper departs from the de-facto EN-Ni practice (and the proposed EN option defeats the Ag-Cu bond), and burst at 2.0 MPa is below 3x MAWP.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The concept sits on expired Harpole, Cooligy and Walpole art, and the proposal correctly flags the need to verify the '513 continuation. However, continuous skived fins crossed by many interior inlet slots, with the outermost outlet slots at the channel ends, are exactly the case the FTO report says '2+ slots' does not safely design around until 2028-2031. The plate's own construction claims are narrow and easy to design around with etched or CNC manifolds.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: A conventional supply chain, all-CNC prototypes in 8-10 weeks and a well-ordered list of risk-retiring experiments are strengths. The braze process will likely need 2+ iterations; NVIDIA buys plates centrally through Group-A suppliers; and Rubin Ultra is moving to microchannel lids. That makes 12-18 months to a volume PO optimistic: 18-24 months is more realistic, with design-in more likely on hyperscaler ASICs than on NVIDIA.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: One core covers a coherent family: GPU, CPU, switch/CPO, wafer-scale tiles, an 800 VDC power-shelf SKU in the same PG25 loop, an aluminium CAB-brazed EV variant and a laser-diode niche. The EV part is a different alloy and joining route that shares only the architecture.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It adopts the corrected physics numbers, gives P90 columns, states where it loses (height, mass, filler, uniform-TTV average) and lists claims to avoid. It also has internal inconsistencies: 'centre-fed' versus offset headers; ±10-12% versus its own ratio of 3.5; 'everything else <1.8 m/s' versus 3.2 m/s slits; mass 1.8 kg versus 2.39 kg in its own model output; 'demonstrated' 21 kW; copper at US$10-12/kg; and C-SAM through 12-30 mm of copper.

fatal_flaws: Unproven make-or-break joint, so the claim 'only processes already run at >100k cold plates/yr' does not hold. One vacuum cycle must close, at the same time, 27 x 432 fin-tip ties (0.10 x 2.0 mm annealed fins), 27 web-top slot-to-slot seals, the frame-to-land seal and the floor-to-bar seals. The liquid comes only from 5-8 µm plated Ag (about 7-11 µm of eutectic) against a stack-up of ±20 µm fin-tip plane plus ±20 µm web-foot plane. The specified 0.1-0.2 MPa stack load is 1.6-3.1 kN per 125 mm plate: differential-expansion, diffusion-bond-class tooling, not the 100-300-plates-per-load batch furnace the US$8 braze cost assumes. At 790 C the first-contact fins will lean or crush into the 0.15 mm gaps. Electroplating the comb on 'both faces' also plates the 27 slot walls unless they are masked, about 4-5 g of Ag that melts and drains straight into the fin entrances under each web edge.

The integrated 50 µm screen, which the 10-year drop-in life claim depends on, does not work as specified. A 12 cm2 pleated cartridge inside a 16 mm port bore leaves about 47-90 mm2 of flow area: 3-6 m/s and several kPa, not 0.4 kPa. By the programme's own fouling-filtration loading numbers (a 5 cm2, 50 µm port cartridge reaches 50% blinding in 13 days at 1e-4 particles/mL), it becomes the loop's filter and needs service every few weeks to months. There is no tool-less access in a 1U tray, the plate has no in-plate sensing, and a blinding screen starves a single GPU in a rack of parallel plates. The '1.0x skived life' claim is not defensible.

Drop-in fit is not established, and the mission ('beats in every measurable aspect') is not met. The plate is 33 mm at the header bar, with horizontal 16 mm stubs, 1.8 kg and an 8-screw retention scheme, aimed at 1U NVL72-class compute trays (1U confirmed) without any envelope check. It loses to the benchmark on height, mass, filler-free construction, uniform-TTV average at 1.2 LPM/kW, and unit cost (+40-80% versus the US$105 skived plate).

The comb cannot be made as written. Closed-end 108 mm through-slots inside a 125 mm frame are impossible with a gang of slitting saws: an arbor-mounted stack is at least ~60 mm in diameter, and the entry-face run-out of a 10.5 mm deep plunge adds about 17-23 mm per end (top-face slot about 143-150 mm). The workable fixes each cost something: slitting from the fin side gives arc-ended, tapered slots and changes along-slot hydraulics; open slots plus brazed end bars add pressure-boundary joints; end-milling takes about 10x the cycle time. Any of them invalidates the US$13 / 2-3 min comb line.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Zoning set without new tooling: per-slot metering-slit width in a stamped or laser-cut floor plate, plus NC-programmed skive pitch, gives each SKU a heat-proportional flow map (die block 85-90%, HBM 0.3-0.5x) from one tool set.
Inertial metering slits sized so the branch loss is at least 6-8x the header dynamic head. Both terms scale with Q^2, so slot-to-slot uniformity holds from 0.5 to 2.4 LPM/kW.

Thick during processing, thin afterwards: skive and braze on a 2.0 mm base, then fly-cut the die face to 1.0 mm (0.8 mm minimum) after brazing. This absorbs braze distortion and sets flatness at 20 µm or better without a separate lapping step.

End-of-line 100% dP-versus-flow test at three flows, with CpK of 1.33 or better on dP, alongside He leak and proof. It catches internal slot-to-slot cross-leaks and blocked fin regions that a leak test cannot see.
Dead-end bleed notches at both ends of every slot, plus a symmetric, reverse-flow-tolerant comb that can be back-flushed, so dense particles do not settle in sieving dead-ends.

Reporting discipline: three dP boundaries (port-to-port, with stubs, with QD pair), flow-equivalence and equal-pumping-power curves, a P90 column, OCP v1.0.0 format with an independent repeat, and an explicit list of claims to avoid.
A three-tier interface ladder on one core: PCM pad as the drop-in, liquid metal on electrolytic Ni for OEMs, and a stepped bare-die pedestal for chip co-design.

Header bar, stamped selector floor and comb as separate machinable or stampable parts. The manifold needs no etching or diffusion bonding, which keeps second-sourcing open across any Taiwanese or Vietnamese skive-and-braze house.
numbers_disputed: Factory cost US$145 at 100k/yr; corrected US$170-190. Four adjustments: (1) copper at Aug-2026 LME records of US$14.3-14.9k/t (Cochilco via miningreporters.com, 17 Aug 2026: US$14,850/t cash) plus the OFE premium gives US$16-18/kg, not US$10-12/kg, adding US$8-12 on a ~2.8 kg blank net of swarf credit; (2) 432 skive strokes at 0.25 mm pitch is about twice a GB200-class core, adding US$10-15, and needs 4-6 machines per 100k/yr rather than 2-3; (3) braze fixtures that must carry load reduce furnace density, adding US$7-12; (4) first-year yield is more like 85-90% than 93-97%, adding US$8-15.
'US$8/kW of demonstrated capacity (21 kW)': nothing has been demonstrated. 21 kW is a model output (±25% per term), so the per-kW cost claim is speculative.

Along-slot uniformity ±10-12%; corrected ±20-25%. The proposal's own branch-to-slot dynamic-head ratio is 3.5-5 against a rule of 15. The manifold-maldistribution table gives max/min 1.46 at ratio 3.5 even for a truly centre-fed slot. Here the side-by-side 25 mm and 30 mm headers put inlet feeds about 16.5 mm and outlet drains about 14 mm off-centre in opposite directions, so the long half is about 70 mm, not 54 mm. The flow hot-spot term becomes 2.3-3 K, so the nominal max dT is about 32.6-33.5 K, not 31.6 K.

'Everything else <1.8 m/s at 36 LPM': the inlet selector-slit jets run at 3.2 m/s at 36 LPM (18/13 LPM through 14.4 mm2 gives 1.6 m/s at 18 LPM) and 2.4 m/s at 150% rated flow. After about 8 jet widths (~0.8 decay) they reach the 0.10 mm fin tips at about 2-2.6 m/s, above the 1.5-2.0 m/s copper erosion-corrosion guidance. The 16 mm copper port bores are at 2.2 m/s at 150% rated flow.

Inlet screen dP of 0.4 kPa clean; corrected about 2-5 kPa clean through the core and annulus of a cartridge in a 16 mm bore at 18 LPM, and about 5-12 kPa at 50% blinding (scaled from fouling-filtration section 3 and the gap report's 2-5 kPa screen budget).
Burst design 2.0 MPa: three times the 0.69 MPa MAWP is 2.07 MPa, and against the preferred 150 psi MAWP in the requirements list it is 3.1 MPa or more. As specified it sits just below the 3x rule.

Annealed copper yield taken as 70 MPa everywhere: OFE after a 790 C vacuum cycle with grain growth is about 40-60 MPa (0.2% offset). At 56 MPa under burst, the header-bar top wall (4 mm over 30 mm) is not yield-safe, although it is still rupture-safe.

Mass of 1.8 kg (15 kW class) and 1.5 kg (GPU class), while the proposal's own crosscomb_model_output.md section G prints 2.39 kg and 2.10 kg finished. The 1.8 kg figure is consistent only with the 64 mm-wide hollowed header bar, which the model run did not use, so the two must be reconciled before any envelope check.

CoolIT height of '~15-20 mm': the benchmark synthesis gives a ~10-13 mm body with the bar ~12-15 mm proud, so 22-28 mm at the bar. CrossComb is therefore 2-5 mm thicker in the body and 5-11 mm taller at the bar.

'C-SAM sampling' of fin-tip bonds: acoustic microscopy cannot resolve 0.1 mm-wide bonds at 0.25 mm pitch through 12-30 mm of copper. Use X-ray CT of samples (Ag contrasts with Cu) plus destructive sectioning, and budget for both.

Time to first volume PO of 12-18 months; corrected 18-24 months, allowing at least two braze-process iterations (fixture load, Ag quantity, slot-wall masking), the comb slitting rework and NVIDIA's Group-A / RVL gating.

conventional-cost.lens: Strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims: differentiation against CoolIT and the Nvidia Group-A suppliers (Jentech, AVC, Cooler Master, Delta); freedom to operate against CoolIT Split-Flow, JetCool, Frore, Mikros and Asetek; application breadth; how convincing the win would be to an OEM or hyperscaler under OCP v1.0; whether the business model is realistic

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: Nominal 28.0 / 31.6 K against the measured 34.4 / 44.2 K matches the physics synthesis HMMC-R row, and the max-dT, uniformity and Q-capacity wins hold up. The average-dT win depends on swapping paste for a PCM pad. At the proposal's own P90 with CoolIT's paste, the average is <=34 K against 34.4 K, which is a statistical tie, so an OEM running a like-for-like test sees parity on the mean.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The robust core misses T_case <= 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with liquid metal (93 C); reaching the line needs the 0.10 mm core behind <=25 um loops or direct-to-die. On 1-3.6 kW uniform TTVs at 1.2 LPM/kW the proposal's own model shows it losing on average dT by 0.4-2.4 K, and even liquid metal loses at 36-45 cm2. That is the volume product class, and it is the comparison CoolIT can run under the OCP spec it authored. The wins appear only on zoned, die-realistic TTVs that need NDA power maps.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 6.3 kPa port-to-port and 1.9 W at 18 LPM are credible. The coupling spec is realistic: UQD08, three dP boundaries per OCP, and an admission that the QDs dominate loop dP. Slot-to-slot metering is sound (7.8x header head). The along-slot ratio of 3.5-5 breaks the programme's own >=15 rule. A single 1.2 mm slit jets at 1.6 m/s into an open-bottom slot and lands on the fin tips, an unmodelled centre-loading effect. The Rev B orifice-strip fix reopens JetCool claim questions.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length stays at 4 mm at any size, the comb tiles with a header pair per 110 mm, and Q capacity is 21 / 29 / 36 kW (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / performance core with liquid metal). Wafer-scale and multi-die scaling is a genuine structural advantage over single-split plates. 30 kW+ still needs liquid metal or 25 um loops, and the 16 mm ports reach the 3 m/s cap at 36 LPM.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Every step is a high-volume process with TW/VN second sources, which hyperscalers value. Factory cost of US$145 is +38% over the ~US$105 incumbent and above the US$110-125 the cost gap report gives the etched-laminate HMMC, so the 'conventional-cost' lens produces the more expensive HMMC route. Other drawbacks: 1.8 kg of copper, and a single-cycle Ag-Cu eutectic braze of 0.10 mm fins at 0.15 mm gaps (erosion, wicking) with unproven yield.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The qualification matrix and burst margin are thorough. Fouling life is 0.6-1.2x the incumbent, so it may be worse. A per-plate screen cartridge with no in-plate sensing is a new service and failure point inside sealed trays. The 33 mm bar height against the MGX envelope is unverified, the plate weighs 1.8 kg on the package, and the wetted path carries declared Ag-Cu fillets that procurement teams will challenge against filler-free unibody competitors.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The design is a continuous skived fin field with interior inlet slots splitting flow both ways and the outermost slots acting as outlets near the field ends. That is the case the FTO gap report says is not a safe design-around ('comprising' plus 'an'), and the proposal restates the refuted 'not a single central slot' argument, skips fin segmentation, and charts only 3 of at least 6 Split-Flow-family patents. It omits '567 (revived by the Federal Circuit in 2024), '691, the '878 CIP chain and '906, and has no analysis of Mikros/Jabil, Toyota TEMA manifold-microchannel or Danfoss ShowerPower families. Its own claims are narrow construction claims on expired Cooligy/Harpole concepts, and it says 'no proprietary process is involved', so it has no moat.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: All-CNC prototypes in 8-10 weeks, TTV data in month 4 and a 12-18 month path to PPAP are credible. First volume around 2028 falls inside the Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031 US Split-Flow window, which gives hyperscaler customers exposure through imports (including ITC risk). Nvidia's centralised Group-A purchasing locks Rubin and Rubin Ultra sockets, so the realistic first socket is a 2028 hyperscaler ASIC with no RVL standing.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: One architecture covers GPU, CPU, switch/CPO, wafer-scale, 800 VDC shelves, aluminium EV and laser-diode SKUs, which is broad on paper. The power-electronics SKUs have no Rth or Tj numbers against pin-fin or ShowerPower incumbents, and the 800 VDC market is US$4-90M/yr. The isothermal-caloric penalty lands in the 5-30 W/cm2 power-electronics regime, and the aluminium EV variant is a separate commodity product.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It is unusually candid about where it loses, gives a claims-to-avoid list and a reproducible model run. Several claims overreach. It asserts a 45-50% gross margin at a US$280-300 ASP when the superseding cost gap says US$300 includes UQDs and hoses. It calls modelled capacity 'demonstrated', understates CoolIT's height, builds its IP section on superseded logic, and keeps the compliant-design hot-spot term even though it breaks the along-slot rule.

fatal_flaws: The mission's claim ('beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect') is not met, and the proposal admits it. It loses on height (33 mm against CoolIT's ~22-28 mm at the bar), mass (1.8 vs ~1.5 kg), factory cost (+38%), fouling-life band (0.6-1.2x), filler-free construction, and average dT on 1-3.6 kW uniform TTVs at 1.2 LPM/kW (+0.4 to +2.4 K, with liquid metal still losing at 36-45 cm2). The last loss sits in the volume GPU class, measured under the OCP v1.0 convention CoolIT authored, so CoolIT can publish a counter-comparison the day CrossComb shows data.

Split-Flow freedom to operate is not cleared and the stated design-around is the one the programme's own FTO gap report rejected. CrossComb uses continuous skived fins with interior inlet slots splitting flow in opposing directions, outermost outlet slots at the fin-field ends, and a comb brazed onto the fin tips, which plausibly reads on 'matingly engaged'. It charts only '330/'284/'513. It misses US 9,057,567, whose claims were revived when the Federal Circuit vacated the PTAB decision on 7 Mar 2024 (CoolIT v. Vidal, 22-1221), plus 9,453,691, the 12,460,878 CIP chain and 12,101,906. First volume around 2028 falls inside the Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031 US window. The fix (fins segmented under every outlet slot, interior-only outlets, a dated expired-art mapping memo) is cheap but absent.

There is no defensible moat, so the business case does not hold. The concept is expired Harpole/Cooligy art, the proposal itself says 'no proprietary process is involved', and the provisional claims are narrow construction claims that an etched or one-piece CNC manifold avoids. Every Group-A house already runs skiving and brazing. CoolIT is the one firm free to build multi-split plates under its own patents until 2028-31, and Nvidia's centralised purchasing can fold the idea into a reference design. A 45-50% gross margin at a US$280-300 bare-plate ASP is not credible against a US$200-260 bare-plate market where Group-A gross margins are 17-20%.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: A gang-slit copper comb brazed to the fin tips at 90 degrees, serving as both manifold and structural tie. It gives the 1.0 mm tied-sandwich base with commodity tooling, without etching or diffusion bonding.
A stamped or laser-cut selector floor with per-slot metering slits: zone flow is set per SKU by a cheap pattern change (near-zero tooling cost), with the branch-to-header dynamic-head ratio kept >=6.
An integrated, serviceable 50 um absolute pleated screen in the inlet boss, plus slot dead-end bleed notches and dP tap ports. This makes the 0.15 mm channel floor deployable on today's loops.
A 100% production dP-vs-flow slope test at three flows to catch internal inlet-to-outlet bypass or blocked fin regions. It is cheap, inline and unusual among incumbents.

A transparency package under OCP v1.0: R vs flow at >=6 points, dP at three named boundaries (port-to-port, with stubs, with UQD pair), 3 plates x 3 assemblies, CpK and an independent-lab repeat. Pair it with flow-equivalence (34.4 K at 0.72 LPM/kW) and equal-pumping-power curves rather than one flow point.
A TCO pitch built on W+ inlet capability (T_case,max ~82 C at 15 kW with 50 C inlet), which the market gap report values at US$4-10M capex per 100 MW, against the weaker $/kW-of-capacity framing.
A green-laser perimeter seam as a filler-free outer pressure boundary, to meet 'no braze' procurement objections.
An explicit 'where we do not win' and 'claims to avoid' section. It builds credibility with hyperscaler thermal teams who will rerun the tests.
A supply-resilience pitch: second-sourceable through any TW/VN skiving and brazing house, and forged near-net header bars at 1M/yr.
numbers_disputed: 'US$280-300 ASP plate with 45-50% gross margin' -> realistic bare-plate ASP is US$200-260. The Morgan Stanley US$300 per plate carries UQD halves and hoses worth US$38-95, and Group-A gross margin is ~17-20%. At US$145-165 factory cost that gives at best 25-37% gross margin, lower under Nvidia's centralised pricing (gap-cost-volume-and-market-anchors.md section 1 and section 2.1; synthesis C12).

CoolIT plate height '~15-20 mm' -> ~22-28 mm at the bar (plate ~10-13 mm thick plus a bar ~12-15 mm proud, from the photogrammetry gap report, synthesis row 'Heat link... height'). The real height penalty is ~5-11 mm, not 13-18 mm: the comparison is wrong, though the error runs in CrossComb's favour.

Split-Flow family 'US 8,746,330 / 9,603,284 / 12,495,513, expiry ~Aug 2028 + PTA' -> the family is at least six patents: '330, '284, '513 (USPTO front matter confirms it continues 15/462,753 -> 14/283,163 -> 12/189,476), '567 (claims revived by the Federal Circuit 7 Mar 2024), '691 and the '878 CIP chain, with '906 still unread. Each expires 11 Aug 2028 plus its own PTA, so the window runs to ~mid-2031 (gap-splitflow FTO; synthesis C13).

'Per kW of demonstrated capacity US$8/kW vs US$9/kW' -> no capacity has been demonstrated; it is model output at +/-25% per term. Using the proposal's conservative Q capacity of 17.4-18 kW (paste) at US$165 gives ~US$9.2-9.5/kW against ~US$9.4/kW, which is parity. Plates are also bought per package, not per kW.

Like-for-like same-paste average '30.0 K (-13%)' -> at the proposal's own P90 it is <=34 K against 34.4 K measured, a statistical tie. The defensible like-for-like wins are max dT (-6 to -9 K), max-minus-average uniformity and dP, not the average.

GPU-class uniform TTV deficit 'average 1-2 K worse' -> the proposal's own model table C gives +2.4 K (36 cm2), +2.0 K (45 cm2), +1.2 K (60 cm2) and +0.4 K (80 cm2) with PCM against CoolIT-like paste. With liquid metal it still loses by 1.3 K at 36 cm2 and 0.8 K at 45 cm2.

Cost premium '~US$40 at 100k/yr' presented as the conventional-cost answer -> the etched-laminate HMMC is costed at US$110-125 (synthesis 6.2, G-COST). Excluding photochemical etching, itself a high-volume conventional process, adds ~US$20-35 per plate, so this route is the costlier HMMC, not the cheaper one.

Nominal max dT 31.6 K with a 1.3 K flow term -> it assumes +/-10-12% along-slot uniformity at an along-slot ratio of 3.5-5, against the programme's >=15 rule, and ignores the 1.6 m/s slit jet landing on the fin tips under each slit. Until the flow rig measures it, quote the +/-20% case (32.6 K) and a P90 of ~36 K externally.

Rubin-Ultra-class CoolIT-like 'T_case ~85 C (est.)' against CrossComb PCM at 71 C -> scaling the proposal's own 350 W/cm2 fit (caloric fixed at constant LPM/kW; base, TIM and convection proportional to flux) gives ~75-87 C for the split-flow plate. The honest margin is ~4-16 K, not ~14 K.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: I re-ran d2d_run.py and coldplate_model.py and got the same numbers: 22.3/24.4 K nominal, 24.2/26.4 K at P90 and end of life. They use the isothermal caloric term (0.60 x 12.66 K), a non-optimistic h_eff of 127 kW/m2K (Nu about 8.4, close to fully developed, fin efficiency 0.56 checks) and the deployable 0.15 mm gap. However, on a ceramic TTV Tier 3A is just Tier 2 with 0.2 mm less base, and most of the margin is the liquid-metal (LM) interface: with the same paste the engine gives 30.0/35.0 K (-13%/-21%), and with the same LM a CoolIT-like plate gives 27.5/34.4 K.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: Removing the lid and TIM1 is a real, physics-backed gain of 21-33 K at the junction.
