But the deployable R core misses Tj <= 105 C at 45 C inlet even by its own numbers (109 C), and reaches 111-119 C with 775 um silicon and its own 30-45 um bond-line formula, before 2-3x on-die hot spots. At 2-4 kW with lidded framing, its plate-average dT is worse than split-flow (caloric pinning at NTU about 5). The die-level comparison against Rubin mixes lid removal, TIM and zoning, and Rubin ships lidded anyway.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: The 5.7 kPa plate dP (ports 2.57 + comb 2.0 + headers 0.5 + channel 0.23 + screen 0.4) and the inertial orifice-comb uniformity basis (global 1.10) match the design-H physics. Couplings are discussed, but the scorecard pumping power is plate-only. 'UQD12-class' is not in OCP UQD v2.0.0, and the 13 mm manifold block cannot hold design-H headers: either the plate is about 30 mm tall or the headers shrink and the uniformity basis no longer holds. Per-zone flow under 3x/0.3x zoning has not been tested.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: The 30.8 kW Q-cap holds 1.2 LPM/kW constant: 37 LPM, 3.06 m/s in the 16 mm ports (twice its own cap), about 22 kPa at the plate plus UQD08 losses of roughly 80-140 kPa. At the fixed 18 LPM design flow the cap is about 25 kW. Tiled engines and per-reticle pedestals are plausible, but LM-field containment risk and header height both grow with area and flow.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Every process is conventional. The stack is risky, though: diffusion-bonding a field of 0.10 x 2.0 mm fins at 900 C and 5-10 MPa (fin-tip stress 12-25 MPa, above annealed Cu flow stress, so upsetting and lean), then fly-cutting a 0.8 mm crowned pedestal over that fin field, a per-SKU face map, Ni porosity control and LM pre-wetting. Factory cost of US$175-225 at 100k/yr is 1.7-2.1x a skived plate, and the stated height is optimistic.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Fouling is handled correctly (0.15 mm gap, 50 um absolute integrated screen, bleeds, dP signature). But the lead product depends on Ga-In containment and ageing over 80-150 cm2 under 0.6-1.7 shear strain per cycle, with no public data. It is not drop-in on lidded parts, makes the plate vendor the de facto TIM1 owner, is exposed to gallium supply restrictions, and is serviced at depot with a 5-year inspection interval.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The engine sits on expired art, but Tiers 3A and 3B sit in the micro-channel-lid / direct-to-die thicket (Intel, Nvidia, Jentech, TSMC, CoolIT compliant member) that the proposal itself lists as 'avoid'. Claims 1 and 4 (LM field with dam, conformally coated passives, pre-wetted FRU) are weak against PS5-style LM containment prior art. Claim 3 is a business-process claim.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: First qualified 3A socket at M15-18 at best, gated by lidless package access that silicon vendors control and by an LM qualification with no precedent at this size. 3B follows the silicon calendar (24-30 months). The proposal itself rates being leapfrogged by in-die cooling after 2029 as certain.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The tier ladder (lidded PCM/LM, bare-die, MCL core, manifold cap) plus CPUs, switches, wafer-scale, RF and CPO is broad. The power-electronics story is weak: a stiff Cu engine Ag-sintered straight to AMB/DBC invites ceramic cracking under -40/+150 C cycling, 0.2 mm gaps in unfiltered EV WEG loops are not deployable, and at 5-30 W/cm2 the manifold's caloric pinning erases its advantage.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: The numbers are fully reproducible and consistent with the physics synthesis, with Monte Carlo bands and an exemplary 'where DD3 does not win' section. But the headline (-35%/-45%) and scorecard compare LM (and lid removal) against CoolIT's paste with no like-for-like row. The 21-25 mm height contradicts the physics source (about 25 mm block, about 30 mm plate). The Rubin rows conflate effects, and the CoolIT-like reconstruction overpredicts CoolIT's measured 4 kW plate by about 40% yet is still used as the comparison baseline.

fatal_flaws: The lead product's (3A, also Tier 2) decisive numbers rest on about 1.5-2 g of Ga-In over 80-150 cm2 of bare die, mold compound and HBM, under 0.6-1.7 CTE shear strain per cycle. No public containment or ageing data exist at this size; the proposal itself rates this 'high / product-defining'. Shipping the LM pre-wetted on the plate side only means bare Si is wetted by a 6-15 psi press, and voids and oxide-skin contact can plausibly double R'' to 0.03-0.05, wiping out most of the gain over lidded LM. If LM fails qualification, the 350 W/cm2 story collapses to 78 K Tj-to-inlet (123 C).

The lead tier has no addressable Nvidia volume socket. Rubin ships with a Au-plated lid, Rubin Ultra is moving to micro-channel lids owned by lid makers (Jentech), and Nvidia buys plates centrally from Group-A. That leaves hyperscaler bare-die ASICs, whose owners design their own plates, and on any 3A socket the plate vendor carries de facto TIM1 and die-warranty liability.

The mission requires beating CoolIT 'in every measurable aspect', and by the proposal's own admission this is not met. It does not beat CoolIT on height or mass (and its 21-25 mm height is understated against the physics value of about 30 mm), on serviceability (LM depot FRU against field paste), or on unit cost (about 1.7-2x a skived plate). On average case dT for low-flux 2-4 kW lidded footprints it is worse than split-flow (16.7 vs 16.1 K at Rubin 2.3 kW, even with LM).

The headline -35% avg / -45% max against CoolIT is mostly an interface swap (LM vs CoolIT's paste), which CoolIT can make too: direct-to-die and MCL are on its published roadmap. The defensible architecture-only margin is -19%/-29% (both plates on LM) or -13%/-21% (both on paste).

The 'decisive gain on real silicon' is not a Tj-compliant claim for the deployable core. 3A-R gives Tj 109 C at 45 C inlet nominally, about 111-119 C with 775 um Si and 30-45 um LM bond lines, and another 5-15 K with on-die hot spots. Only the 0.10 mm P core behind <= 33 um absolute loop filtration gets near 105 C.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: One bonded HMMC engine whose product tier (lapped Cu for PCM, electrolytic Ni without Au for LM, stepped pedestal for bare die, Ni/Au lid-core) is set only by post-bond face finishing: one furnace, one wetted-side qualification.

A post-bond fly-cut stepped pedestal: die plateau crowned to the inverse of the hot-state shadow-moire warpage per package SKU, and HBM fingers that always keep >= 30 um of gap so the plate never bears on HBM.
Load-limited kinematic float (0.04-0.10 MPa on the dies) with stiffener hard-stop pads that take shock, decoupling thermal contact from mechanical loads.

Gallium containment engineered as a subsystem: 3-5 um electrolytic Ni (0.0006 cm2K/W) or 1 um sputtered W barrier, no Au on the plate side, FKM dam, capture moat, conformally coated passives, Galinstan for -40 C storage, porosity test.

A separable manifold cap (headers, metering comb, screen, ports) as the future fluid-delivery layer for Si micro-coolers and in-die channels, plus a proposed OCP liquid-cooled package interface (port pitch, seal face, cleanliness class).

Zoning by comb hole count at fixed slot pitch (die block 85-90% of flow, HBM 0.3-0.5x, unheated margin about 2% against stagnation), so a new package needs new comb artwork rather than a new plate, backed by heat-map-to-comb software.
100% production dP-signature test at rated flow (5.3 +/- 0.6 kPa) that doubles as field fouling and screen-service monitoring.

Junction-to-inlet R'' and 'max die flux at Tj <= 105 C' as the comparison metric for real silicon, plus a bond-line penalty table as a design rule (each 25 um costs about 4 K with LM, 10 K with PCM, 25 K with paste at 350 W/cm2).
A TTV-C real-silicon diode test vehicle (tiled 26 x 33 mm dies with HBM dummies on a warping 120 mm substrate) as the only credible proof of junction-level claims, plus independent-lab repetition.
numbers_disputed: Headline 22.3/24.4 K, quoted as -35%/-45% vs CoolIT: for a like-for-like interface, the CoolIT-like reconstruction with the same LM+Ni (0.0156) gives 27.5/34.4 K (coldplate_model.py, my run), so the architecture gain is -19% avg / -29% max. With the same paste the engine gives 30.0/35.0 K (-13%/-21%).

Plate height 21-25 mm (13 mm manifold block): manifold-maldistribution.md requires about 25 mm of block (8 mm slots + 15-20 mm design-H headers + walls), so the plate is about 28-31 mm, consistent with the physics synthesis's 'plate is ~30 mm thick'. A 16 mm horizontal port bore alone needs about 20 mm of wall height.

Q capacity 30.8 kW: at constant 1.2 LPM/kW this needs 37 LPM, 3.06 m/s in the 16 mm ports (twice its own 1.5 m/s rule), about 22 kPa at the plate plus UQD08 losses of 78-139 kPa at 36 LPM. At the fixed 18 LPM design flow the model gives T_case,max 84.7 C at 25 kW, so the corrected capacity is about 25 kW.

Pumping power 1.7 vs 7.4 W (4.3x): this is plate-only. With one common UQD08 pair (20-35 kPa at 18 LPM) the loop totals are about 33 vs 52 kPa, a 1.6x advantage. 'UQD12-class' is not in OCP UQD v2.0.0 (gap-hydraulic report: 'not confirmed to exist'), and the synthesis's corrected CoolIT reconstruction is 21.8 kPa, not 24.6.

Tj-to-inlet 64.4 K and 323 W/cm2 max die flux for 3A-R: these assume 0.6 mm Si at 120 W/mK (0.050) and LM at 0.0156. With 775 um Si (0.065-0.074), the proposal's own 30 um bond-line formula (0.0176) and an isothermal die-zone caloric (NTU 0.49, cal_frac 0.54, 7.2 K instead of 6.7 K), I get 66-74 K (Tj 111-119 C) and a max flux of about 280-300 W/cm2, before 2-3x on-die hot spots (+5-15 K).

Rubin 2.3 kW die-average Tj-to-inlet, CoolIT 53 K vs DD3 28 K: this mixes lid removal, TIM and zoning. A CoolIT-like split-flow plate going direct-to-die on the same LM computes to about 42 K (16.7 + 117 x (0.05 + 0.0156 + 0.051 + 0.099)), and about 37.5 K if zoned, so the plate-attributable gain is 9-14 K, not 25 K. The CoolIT-like model also overpredicts CoolIT's measured 4 kW plate (50.7 K vs < 36 K max), so the CoolIT baseline is inflated.

4 kW point, Tier 1 PCM at 34.4 K max: against CoolIT's measured < 36 K (Tr < 0.009 C/W, TIM included) this is parity within the stated +/-25%, not a win. Only the LM tiers (26.1 K) clearly beat the real 4 kW plate.

3B indium shear strain of 0.06-0.1 per cycle is a per-die figure. For one Cu lid-core over a 53 x 67 mm 4-die block on CoWoS-L, outer-die corners could see about 0.2 per power cycle and about 0.6 per -40/+125 C cycle (TIM physics rule: soldered attach needs plate CTE <= 8 ppm/K). The block diagonal (about 85 mm) also exceeds the proposal's own > 70 mm CuW threshold (+30% R).
'CoolIT 34.4 K average reproduced at 0.55 LPM/kW (8.2 LPM)': the outlet rise is 27.8 K, so the outlet is 72.8 C, above the 65 C return limit. The proposal flags this only for the 0.42 LPM/kW case.

HBM finger base of 0.55 mm and a 0.3 mm deep moat cut into a 1.0 mm base: both go below base-stress-stiffness.md's 0.8 mm minimum finished thickness (machining 0.1-0.2 mm + erosion 0.1 mm). Where the moat sits on the perimeter land, the land safety factor falls roughly as t^2 (5.8 to about 2.8 at a 1.5 MPa burst, about 1.4 at the proposal's 3.0 MPa design burst) unless the land is stepped thicker.

direct-to-die.lens: Manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility (process chain at volume, yields and tolerances, cost basis, fouling and filtration, materials compatibility with OCP/ASHRAE/Nvidia, burst and proof, service life, height and mass fit in MGX/NVL trays, qualification burden)

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The engine numbers reproduce the physics synthesis: 22.3/24.4 K with liquid metal (LM) and 27.4/30.4 K with PCM on the die, against CoolIT's 34.4/44.2 K, so the plate wins whichever interface is used. The headline gain is mostly the TIM, though. Paste to LM is 7 of the 12 K, the OCP v1.0.0 method tests with a recommended TIM (most likely PCM), and the proposal itself admits the lead tier (3A) beats Tier 2 by only 0.6 K on a ceramic TTV.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: This is where the concept earns its place: removing the lid and TIM1 gives 64 K junction-to-inlet, against 86 K for the best lidded path on the same engine. Even so, the robust core misses Tj <= 105 C at 45 C inlet (109 C), and the 3A-P core needs loops filtered to <= 33 um absolute. At Rubin plate level with a lid, the average is at parity or slightly worse than split-flow; the win is in the maximum.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 5.7 kPa including the screen, a 1.10 global max/min and an inertial etched comb that keeps uniformity independent of flow all match the synthesis design H. The coupling analysis is realistic: a UQD08 pair costs about 25 kPa at 18 LPM. However 'UQD12' is not confirmed to exist in OCP UQD v2.0.0, and the dP rise from a loaded screen is ignored.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Q capacity is 30.8 kW with LM and 22 kW with PCM at T_case <= 85 C, and the manifold tiles to wafer scale with per-tile floats. The weak point is the single LM field. CTE shear between the Cu pedestal and Si grows linearly with span, to a shear strain of about 1.5-2 per cycle on 120-150 mm CoWoS-L, which is exactly where scaling is claimed.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: The tied sandwich (0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins diffusion-bonded tip-to-grate at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa) has no volume precedent. Fin-tip contact fraction is about 0.2, so local stress is 25-50 MPa, above the hot flow stress of annealed Cu, which means fins upset and gaps close. 850-950 C is also above the usual 50-75 % Tm diffusion-bonding window, and the BAg fallback brings back filler wicking into 0.15 mm gaps. Factory cost of US$175-225 at 100k is +65-115 % over the ~US$105 skived incumbent, on optimistic assumptions: 12 % yield/overhead and 50-200 plates per cycle.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The hermetic, braze-free all-Cu body, the burst/proof figures and the all-Cu/316L/EPDM wetted path are good. Against that: LM over 80-100 cm2 has no public reliability data (the proposal rates it high/product-defining); a liquid TIM cannot carry the 140-340 N static clamp, so the load goes through point contacts on bare Si; the 12 cm2 screen fails the evidence base's own pore-count rule; and 3B puts an EPDM O-ring seal over the package. Tier 3A is not drop-in (lidless die without Au backside, stiffener hard-stop pads, per-SKU pedestal, module owner warranting LM as TIM1). The plate is about 2x CoolIT's height at 2.3 kg, and LM service is a depot FRU swap.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: It correctly steers clear of JetCool, Corintis, TSMC IMC-Si and Nvidia sensor IP. But continuous skived fins with between-end inlet slots can still read on the Split-Flow continuation '513 (expiry Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031, not '~Aug 2028'). 3B sits in Jentech/Nvidia/Intel microchannel-lid space, and the spring float has to be cleared against '886/'733. The proposed claims (dammed LM field, pre-wetted LM FRU, tier set by face finishing, direct-to-substrate sintering) face heavy prior art: PS5 foam dam, RTX 5090 FE, Semikron SKiN.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The lead product is gated by access to lidless packages, 2,000-cycle LM data, negotiated die-warranty indemnity and a module owner's JEDEC qualification. Meanwhile Nvidia is moving Rubin to gold-plated lids and the microchannel lid (where Jentech is the incumbent). The M15-18 qualification date is optimistic (24-36 months is realistic), and if LM fails, 3A collapses to PCM on the die, which is already Blackwell practice.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family covers lidded GPUs, bare-die ASICs, microchannel-lid cores, a manifold cap for in-silicon cooling, switches/CPUs, wafer-scale, RF/laser and co-packaged optics. Power electronics is weak: Ag-sintering ceramic substrates to a rigid 20+ mm Cu engine invites CTE fatigue over -40/+150 C cycling, and an all-Cu engine does not fit Al/WEG EV loops (the proposal admits this is a licensing play).

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It is model-traceable (d2d_run.out matches), has Monte Carlo bands, tags its sources and carries an honest 'where DD3 does not win' list. The weaknesses: it never states a same-TIM like-for-like number, the die-flux headline (129 to 323 W/cm2) mixes lid removal with engine gain, height and mass are called 'unknown' when the evidence base says CoolIT is ~10-13 mm, the screen size contradicts the physics rule, and B300 is listed as lidded when the envelope report says it is bare-die.

fatal_flaws: The lead product (Tier 3A: one LM field over the whole 80-100 cm2 molded interposer of a bare-die CoWoS-L) rests on an interface with no public reliability data above about 10 cm2. Consumer precedents (PS5, ROG, RTX 5090 FE) are 1-8 cm2. On a 120-150 mm package the Cu (17 ppm/K) to Si (~3 ppm/K) shear strain is about 1.5-2 per power cycle at 30 um bond line, on top of a 20-40 um cyclic gap change and a gallium short risk on the substrate. If the LM qualification fails, 3A falls back to PCM on the die (27.4 K on the TTV, 78 K at the junction). That is already today's Blackwell bare-die practice (Lenovo B200: PCM on die, putty on HBM), so nothing differentiates it beyond the HMMC engine the sibling proposals share.

The process chain that every structural and thermal claim depends on (0.8 mm pedestal, zero pressure bow, burst safety factors) has never been run at volume. Diffusion-bonding a skived 0.10 x 2.0 mm fin field tip-to-grate at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa puts about 25-50 MPa on the fin tips (fin solidity 0.4 x grate coverage 0.5), well above the flow stress of annealed OFE Cu at that temperature. The fins will upset or buckle and close the 0.15 mm gaps. Dropping the pressure leaves the laminate interfaces unbonded; the BAg fallback brings back filler wicking. Oregon State microlamination work documents exactly this trade-off between fin aspect ratio and bond quality.

As written, 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' is indefensible. The plate is 21-25 mm tall against CoolIT's ~10-13 mm (evidence base SYNTHESIS C19) and weighs 2.3 kg. Factory cost is +65-115 % over the skived incumbent. Serviceability (LM pre-wetted FRU, depot refurbishment) is worse than paste. The proposal concedes some of these but understates height as 'undisclosed'.

Drop-in fails for the lead tier. 3A needs a lidless die with no Au backside metallisation, hard-stop pads on the package stiffener held to +/-25 um, a per-SKU pedestal and dam, and a module owner willing to accept a third-party gallium TIM1 with negotiated die-warranty indemnity. Meanwhile Nvidia is moving Rubin to gold-plated lids and microchannel lids owned by Jentech, which leaves only hyperscaler ASIC sockets that already have incumbent bare-die suppliers.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: One bonded engine whose tier is set only by post-bond face finishing (lapped flat / electrolytic Ni plus dam groove / stepped pedestal), giving a single wetted-side qualification and one furnace route across lidded, LM and bare-die SKUs.

An etched heat-map orifice comb at the slot tops. Zoning becomes a phototool change (US$0.5-3k) rather than a new plate, the branch is inertial so uniformity holds at any flow, and fluid never passes over HBM downstream of a die.
A stepped pedestal whose HBM fingers always clear the stacks by >= 30 um (the plate never bears on HBM), crowned to the measured hot-state shadow-moire warpage of each package SKU (JESD22-B112).
Stiffener hard stops as the shock load path (engaging at 50 um overtravel), keeping 50 g shock loads off the dies.

A separable manifold cap (headers, comb, screen, ports) positioned as a standard 'liquid-cooled package interface' for microchannel lids, Si micro-coolers and in-die channels, so the company keeps the fluid-delivery role when in-silicon cooling arrives.
100 % production dP-signature test (5.3 +/- 0.6 kPa at 18 LPM) as a combined screen for blockage and bond quality, alongside 100 % He leak and an ISO 16232 flush.
An explicit TIM1-ownership and qualification table per tier, with a hyperscaler ASIC as the first bare-die socket because the buyer owns both package and plate.
Bond-line penalty table at 350 W/cm2 (LM / PCM / paste per 15-80 um) as the argument that bow control and interface choice outweigh fin refinement.

For any LM face: electrolytic Ni 3-5 um (never high-P electroless Ni) or a 1 um W barrier, no Au anywhere, Galinstan where -40 C storage applies, and coupling sizing that admits a UQD08 pair costs about 25 kPa at 18 LPM.
numbers_disputed: Max die flux at Tj <= 105 C: '129 -> 323 W/cm2' (2.5x). The 129 is a CoolIT-like plate with a lid and paste. The same plate direct-to-die with LM has R''j-in of about 0.357 - lid 0.064 - TIM1 0.015 - paste 0.07 + LM 0.016 = ~0.22 cm2K/W, which gives about 235-250 W/cm2. The gain attributable to the engine is about +30-35 %, not +150 %. Likewise, 139 K vs 64 K junction-to-inlet becomes about 85 K vs 64 K like-for-like.

Headline 15 kW TTV figures of 22.3/24.4 K (-35 %/-45 %) use LM on the heater. Under the OCP v1.0.0 recommended TIM (most probably PCM) the same plate gives 27.4/30.4 K (-20 %/-31 %). With CoolIT's paste it gives about 29.5/34.5 K (synthesis HMMC-R same-paste 30.0/35.0 K, minus ~0.5 K for the 0.8 mm base). The scorecard's 'conservative' column should use one of these, not LM end-of-life.

Height and mass 'probably no better, CoolIT undisclosed': the evidence base puts CoolIT at ~10-13 mm thick (bar 12-15 mm proud). D2D-15 at 21-25 mm is about 2x taller, and 2.3 kg is about 1.5x a ~1.2-1.6 kg plate of CoolIT's construction. This is a measured loss, not an unknown.

Integrated screen '50 um absolute, >= 12 cm2, clean 0.4 kPa': fouling-filtration rule 3 requires pore count >= 100x the channel-inlet count. At 0.15 mm there are 23,364 inlets, so >= 2.3e6 pores are needed; 12 cm2 of 50 um mesh has about 1.6e5 (7x). Scaling the report's 5 cm2 case gives about 30 days to 50 % blockage at 1e-4/mL of particles above 50 um, and about 20 kPa dP at 50 % blocked, which would roughly quadruple plate dP. The fix is >= 150-170 cm2 of pleated media, or a tray/rack cartridge plus <= 50 um absolute CDU filtration.

Diffusion bond '850-950 C, 5-10 MPa, 50-200 plates per 8-12 h cycle': fin-tip contact stress would be 25-50 MPa. A workable window is <= 1-2 MPa effective at the fin tips, or 600-800 C (50-75 % Tm), or a TLP/braze route. Realistic batch size for pressure-controlled bonding of 21-25 mm tall parts is about 10-40 per cycle, so 2-3x the furnace count or capex (US$6-15M rather than US$3-6M) for 100k/yr.

Engine yield/overhead of 12 % at 100k: for a first-of-kind tip-bonded fin sandwich with a fly-cut 0.8 mm pedestal and Ni over a stepped face, 20-30 % is the realistic figure in the first two years. That moves the D2D-RU factory cost from ~US$175 to ~US$200-230, and D2D-15 from ~US$225 to ~US$260-290, i.e. +90-175 % over the ~US$105 skived incumbent.

Die load '0.04-0.10 MPa over 34 cm2 of logic': a liquid TIM cannot hold a 30 um film under static clamp. Squeeze-out takes milliseconds to seconds at ~2 mPa s, so the 140-340 N is carried at the high-point contacts between the Ni pedestal and bare Si. With die-height mismatch of +/-10-25 um across four dies, local stress can exceed the ~0.3 MPa die-crack guideline many times over unless gap-setting stops carry the static load.

LM reliability scope: the qualification table covers only the 20-40 um gap change. The TIM report gives Cu-on-Si shear strain of 0.9-1.65 per 55 K cycle at 25 um bond line for 60-108 mm spans; for 120-150 mm CoWoS-L at 30 um it is about 1.5-2. This lateral pumping term is missing from the risk table and the test plan.

Split-Flow FTO 'single central inlet slot, ~Aug 2028': the gap FTO report bounds expiry at Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031 (patent term adjustment) via continuation '513, and says that adding inlet slots is not by itself a design-around for continuous skived channels with between-end inlets.
'UQD12-class' coupling: not confirmed to exist in OCP UQD v2.0.0 (gap-hydraulic report). Specify a 3/4-in-class coupling or dual UQD08 pairs (15-28 kPa) instead.

B300 listed as a lidded Tier 1 package: the envelope report gives B200/B300 as bare die with a stiffener. The lidded market is Rubin and MI455X, and 3A-fallback (PCM on die) is already Blackwell practice, not a new product.
3A qualified for a hyperscaler ASIC at M15-18: with 2,000-cycle LM data arriving at M12-15 and a module-owner JEDEC TC/PC/HAST plan taking 6-9 months after DVT hardware, 24-36 months is realistic.

direct-to-die.lens: strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The model (d2d_run.out, consistent with SYNTHESIS-physics) gives 22.3/24.4 K against 34.4/44.2 K. But the 3A tier itself adds only 0.6 K over Tier 2 on a ceramic TTV, and the headline compares liquid metal against CoolIT's paste. The OCP spec measures R with a recommended TIM (probably PCM). On that basis the claim falls to about 28/31 K versus about 32.6/40.4 K for a CoolIT-like plate re-tested with PCM: -14% avg / -23% max, not -35% / -45%.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: At the junction this is the strongest external-plate path: 64 K versus 86 K for lidded LM on the same engine, and 3A-P reaches Tj of about 101 C. But the 139 K CoolIT comparator is a lidded-paste strawman, and 350 W/cm2 die-average is a 2029+ case, not Rubin Ultra (~87 W/cm2 per the gap-nvidia report). At realistic 87-117 W/cm2, LM gains only about 4-5 K over PCM on die. On the lidded Rubin 2.3 kW plate-level framing, the average is no better than split-flow (16.7 and 18.4 K versus 16.1 K).

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: It inherits the corrected design-H manifold: 5.7 kPa with the screen, 1.7 W, global max/min 1.10, and an honest statement that quick disconnects dominate the loop (UQD12 spec). Two deductions. The orifice comb sits at the bottom of the slot, about 2 mm above the fin tips, whereas the physics rule puts it at the slot top so the jets decay; that brings jet-footprint non-uniformity and JetCool adjacency. And the 36 LPM rows break the proposal's own 1.5 m/s velocity cap.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length does not depend on package size, Q-cap is 30.8 kW (R core) and 38.9 kW (P core) at Tcase 85 C, and tiling to wafer scale with per-tile floats is credible. Against that: 30 kW+ at 1.2 LPM/kW needs ports of about 23 mm (or it breaks the velocity rules). LM containment over 100-150 mm warping CoWoS-L is unproven. The real height of about 30 mm hurts dense blades such as Kyber.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Diffusion-bonding 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins at 850-950 C / 5-10 MPa puts roughly 25-50 MPa on the bonded fin tips (about 20% contact area), well above the flow stress of annealed Cu at that temperature, so fin creep or buckling is a first-order yield risk the proposal does not rank. The braze fallback risks filler wicking into 0.15 mm gaps. Fly-cutting a 0.8 mm crowned pedestal over a fin field, per-SKU warpage metrology, and Ni-pinhole control add further steps. Factory cost of $175-225 is about 1.7-2x a skived plate.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Fouling handling is good: an integrated 50 um absolute screen and a 0.15 mm floor. The lead tier, though, is not drop-in (it needs lidless silicon). It rests on LM containment over 80-100 cm2 under cyclic warpage, for which no public data exist, and which the proposal itself rates high-likelihood and product-defining. It makes the plate vendor the de facto TIM1 owner, with die-warranty exposure on $30-50k packages, and it imposes a 5-year LM inspection and depot FRU model that is worse than paste for serviceability.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The core engine sits on expired art (Harpole, Cooligy, Walpole). The IP section, however, is stale against our own gap-splitflow report, which shows 'avoid a single central slot' is not a design-around under 'comprising' claims and puts expiry at Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031. It omits the live Mikros/Jabil diffusion-bonded laminate families and does not flag the heat-map-dense orifice jets as JetCool/PKU-adjacent. It contradicts itself by listing micro-channel-lid constructions (Intel liquid-cooled IHS, Jentech, Nvidia) under 'avoid' while selling 3B. Its own claims are weak: dam-contained LM has prior art (Sony PS5 2020 UV-resin seal patent, RTX 5090 FE), stepped pedestals are routine in bare-die plates, and process-family claims cannot be policed.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The lead product depends on two gates the company does not control: lidless package access, and module-owner qualification of a third-party LM as TIM1. Nvidia is moving to lids (Rubin gold-plated lid) and micro-channel lids (Rubin Ultra/Feynman via Jentech), not to bare die. 'Qualified at M15-18' is optimistic; realistic first 3A revenue is 2029, just as TSMC IMC-Si and in-die microfluidics arrive. In practice, Tier 1/2 is the product that ships.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: Breadth across AI data-centre packages is real: lidded, bare-die, micro-channel-lid component, manifold caps for silicon coolers, switch ASICs, wafer-scale, plus RF/laser niches with high margin. The power-electronics row conflicts with our own power-electronics report. 0.2 mm gaps and bare copper in Al/Si-OAT WEG loops are non-starters there (features of at least 0.3-0.5 mm are needed). Direct-to-substrate sintering requires the module vendor, and 'EV is a licensing play' is not a business model.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: Unusually candid. The 'where DD3 does not win' section, Monte Carlo bands, provenance tags, and admissions on height, mass, serviceability and in-die leapfrogging are all to its credit. Offsetting that: the scorecard puts LM against paste rather than the OCP-recommended TIM, the junction comparator is lidded paste rather than a bare-die PCM split-flow plate, the 21-25 mm height contradicts its own header dimensions and the physics synthesis (~30 mm), and costs are KB-M/L.

fatal_flaws: The lead differentiator is a package decision, not a plate invention. Removing the lid and TIM1 (the 21-33 K junction gain over lidded options) is open to any plate vendor once the silicon vendor ships lidless parts. CoolIT's brief names 'direct-to-die and micro-channel lids' as its next step, and Frore already pitches delidded Rubin. Against CoolIT this cannot be defended as the architecture's own win. The plate-attributable gain is the engine/zoning (~28 K at 350 W/cm2) plus LM (~14 K), and the engine is shared with every HMMC proposal.

Under the OCP Cold Plate Test Spec v1.0.0 (authored by CoolIT, R measured with a recommended, probably PCM, TIM), the 3A tier cannot be seen on a TTV: 0.6 K versus Tier 2. The LM-versus-paste headline (-35% / -45%) will be rejected as apples-to-oranges. The defensible OCP-format claim is about 28/31 K versus about 32.6/40.4 K for CoolIT re-tested with the same PCM.

The mission requires a win in every measurable aspect, and DD3 does not deliver one. By its own account it loses or merely ties on height (21-25 mm claimed, ~30 mm realistic) and mass (2.3 kg), on serviceability (LM depot FRU versus field paste), on factory cost (~1.7-2x skived), and on average dT on large low-flux lidded footprints (Rubin plate-level 16.7-18.4 K versus 16.1 K).

The lead product may have no customer. Nvidia's 2026-28 path is lidded (Rubin gold-plated lid), then micro-channel lid (Jentech). Bare-die hyperscaler ASICs run at 80-110 W/cm2, where LM buys only ~4 K over today's PCM-on-die, too little to accept a third-party LM as de facto TIM1. By the time high-flux bare-die silicon exists (2029+), TSMC IMC-Si and in-die microfluidics compete for the same socket.

TIM1 liability: the plate supplier becomes the owner of the interface that sets Tj on $30-50k packages. A fleet-level LM migration or short event, in a mode with no public reliability data at 80-100 cm2 under cyclic warpage, creates indemnity exposure a plate company cannot carry. 'Insurance/indemnity cap' is not a mitigation module owners will accept.

As written, the IP posture cannot be defended. The Split-Flow design-around ('no single central slot') is insufficient against open-ended claims; the window runs to as late as mid-2031, and DD3's 14 centre-fed slots splitting flow both ways over continuous skived fins need the segmented-fin / interior-outlet design-ins from the gap report. 3B practises the micro-channel-lid constructions the proposal lists under 'avoid'. Mikros/Jabil diffusion-bonded laminate families are not screened.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: One bonded engine whose tier is set only by post-bond face finishing: lapped Cu for PCM, 3-5 um electrolytic Ni for LM on the lid, and a stepped pedestal for bare die. One wetted-side qualification, one furnace, one product line.

Treat LM containment as a designed subsystem, not a recipe: FKM perimeter dam, capture moat, Ni or W barrier, conformal coat on passives within 5 mm, hard stops through the stiffener. Ship it as a factory pre-wetted, capped, nitrogen-packed FRU so the interface becomes a part number rather than a field process.

A pedestal crowned to the hot-state shadow-moire shape of each package SKU, plus a load-limited kinematic float (6-15 psi on the dies) with HBM never bearing load (at least 30 um gap, LM or putty filled).
Electrolytic sulfamate Ni 3-5 um with no Au and never high-P electroless Ni on the heat path (t/k <= 0.001 cm2K/W). Sputtered W as a long-life barrier option.
An integrated, serviceable 50 um absolute pleated screen with dP-signature alarm at 3x clean, plus a 100% end-of-line dP signature test (5.3 +/- 0.6 kPa) as a production gate.

A separable manifold cap (headers, heat-map comb, screen, ports) positioned as the fluid-delivery layer for micro-channel lids and silicon micro-coolers, together with an OCP 'liquid-cooled package interface' proposal. This keeps the company relevant after 2029 and makes it a standards play rather than a fight over in-die IP.

TTV-C: real-silicon thermal test dies with diode sensors, tiled 4x on a warping 120 mm substrate with HBM dummies and a stiffener, plus an independent-lab repeat. It is the only credible way to prove any junction-level claim to an OEM.
A junction-level KPI: maximum die flux at Tj <= 105 C with 45 C inlet. It is a cleaner OEM-facing metric than case-to-inlet on a ceramic TTV.
Hyperscaler custom ASICs, where the buyer owns both package and plate, as the first co-design socket, with a Group-A licence or manufacturing partnership as the route to Nvidia volume.
Gallium supply hedge: about 2 g per plate, non-Chinese and recycled Ga, 12-month stock, Galinstan for cold storage, and a PCM fallback that keeps the product alive.
numbers_disputed: Junction comparator '139 K CoolIT-like' (lidded paste): the fair comparator for a bare-die socket is a split-flow plate on bare die with PCM, which Group-A ships today for B200-class parts (Lenovo docs). Subtracting lid plus In TIM1 (~0.079 cm2K/W, ~28 K at 350 W/cm2, per tim-and-direct-to-die) and paste-to-PCM (~5 K) gives about 106 K, not 139 K. The fair gain is 106 -> 64 K. Correspondingly, CoolIT's allowable die flux at Tj <= 105 C is about 175 W/cm2, not 129, so the ratio is about 1.85x, not 2.5x.

Headline benchmark -35% avg / -45% max: under the OCP-recommended TIM (PCM-class), DD3 gives 28.0/31.1 K (Tier 1) or 27.4/30.4 K (3A on heater). CoolIT-like re-tested with PCM gives 34.5-1.9 = 32.6 K avg and 44.3-1.9-2.0 (scatter 3.5 -> 1.5 K) = 40.4 K max. That is -14% / -23%.

Plate height 21-25 mm: the two-level centre-fed/centre-collected headers (10x15 and 14x20 mm) have to cross every 8 mm-deep slot, so they sit above the slots. That alone needs about 22 mm of manifold block, against the 13 mm claimed. With fins, grate, plenum, comb and cover the total is about 28-32 mm, consistent with SYNTHESIS-physics ('plate ~30 mm thick').

Relevance of 350 W/cm2 die-average: per gap-nvidia-rubin, Rubin Ultra is ~87 W/cm2 die-average and Rubin 2.3 kW ~117 W/cm2. At those fluxes LM versus PCM on die is worth only 0.04 cm2K/W x 117 W/cm2 = ~4.6 K, so the 'decisive' 3A gain at the 2027-28 commercial socket is about 5 K over the 3A PCM fallback, not 21-33 K.

Split-Flow expiry '~Aug 2028': gap-splitflow bounds it at Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031 depending on the '330 patent term adjustment, with '284 and '513 terminally disclaimed. 'Avoid a single central slot' is not a sufficient design-around under 'comprising' claims.

36 LPM operating rows (2x flow, and the Q-cap of 30.8 kW at 1.2 LPM/kW = 37 LPM): 16 mm ports run at 2.98 m/s and 20 mm ports at 1.91 m/s, both above the proposal's own 1.5 m/s cap. Ports of about 23 mm are needed, which grows the envelope, and the comb holes reach ~2.4 m/s, so Cu erosion needs checking.

Factory cost ~$175 (D2D-RU at 100k/yr): this assumes 50-200 plates per diffusion-bond cycle with no fin collapse. Bonding at 5-10 MPa nominal on ~20% fin-tip contact gives ~25-50 MPa local, against single-digit-MPa flow stress for OFE Cu at 900 C. Expect lower bond pressure and longer cycles, or braze. A realistic factory cost is $200-260 until bond coupons prove otherwise, against $105 for skived.

'CoolIT's 34.4 K reproduced at 0.55 LPM/kW (54% less flow)': at that flow the outlet rise is 27.6 K (72.6 C outlet), which breaks Nvidia's 65 C return limit. The usable floor is 0.75 LPM/kW, giving 28.1/30.2 K at 2.3 kPa, so the honest flow saving is about 38%, not 54%.

Power-electronics 'de-rated engine, 0.2 mm gaps, WEG 50/50': our power-electronics report sets features of at least 0.3-0.5 mm for WEG/aluminium loops and flags bare Cu as incompatible with Si-OAT aluminium chemistry. A 0.2 mm Cu core is not deployable in EV or charger loops without a separate Al-compatible, at least 0.5 mm SKU.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: I re-ran jet_hybrid_model.py and got the stated 26.9/29.9 K (PCM). The model imports the programme coldplate_model unchanged, uses the isothermal caloric and the 117 cm2 calibration. After correcting the descent-region continuity error, h_eff falls to 137-142 kW/m2K and the result is 27.1-27.4 / 30.1-30.4 K. That is still about -20 % avg and -31 % max against CoolIT, but the jet adds only 0.6-0.9 K over HMMC-R, and with CoolIT's paste the P90 average (35.5 K) does not beat 34.4 K.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: At 350 W/cm2 the zoned plate is far better than split-flow, but the robust core reaches only 88 C with liquid metal at 6 mm pitch. The 84.5 C figure needs a 4 mm die pitch whose galleries are not sized and break the proposal's own velocity rules, plus a 0.8 mm base, and correcting continuity and caloric puts it at 85.0-85.7 C before any maldistribution. At 2-4 kW the jets add 0.6-1.3 K, JH is about 2 K worse than CoolIT-like on the average for uniform GPU footprints, and with paste it loses to CoolIT's 4 kW plate (0.0093 vs <0.009 C/W).

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: The plate dP is the right order, couplings are handled honestly (UQD08 ~25 kPa vs UQD12 ~5 kPa), and the inertial nozzle's branch/head ratio of 6.4 meets the U/CC rule. However, the nozzle loss is modelled as about 1.2 jet heads (equivalent Cd ~0.9), while section A of the same model uses 2.78 heads. A realistic Cd of 0.65-0.75 gives 2.4-3.1 kPa at the nozzle and 6.2-6.9 kPa for the plate, which removes the 'same dP as HMMC, +15 % h' premise. Die-zone galleries run at 0.66-0.8 m/s, giving slot-entry ratios of 6.5-9.7 against the >= 15 rule.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Parallel cells and per-die artwork scale in area, and dP does not depend on size. At 30 kW and 1.2 LPM/kW, Vj reaches 3.1 m/s, above the proposal's own erosion cap, so the nozzles must open up and the jet increment, the reason for the architecture, mostly disappears. Plate dP is ~24-27 kPa at 36 LPM with 16 mm ports, Q capacity is 22.9 kW (PCM) or 32 kW (liquid metal), and the height is understated.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Every step is conventional, but nobody has yet shown a five-layer, one-cycle diffusion bond onto 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins. At 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa gross, the fin tips (40 % area) carry ~12-25 MPa, above annealed Cu flow stress at that temperature, so fin creep and slot narrowing are likely. The 0.22 mm slots in a 0.20 mm PCE foil sit at the process limit, and the electroless-Ni erosion fallback does not fit a Cu-Cu bond sequence. The ~US$180 at 100k (1.8x a skived plate) assumes an optimistic US$32 bond cycle for 148 x 152 mm parts that each need 110-225 kN of press load.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: It has the same 0.15 mm channel and 50 um screen as HMMC-R, a leak-before-break laminate, OCP-format qualification and a dP-signature alarm. But the jets move the core from the fouling report's no-impaction regime (St ~0.2) to St 1-7 for JH-R and ~11 for JH-X, which is the mechanism that report used to disqualify fine channels. The inherited 10-year life and JH-X's 2.3x life are therefore unsupported until E3. The jet speed of 1.55-1.94 m/s also already exceeds the 1.5 m/s Cu guidance the proposal cites.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The JetCool design-around (sealed plate, parallel rather than staged jets) is reasonable. But the plate keeps continuous fins with interior split flow, against the FTO report's segmented-fin advice, so Split-Flow exposure runs to 2028-31 and the trench fallback costs h. Frore's power-mapped 'short-loop jet channels' are the closest overlap, and its 2023-early-2025 filings should be published by now, yet the proposal calls them unpublished. Its own claims are thin against Sung & Mudawar, Cooligy US 7,104,312 and the sibling HMMC comb claim.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The plan reaches a qualified product at M15-18, with a cheap kill-or-confirm coupon (E1) and an HMMC comb fallback that fits the same block. Against that, several unknowns stack: the size of the jet increment, a 3,000 h erosion test, impaction fouling and the fin-tip diffusion bond. Nvidia's centralised Group-A purchasing still gates the main socket.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: It is strong for AI-DC test vehicles and multi-reticle zoning. At GPU scale the value shrinks to zoning, and the proposal admits jets bring nothing to 800 VDC shelves. The SiC claim of a 2-4x cold-start dP rise is understated: in 50/50 WEG at -40 C, Re_slot falls ~50x to ~10, so the realistic rise is ~5-10x. Laser-diode and RF niches are plausible.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: The proposal is unusually candid. It reuses the model unchanged, runs a Monte Carlo, lists where it does not win and which claims to avoid, and corrects its own earlier Martin and Womac errors. But it repeats a continuity error of the same class in the descent region, treats the nozzle Cd inconsistently, gives a 17.8 mm stack that cannot hold its own galleries and troughs, and states impaction-fouling and cold-start figures it has not tested.

fatal_flaws: Nothing kills the architecture outright. Because the jet increment is only ~1 K, the worst case falls back to HMMC-R performance (28/31 K with PCM), which still beats CoolIT. The jet-specific headline claims, however, are not defensible as written.

The JH-X claim that the screen-free SKU still beats CoolIT on every thermal metric is indefensible. With the descent region corrected for continuity, h_eff is 74-80 kW/m2K, not 88. That gives 33.5-34.8 K average with PCM and 35.4-36.7 K with paste, so it loses like-for-like and at P90. Its 2.3x fouling-life claim also ignores St ~11 impaction of 90 um particles at 1.57 m/s.

The claim that the robust core reaches <= 85 C at 350 W/cm2 (84.5 C) rests on a 4 mm die-pitch gallery network that is never sized. At 7 mm depth, 1.3 mm galleries run ~0.8 m/s with a slot-entry ratio of ~6.5 against the >= 15 rule, and the 'etched gallery laminate' alternative would be shallower and worse. Corrected h_eff and caloric already give 85.0-85.7 C before any along-gallery maldistribution, which would add roughly 1 K more.

The 17.8 mm stack is geometrically infeasible. An 11.5 mm block cannot hold 7.0/8.4 mm galleries milled from below plus the ~6 mm-deep troughs needed for 200/300 mm2 at 0.78/0.52 m/s. With only 2.4-3.8 mm of depth left, the troughs would have to be 53+79 mm wide, which does not fit the 108 mm field. A realistic height is ~20-21.5 mm, with no gain over HMMC-elite.

The jets reintroduce inertial impaction (St 6.9 for 50 um Cu oxide at the 0.15 mm gaps), the mechanism the fouling report used to rule out fine channels. Particles collect at the zero-shear stagnation lines under every nozzle row. The claimed 10-year life (0.6-1.2x a skived plate) is borrowed from a low-St HMMC analysis and is unsupported until E3 runs.

The joining route is an unquantified, potentially programme-stopping risk. A one-cycle diffusion bond at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa gross puts ~12-25 MPa on 0.10 mm fin tips, above annealed copper's flow stress at that temperature, so fins can creep or crush and nozzle slots can narrow. Braze is excluded near the 0.22 mm nozzles, so no fallback join is defined, and the electroless-Ni erosion fallback does not fit a Cu-Cu diffusion bond.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Move the metering orifice the HMMC needs anyway down to the fin tips as an etched slot-nozzle foil (N1) bonded to the fins. One part then meters the flow, ties base to manifold, and carries the power-map zoning, and it replaces the comb, plenum and grate layers.

N1/N2 nozzle-tie laminate with a stiffener foil: the internal foils sit inside the pressure envelope, so a foil failure cannot leak externally (leak-before-break), and N2 drops N1 stress over 3 mm galleries from ~216 MPa to 21-27 MPa.

Zoning programmed by phototool artwork: nozzle open area follows the power map, every zone is fed in parallel from shared centre-line headers, and HBM gets upstream-metered open slots, so no fluid crosses a die before an HBM.
A hierarchy of passage widths (port > trough > gallery > window > nozzle > channel), each stage wider than the next, so the metering element never becomes the sieve.

E1, a single-cell coupon with swappable N1 foils (open slot, jet, trench) that measures the h_eff increment for ~US$50k before any tooling. It is the cheapest way to settle the jet-vs-manifold question.
Practice for the jet SKU: a jet-velocity cap tied to an erosion test matrix (E3), a 100 % flow/dP signature on every plate, and a plate-dP rise used as the fouling and screen alarm.
Scorecard discipline: like-for-like paste rows, Monte Carlo P90 conservative column, an explicit 'where it does not win' list and a 'claims to avoid externally' list.
numbers_disputed: JH-R h_eff 147 kW/m2K: I estimate 137-142. The model applies descent velocity (Vj+u_ch)/2 = 0.82 m/s over x1 = 1.11 mm per half-cell, which needs ~2.7x the jet's actual flow (0.11 mm column at 1.55 m/s). I re-ran a root-weighted 1-D fin with enhancement only on the jet column plus the bottom 0.3-0.5 mm of the turn region. TTV with PCM becomes 27.1-27.4 / 30.1-30.4 K (claimed 26.9/29.9), and the gain over HMMC-R is 0.6-0.9 K, not 1.1-1.3 K.
JH-X h_eff 88 kW/m2K: I estimate 74-80 by the same correction. Average with PCM is 33.5-34.8 K (claimed 32.2), with paste 35.4-36.7 K (claimed 34.1), and Q capacity is 16-17 kW (claimed 17.9).

Nozzle dP 1.76 kPa: I estimate 2.4-3.1 kPa. Applying Cd 0.65-0.75 to the 0.22 x 0.15 mm slot-into-gap opening at 1.55 m/s gives 1/Cd^2 = 1.8-2.4 heads, against the 1.2 heads the model uses (its own section A uses 2.78). Plate dP at 18 LPM becomes 6.2-6.9 kPa (claimed 5.5), and at 36 LPM with 16 mm ports ~24-27 kPa (claimed 21.7). This erodes the 'same dP as HMMC-R' and equal-pumping-power gains.

Plate height 17.8 mm: I estimate ~20-21.5 mm. The block needs 8.4 mm of outlet gallery, 0.7 mm floor and ~6 mm of trough, about 15.1 mm, not 11.5. The LP15 figure of 14.5 mm is unsupported for the same reason.

Die-zone gallery velocity <= 0.52 m/s: I estimate 0.66 m/s at 6 mm pitch (11 centre-fed 2.3 x 7 mm galleries carrying 14 LPM over a 66 mm die block) and ~0.8 m/s at 4 mm pitch (1.3 mm galleries). That gives slot-entry branch ratios of 9.7 and 6.5, below the >= 15 rule from manifold-maldistribution.md.

350 W/cm2 hottest die, T_case,max 84.5 C (4 mm pitch, 0.8 mm base, liquid metal): I estimate 85.0-85.7 C after the continuity correction and an isothermal caloric shift of +0.15-0.2 K. With ~1 K more from the ratio-6.5 gallery maldistribution it reaches ~86-87 C, which misses 85 C. The 6 mm case is 88.7-89.1 C (claimed 88.0).

Hot-die caloric is held at 6.7 K for every h_eff. The isothermal formula adds +0.1-0.35 K as h rises from 127 to 158-216 kW/m2K. This is small but runs against the jet's favour, and the proposal itself cites the rule.

JH-R relative fouling life 0.6-1.2x (10 years): unsupported. The jet gives St = 6.9 for 50 um Cu oxide, while the fouling report's 0.15 mm floor was set for St ~0.2 at 0.05-0.08 m/s. JH-X life 2.3x is likewise unsupported, at St ~11 for 90 um particles at 1.57 m/s in 0.30 mm gaps.
SiC cold-start dP rise of 2-4x: I estimate ~5-10x. In 50/50 WEG Re_slot falls from ~590 at 65 C to ~10 at -40 C, the nozzle loss becomes viscous (~3x), and the ~11 % viscous share grows ~50x.

Jet velocity at the rated 1.5 LPM/kW is 1.94 m/s, and nominal is 1.55 m/s. Both exceed the 1.5 m/s copper erosion-corrosion guidance the proposal itself cites, and impingement at a stagnation corner is harsher than pipe flow.

Diffusion-bond cost of US$32 per plate at 100k: likely optimistic, though this is less certain. Each 148 x 152 mm part needs 110-225 kN at 5-10 MPa, which limits batch size per press. The furnace-batch figures quoted come from etched laminates with large land fractions, not from skived fin fields.

jet-hybrid.lens: Manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility: process chain at volume, yields and tolerances, cost basis, fouling and filtration, materials (OCP/ASHRAE/Nvidia), burst and proof, service life, height and mass fit, qualification burden

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: With a PCM pad it reaches 26.9/29.9 K (P90 30.3/33.4) against 34.4/44.2 K, so it clearly beats CoolIT on the average and the maximum. The gain over the HMMC-R reference is only about 1 K, which is inside the model's own uncertainty band. The proposal admits that with CoolIT's paste the P90 average (35.5 K) does not beat the benchmark.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: At the hot die the result is 88 C with liquid metal at 6 mm pitch. Reaching 85 C needs the 4 mm pitch, which adds an etched gallery laminate, plus a 0.8 mm base. On 1.4-3.6 kW plates the jets run at only 0.6-0.8 m/s and gain 0.6-1.3 K, and against CoolIT's 4 kW plate the paste version loses (0.0093 vs <0.009 C/W). The floor stagnation term assumes the jet reaches the base undecayed after a 2 mm descent inside a 0.15 mm gap.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: The plate dP of 5.5 kPa and the inertial nozzle metering (branch/head 6.4) are credible, and it honestly states that UQD08 couplings cost about 25 kPa and that the 15 kW class needs UQD12. However, uniformity now depends on nozzle-width tolerance and on creep during bonding. PCE holds ±25 µm, not the ±15 µm claimed, which is ±11 % local flow. The 91 % die-zone flow split cannot be checked by a global flow-signature test.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Because every cell is fed in parallel, dP does not depend on size. But for a given artwork the 1.94 m/s erosion cap limits flow to about 22.5 LPM per 117 cm2. Higher power therefore needs new artwork, or the jets fall back to plain HMMC behaviour. The bonding press force (113-225 kN per 225 cm2 at 5-10 MPa), the skive blade width and the plate mass (~4 kg for wafer-scale plates) all scale badly.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Skiving, PCE, CNC and vacuum hot presses each exist at volume. Diffusion-bonding a 0.2 mm nozzle foil to 85 % of the tips of 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins in one cycle has no volume precedent. At 5-10 MPa the fin tips (40 % of the area) see 12.5-25 MPa at about 0.87 Tm, enough to make them creep. Under the 3 mm galleries the foil stack can pass on only about 1-2 MPa. The process chain also has no fin-tip planarisation or deburr step. My corrected factory cost is about US$215-240 at 100k, not US$180, because of the 2026 copper price and a probable two-step bond.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The nominal jet velocity of 1.55 m/s already sits at the 1.5 m/s copper limit that CoolIT is still testing, and a soak at 1.5x rated flow puts it at 2.33 m/s. The proposed electroless-Ni fallback cannot go through the 850-950 C bond: the Ni-P eutectic is about 880 C. Plating after bonding through 0.22 mm nozzles into 0.15 mm gaps covers poorly. The '+2 kPa screen alarm' cannot be seen inside a tray carrying 50-100 kPa of loop dP, and each plate carries its own debris-trapping screen. Pressure ratings (MAWP 1.0 / burst 3.0 MPa) and leak-before-break are sound, but the 2.1 kg mass and the new jet failure modes add to the qualification burden.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The JetCool open-cavity and series re-impingement claims are designed around sensibly. However, every nozzle is a split-flow inlet across continuous fins, so the Split-Flow risk (to 2028-31) applies as it does to the HMMC; a trench fallback exists. Defensibility is weak: slot jets into microchannels are published prior art (Sung & Mudawar), as are normal-flow laminates (Valenzuela/Mikros) and Cooligy's hot-spot targeting. The proposed claims rest on a metering ratio and an artwork map.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The release target is M15-18 (Jan-Apr 2028), gated by an unproven one-cycle bonding window, furnace capex and lead time, a 3,000 h erosion test, and soaks of up to 5,000 h. The E1 coupon could remove the jet increment altogether, leaving an HMMC with a different metering foil (the fallback is good). Access to Nvidia's centralised Group-A purchasing remains unsolved.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: Inertial metering suits viscous cold starts in EV and SiC coolers, and targeted jets suit laser diodes and RF niches. The aluminium CAB variant, however, is essentially a separate product and process. On the 800 VDC shelf and on CPU, NIC and switch parts the jets add nothing by the proposal's own account.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: Unusually candid: it gives P90 values, says where it does not win, lists claims to avoid, and plans a kill/confirm coupon. Against that, the Q-capacity and equal-pumping-power numbers run the jets above its own velocity cap. The PCE tolerance and copper cost are more optimistic than the evidence base and the 2026 market. The one-cycle bond and the ENi fallback are asserted without a process-window check, and JetCool's vendor claims are used to sanity-check a geometry they do not cover.

fatal_flaws: Conditionally fatal: the bonding process window is unproven. The stated one-cycle vacuum diffusion bond (850-950 C, 5-10 MPa) puts 12.5-25 MPa on 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fin tips (40 % tip area fraction), above copper's roughly 10-15 MPa flow stress at about 0.87 Tm. That risks fin creep or barrelling that closes the 0.15 mm gaps, and creep narrowing of the 0.22 mm metering slots. Meanwhile, under the 3.0-3.4 mm L2 galleries (about 80 % of the fin field) the 0.8 mm N1+N2 stack can pass on only about 1-2 MPa before it yields at bond temperature, because its bending stress is about 8x the contact pressure. The likely result is stripes of unbonded tips. Oregon State microlamination work reports the same trade-off: pressure high enough to bond deforms the channels. If no window exists, the tied 1.0/0.8 mm base and the nozzle-tie laminate, which are the core of the concept, cannot be built at yield. At minimum, a two-step lower-pressure bond or a TLP/braze route must be demonstrated before tooling.

The jet differentiator may not survive erosion qualification. The nominal Vj of 1.55 m/s sits at the 1.5 m/s copper hot-water limit that CoolIT is still testing (2025 study, no results published). A long-duration soak at 1.5x rated flow runs the jets at 2.33 m/s. If E3 confirms about 1.5 m/s, the jets must be derated to about 1.0 m/s at 150 % flow, the increment collapses toward zero, and JH becomes an HMMC with a nozzle foil. The stated ENi wetted-path fallback is incompatible with the bond cycle (Ni-P eutectic about 880 C), and post-bond electroless Ni through 0.22 mm nozzles into 0.15 x 2 mm gaps has poor throwing power.

Several headline claims, as written, cannot be defended because they break the proposal's own velocity cap. Q capacity of 22.9 kW (PCM) and 32.3 kW (LM) at 1.2 LPM/kW needs 27.5 and 38.8 LPM, which means Vj of 2.38 and 3.35 m/s. The equal-pumping-power point (28.5 LPM) runs at 2.46 m/s. All of these exceed the 1.94 m/s continuous cap, and the LM point exceeds even the 3.1 m/s qualification-only point.

The core value, nozzle-programmed zoning with 91 % of flow to the dies, cannot be screened at 100 %. The production flow/dP signature measures only global dP, so local slot narrowing from bond creep or etch-factor differences between 0.42 mm die nozzles and 0.5 mm HBM orifices goes undetected. Per-zone verification needs TTV or IR testing of every plate, or sampling, which is not costed.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Use the nozzle foil as the only metering element: an inertial slot nozzle at the fin tips (branch/head of 6 or more) replaces the HMMC orifice comb, spends the unavoidable metering loss where it raises h at the fin roots, deletes a laminate and about 3 mm of height, and keeps uniformity independent of flow from 9 to 36 LPM.
Zone by phototool artwork: one etched foil carries the power map, so a customer-specific SKU costs a US$0.5-3k phototool and days of lead time, not new tooling.
Use a two-foil tie laminate (thin nozzle foil plus a 0.6 mm windowed stiffener): over a 3 mm gallery it cuts foil stress from 216 MPa to 21-27 MPa at burst. This is a reusable tie-chain design rule.
Keep passage widths monotonic from port to channel (16 > 6 > 3 > 1.0 > 0.22 > 0.15 mm) so the metering feature is never the sieve.
Offer the JH-X screen-free coarse-passage SKU (0.30 mm minimum passage, no integrated screen) for legacy and dirty loops, retrofits and edge sites.
Use the single-cell coupon with swappable foils (E1: open slot, jet, trench) as a roughly US$50k, three-month kill/confirm before any furnace tooling.
Give leak-before-break by construction: internal foils carry only internal dP and tie loads and are never part of the external pressure envelope.
Apply inertial metering to SiC and EV module coolers: cold-start dP rises an estimated 2-4x, against 50-80x for viscous micro-channels.
Adopt the explicit velocity-capped jet rule plus 'claims to avoid' discipline, and publish OCP v1.0.0 six-point R and dP data with an independent repeat.
numbers_disputed: Q capacity at T_case,max <= 85 C: claimed 22.9 kW (PCM) and 32.3 kW (LM) at 1.2 LPM/kW, which implies Vj 2.38 and 3.35 m/s. Holding flow at the 1.94 m/s continuous cap (22.5 LPM) and re-running jet_hybrid_model.plate_eval gives 21.9 kW (PCM), 28.3 kW (LM) and 19.0 kW (paste).

Equal-pumping-power (6.5 W) result of 23.2/26.2 K at 28.5 LPM: the jets run at 2.46 m/s, above the cap. The highest flow inside the cap is the 22 LPM point, 24.9/27.9 K at 8.6 kPa, so the 6.5 W claim should be labelled qualification-only.

N1 slot tolerance of ±15 µm (PCE), giving ±5-7 % local flow: manufacturing-cost.md gives ±25-50 µm for PCE and the HMMC-elite proposal uses ±25 µm. On a 0.22 mm slot, ±25 µm is ±11 % open area, which means ±11 % local flow for a nozzle-dominated branch, before etch-cusp Cd scatter and bond-creep narrowing. Holding ±10 µm needs green ps-laser cutting of N1 at an extra US$5-15 per plate, which the US$10 foil line does not include.

OFE copper at US$23-25 for 2.2 kg incl. swarf: LME cash was about US$14.4-14.7k/t in September 2026 (Cochilco 1 Sep, Westmetall 8 Sep), roughly US$17-19/kg as OFE mill product. Raw stock is about 4 kg (11.5 mm block blank ~2.3 kg, skive blank ~1.1 kg, cover 0.45 kg, foils ~0.3 kg after nesting). Net of swarf credit that is about US$45-55, i.e. US$20-30 more per plate.

Diffusion bond at US$32 per plate (100k/yr) in one cycle, with US$3-6 M capex for 2-3 furnaces: a two-step bond (foils to fins under a flat platen, then the block) is likely needed, adding US$15-25 per plate and roughly doubling furnace hours. At 5-10 MPa over 225 cm2 each plate needs 113-225 kN, so 50-200 plates per cycle requires multi-hundred-tonne large-platen vacuum hot presses at about US$2-5 M each. My corrected factory cost is about US$215-240 at 100k/yr, not US$180; it is still below the ~US$400 Group-A ASP.

Bond parameters of 850-950 C at 5-10 MPa: local fin-tip stress of 12.5-25 MPa exceeds copper's flow stress at about 0.87 Tm. A practicable nominal pressure on a 40 % tip-fraction fin field is about 1-3 MPa or a lower temperature, which lengthens cycles and lowers the tie fraction actually achieved below the assumed 85 %.

Continuous jet velocity limit '1.94 m/s at 1.5 LPM/kW': a long-duration soak at 1.5x rated flow (27 LPM), per the standards-reliability matrix, runs 2.33 m/s. That breaks the evidence base's rule of 1.5-2.0 m/s in copper passages at 150 % rated flow.

Floor stagnation h of 42 kW/m2K: it is computed for an undecayed plane jet at the base after a 2.0 mm descent (H/w_n about 9) inside a 0.15 mm gap. The viscous decay time h^2/(12 nu) is about 1.5 ms against a 1.3 ms transit, so the jet arrives at roughly half velocity, and since h scales as sqrt(V) the value is about 30 kW/m2K. Because the stagnation term is only about 5 of the 20 kW/m2K increment, h_eff drops only to about 143-145 kW/m2K. The increment is mostly developing flow on the fin walls, which an HMMC partly shares.

JH-X relative fouling life of '~2.3x (23 y vs 10 y)': W/d of 3.3 on a ~90 µm absolute loop sits at the 3x bridging threshold, not the 6x no-successive-deposition rule, so 'fouling-proof' and 23 years have no basis. Defensible claim: at least 1x a skived plate without a screen, to be proven by the ISO 4406 dosing test.

jet-hybrid.lens: strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: It clearly beats CoolIT at nominal: 26.9/29.9 K with PCM and 28.8/33.8 K like-for-like with paste, against 34.4/44.2 K. But the paste P90 average is 35.5 K, so the average win is not robust. About 1.9 K of the headline -22 % comes from swapping paste for PCM, not from the plate, and the jet's own gain over HMMC-R (about 1.1 K average) is inside the stated +/-25-30 % per-term model band.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: This is the best part of the jet story: 3-5 K better than an open-slot core at the hot die without 33 um filtration. Even so, the 6 mm design still misses 85 C at 88 C with liquid metal; only the 4 mm pitch plus 0.8 mm base gets there, at 84.5 C. At 1.4-3.6 kW GPU plates the jet gain is 0.6-1.3 K, and on the uniform footprint the plate is about 2 K worse than CoolIT-like on the average.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 5.5 kPa port-to-port with an inertial nozzle (branch/head 6.4), so uniformity does not depend on flow rate, is a real and testable advantage. Coupling realism is good: it states that UQD08 costs about 25 kPa and specifies UQD12-class couplings. One deduction: the 36 LPM point runs 3.1 m/s jets, which are not qualifiable until E3 passes.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Parallel tiled cells and photo-tool zoning scale well to multi-die and wafer-scale parts. But at 30 kW (36 LPM) the erosion cap and the metering ratio pull against each other: widening the nozzles to keep below about 2 m/s cuts nozzle dP and breaks the branch/head >= 6 rule. 30 kW at an 85 C case also needs liquid metal (median Q cap is 22.9 kW with PCM, 32 kW with LM).

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: A 5-layer vacuum diffusion bond that joins thin foils to 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fin tips is not a process the Group-A houses (AVC, Cooler Master, Delta, Jentech) run at volume, and furnace capacity is the gate. The US$180 at 100k/yr assumes 50-200 plates per 8-12 h cycle, which looks optimistic. Fin creep or collapse under 5-10 MPa at 850-950 C is not in the yield-risk list.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Several new failure modes are unqualified: Cu erosion at the stagnation lines (no public PG25 threshold; CoolIT itself is still studying it), particle impaction at Stokes numbers 1-7, and a fully annealed copper body (70 MPa yield) under mounting load. The 'capped' velocity is 1.94 m/s at rated maximum flow, above the 1.5 m/s guideline the proposal itself cites. Drop-in needs UQD12-class couplings, 17.8 mm height and 2.1 kg, plus an integrated screen that has to be serviced.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The headline feature (jets fed from inlet headers into micro-fin channels in a sealed micro cold plate) sits in live, uncharted claims. Microfabrica US 12,255,123 B2 (granted Mar 2025, priority Mar 2021, so to about 2042) claims a micro cold plate with a 'hybrid microjet and microchannel heat transfer array', and its 2016-priority parent family discloses 'integrated fin and microjet arrays'. The proposal also skips IBM's Parida jet-plate-on-channel-wall family, Penn State US 12,029,008, Mikros diffusion-bonded laminates and JetCool's sealed SmartPlate families. Its Frore design-around is a manufacturing-method distinction, not a structural one, and its own claims are weakened by IBM Parida, Sung & Mudawar, PKU 2025 and the Cooligy zoning art.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The roadmap releases in Jan-Apr 2028, which misses the Rubin Ultra design freeze, so the realistic first sockets are Feynman-era or hyperscaler ASIC programmes in 2028-29. The jet-specific gates (E1 increment, E3 3,000 h erosion and impaction, E4 bond mechanics) add risk HMMC does not carry. The HMMC-comb fallback in the same block is sound risk management.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: It is honest that jets add nothing on 800 VDC power shelves (gap-pad limited) or CPU/NIC plates. The SiC EV version is really a different aluminium CAB product sold by licence, against module-vendor pin-fin incumbents and 24-36 months of AQG 324. Laser diodes, RF GaN and directed energy are a genuine natural fit for point-targeted jets, and JH-X serves dirty loops.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: The thermal honesty is exemplary: Monte Carlo bands, corrections to its own draft, an explicit 'where it does not win' list, P90 failures stated, and a list of claims to avoid. Deductions: the jet increment rests on an unvalidated region-weighted model; the IP table claims 'USPTO records found this session' yet misses the most directly relevant live family; and 'velocity-capped' describes a rated point above the guideline it cites.

fatal_flaws: IP indefensibility of the core differentiator. Jets from inlet-fed nozzles impinging into a micro-fin channel array inside a sealed micro cold plate reads directly on the opening of claim 1 of Microfabrica US 12,255,123 B2. That patent was granted 18 Mar 2025 (application 17/699,049, provisional 18 Mar 2021, live to about 2042), and its claim 1 recites a micro cold plate with header/manifold inlet and outlet plus a 'hybrid microjet and microchannel heat transfer array' whose microjet structures direct fluid from the inlet onto the primary heat-exchange region. The parent family (US 9,953,899, 10,665,530, 10,957,624, 11,456,235; Apr 2016 priority, to about 2036) discloses 'integrated fin and microjet arrays'. None of these appear in the proposal's IP table, and the programme's own ip-landscape.md had flagged a 'jet-enhanced manifold (orifices impinging on fin roots)' as needing claim review before adoption. Until this is claim-charted and cleared, the headline architecture cannot be sold in the US without licence or injunction exposure.

The jet increment cannot be shown where the benchmark is measured. At the 15 kW TTV the gain over the programme's own HMMC-R (built on expired Harpole/Cooligy art) is 1.1 K average and 1.3 K at equal pumping power. That is inside the model's +/-25-30 % per-term band and below what an OCP-format test can separate (TC surface-extrapolation error 0.4-5 K; CoolIT's own 10 K plate-to-plate spread). The architecture therefore takes on the most crowded live IP space (JetCool/Flex, Frore, Microfabrica) plus new erosion and impaction risk for a TTV benefit an OEM cannot verify. Everything it shows against CoolIT at 15 kW is already delivered by HMMC-R.

The 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' claim fails on the proposal's own numbers. With paste the P90 average is 35.5 K against 34.4 K. Against CoolIT's 4 kW plate with paste it gives 0.0093 C/W against CoolIT's < 0.009. On the uniform-footprint GPU-class plates the average is about 2 K worse. Height and mass are not won, and cost is +US$75-80 over a skived plate. The headline -22 % / -32 % compares our PCM with CoolIT's paste. Under the OCP spec's single recommended TIM (probably PCM), CoolIT also drops about 1.9 K, so the plate-attributable win is about -17 % average.

There is no credible route to Nvidia volume. Rubin plates are bought centrally from Group-A (Jentech, AVC, Cooler Master, Delta) at about US$400 and capacity above 100k a month. A 5-layer vacuum diffusion bond those houses do not run cannot simply be licensed to them, and 2-3 furnaces (about 100k plates a year) are a rounding error against Group-A volumes. The proposed 'JH-X retrofit' channel barely exists, because plates are qualified as part of the server tray and are not field-swapped. That leaves hyperscaler ASIC programmes in 2028-29 as the only realistic entry, where the jet's roughly 1 K advantage over HMMC is not a selling point.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Put the metering restriction at the fin tips (nozzle-tie foil), so the inertial metering dP that a manifold plate pays anyway also raises h at the fin roots. Graft it as a die-zone-only option on HMMC once the Microfabrica / JetCool / Frore claim charts clear it; keep open slots elsewhere to limit the exposure.

Programmable zoning by photo-tool artwork: one etched foil's open-area map is the device power map, at US$0.5-3k tooling per artwork. This is a strong business lever for fast per-ASIC customisation in hyperscaler programmes, and it works equally for orifice-comb or slot-width zoning without jets.

The inertial branch rule: nozzle or orifice dP >= 6x the header dynamic head, so uniformity holds from 9 to 36 LPM. Pair it with a 100 % flow/dP signature test that serves as both factory QC and the field fouling alarm (+2 kPa = screen at 3x clean).

JH-X, a screen-free coarse SKU (0.30 mm minimum passage, every passage >= 3.3x the absolute filter rating) that still beats CoolIT on average, maximum and dP. It suits legacy or dirty loops, edge sites and power electronics, and the coarse-channel idea carries over to HMMC (the jet adds +45 % h_eff there, but an open-slot coarse core may already beat CoolIT on maximum and dP).
The N2 stiffener foil, which spreads tie loads over the galleries so internal foils see only internal dP. That gives leak-before-break by construction and lets thin metering foils survive burst.

Commercial disclosure discipline: a full OCP v1.0.0 report (6 flow points, dP at 45 C, named TIM, three plates plus an independent lab), an explicit 'claims to avoid' list, and an 'inlet temperature allowed for 85 C case' metric (55 C against about 41 C for CoolIT) as the TCO headline for dry-cooler and heat-reuse buyers.

E1 single-cell coupon with swappable foils (open slot / jet / trench) at about US$50k in months 1-3, as a cheap kill-or-confirm gate before tooling. Add E3 erosion and impaction testing in dosed PG25, which every plate with sub-mm orifices (including HMMC's 1.2 m/s orifice comb) needs anyway.
A velocity-capped, erosion-qualified rule written into the product spec, with electroless Ni on the wetted path as the fallback.
numbers_disputed: Diffusion-bond throughput and cost: the proposal assumes 50-200 plates per 8-12 h cycle, about US$32 per plate at 100k/yr, and a US$180 factory cost. Bonding a 148 x 152 mm plate at 5-10 MPa takes about 112-225 kN per plate column, and a graphite-fixtured vacuum hot-press cycle including heat-up and cool-down is typically 16-24 h. I estimate 20-60 plates per cycle and US$50-90 for the bond step, so factory cost is about US$200-240 at 100k/yr and the 2-3 furnace capex does not reach 100k/yr.

Bond pressure vs fin integrity: 5-10 MPa nominal on 0.10 mm fins at a 0.4 area fraction puts 12.5-25 MPa on the fin tips at 850-950 C, at or above the hot flow stress of annealed OFE copper (about 10-20 MPa), so expect creep collapse or buckling of the 2 mm fins and slot narrowing. Realistic fin-tip bonding pressure is about 1-3 MPa (or braze/TLP), which lowers the achievable bond fraction below the 85 % assumed in the 8.8 MPa tie-stress calculation.

'Velocity-capped' jets: 1.55 m/s nominal and 1.94 m/s at the rated 1.5 LPM/kW maximum, against the 1.5 m/s copper erosion guideline the proposal cites (standards-reliability.md gives 1.5-2.0 m/s continuous). The rated point is about 30 % above the guideline, so the qualifiable continuous maximum is about 1.2 LPM/kW until E3 passes, not 1.5.

The jet increment as a differentiator: -1.1 K average / -1.3 K at equal pumping power against HMMC-R. The convection term is 8.8 vs 10.1 K, and at +/-25 % per term (the proposal's own band) the difference is 1.3 +/- about 2.5 K, which is not statistically distinguishable from zero. It should be presented as 'parity with HMMC +/- 2 K at the TTV', not as decisive differentiator #1.

Plate-attributable win vs CoolIT: claimed -22 % average / -32 % maximum. CoolIT re-run on the same PCM loses about 1.9 K of TIM term and about 2 K of scatter, giving roughly 32.5 / 40 K. JH-R PCM at 26.9 / 29.9 K is then about -17 % average / -25 % maximum on a like-for-like OCP basis.

SiC EV cold-start dP: claimed about 2-4x at -40 C because the jets are inertial. 50/50 WEG viscosity rises about 50-60x from 65 C to -40 C, dropping slot Re from hundreds to about 2-6, where the orifice Cd falls (sqrt(Re) regime) and roughly doubles to quadruples the nozzle loss. The about 11 % viscous channel/return share and the galleries scale with the full viscosity ratio. Overall plate dP rises about 5-10x, not 2-4x.

Split-Flow timing: the roadmap says 'volume ramp 2H 2028, as Split-Flow expires'. The family's US expiry window is 11 Aug 2028 to about mid-2031 depending on the '330 PTA (gap-splitflow report), and the proposal's own IP table says so. A 2H 2028 US ramp therefore still needs the claim chart and opinion letter, especially because JH keeps continuous skived fins with multiple interior inlets ('comprising' / 'an' covers multiple inlets) rather than segmented fins.

JH-X relative fouling life: claimed about 2.3x a skived plate (23 years vs 10). The relative-life model does not include the jet-specific impaction and stagnation-line deposition mechanism the proposal itself identifies (St 6.9 for 50 um Cu oxide). Until E3, claim no more than about 1.0-1.5x.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The 28.0/31.1 K (PCM) and 30.0/35.0 K (same paste) figures reproduce the corrected model and the synthesis exactly. h 13.2 kW/m2K at Re 19 with entrance effects, eta 0.56, h_eff 127 kW/m2K, the isothermal caloric term (NTU 1.25 gives 7.6 K) and the 0.15 mm deployable gap are all right, and I re-derived each one. Two weaknesses: no footprint sensitivity is shown (at the 100 cm2 photogrammetric lower bound the same-paste margin falls to 0.9 K and Tier 1 rises to 31.3/34.5 K), and the 1.5 K flow hot spot is carried over from design H although the manifold geometry has changed.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The proposal is honest that the R core misses 85 C at 350 W/cm2 (107 C with PCM, 93 C with LM) and that the P core reaches 84.5 C only on 25 um loops, which leaves zero margin. On GPU-class lids Tier 1 loses the average by 1.3-3.2 K even against the CoolIT-like reconstruction. That reconstruction overpredicts CoolIT's real 4 kW plate by 15-24 K, so against real competitor hardware Tier 1 is at parity at best (25 cm2) and loses by about 5 K at the roughly 20 cm2 heated area the research inferred.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: This is the strongest part of the proposal.
