It gives an explicit Cv-based coupling, hose, fitting, TFM and orifice budget, a rack-manifold network with momentum coefficients (the U-beats-Z result is physically correct when momentum dominates), mixed-load balancing, and equal-power and flow-equivalence comparisons. Against that: the headline compares LoopCore on dual UQDB08 with CoolIT on a single UQD08 (65-80 kPa) when the same-coupling comparator is 36-40 kPa. The manifold was re-topologised (flat 29/43 mm troughs, comb at the slot bottom) without re-running the maldistribution model, and fixed orifices are static balancing, not 'self-balancing' or flow-capping.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: The field scales at a constant 4 mm flow length and zoning only needs new comb artwork, which is sound. But Tier 1 caps at 21.6 kW on 117 cm2, 30 kW needs LM or the filtration-gated P core, and at 36 LPM the tray loop is 99-115 kPa because of the couplings. The wafer-scale and multi-module claims are not analysed.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: The chain (skive, photo-etch, CNC, vacuum braze) is conventional, but the brazed stack has 5-6 layers and carries risk of Ag wicking into the 0.15 mm gaps and of fin-tip voids. The 0.7 mm x 8.4 mm Cu walls between slots are hard to CNC and not credibly forgeable. Plate cost is US$165 against roughly US$100-115 at 100k, the TFM adds US$120-200 per tray, and the plate weighs 2.2 kg; the costing itself is transparent.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The 0.15 mm floor, captive 50 um screens, filtration ladder, commissioning bypass and test plan follow the physics reports. Four problems remain. (1) The dP-signature fouling alarm cannot see channel films. (2) Reverse back-flush drives TFM and screen debris into the unscreened outlet side of the channels. (3) A 2.5 mm cover over the 29/43 mm troughs fails 1.5 MPa proof unless posts are added, and the burst analysis ignores this. (4) Dual UQDB08 pairs plus a bulkhead TFM are not drop-in for MGX/NVL trays, and the warm-water operating points exceed the 65 C return/coupling limit.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: Building on expired Harpole/Cooligy art and keeping sensors out of the plate are sensible. However, continuous skived fins fed by interior slots read squarely on the open-ended Split-Flow claim to 2028-31 (acknowledged, still unresolved), and the TFM against NVIDIA's intelligent-plate filings is an open gate. The 'no impingement' distinction from microjet patents is physically false (L/d 3 at Re ~480), and the proposed provisionals (balancing orifices, factory dP signature, strainers plus flushing protocol) are close to standard hydronic practice, so defensibility is weak.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: A 12-18 month plate programme is plausible, and E1-E5 are well chosen and cheap (the E1 rig is under US$40k). But the platform value depends on tray, rack-manifold (2.5 in), CDU-class and BMC/Redfish changes that NVIDIA, ODMs and hyperscalers control, with Group-A centralised purchasing in the way. That multiplies adoption risk well beyond a drop-in plate.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family covers GPU, CPU, switch, VPD and VR skirt, and the keyed-orifice idea that lets 800 VDC power-shelf branches share a GPU manifold is genuinely useful. The power-electronics content is thin: there is no SiC module-level thermal analysis, the all-Cu screened plate does not fit Al EV loops, and EV is 'licence only'.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It is very transparent: it includes 'where we do not win' sections, admits the GPU-class average loss and the height, mass and cost penalties, shows P10-P90 bands and reports model numbers faithfully. Points come off for these overreaches: the single-UQD08 headline comparator, the 4 kW 'win' that depends on the favourable 25 cm2 assumption, warm-water values that violate the proposal's own 65 C return limit, a CDU-count claim that assumes flow-limited CDUs, fouling prognostics that do not work physically, and a 21 mm stack never re-checked against the synthesis's ~25-30 mm.

fatal_flaws: The mission claim 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' is not met, and the proposal admits it. It loses on height (21 mm vs ~10-13 mm), mass (2.2 kg), plate cost (+US$50-60 at 100k plus a US$120-200 TFM), GPU-class average dT and fouling life (parity at best). Its unit resistance only ties CoolIT's measured 4 kW plate.

Primary market, 1.4-4 kW lidded GPU plates: Tier 1 loses the average by 1.3-3.2 K even to the CoolIT-like reconstruction. That reconstruction overpredicts CoolIT's real 4 kW plate (<36 K max) by 15-24 K: the model gives 50.7 K at 25 cm2 and 60.3 K at 20 cm2. Against real competitor plates LoopCore-G is therefore at parity or worse, which undermines 'AI accelerators first'.

The smart-periphery differentiator, field fouling and R-drift prognostics from the TFM dP signature, is physically insensitive to the failure it targets. The inertial comb and ports set the 3.7 kPa plate dP; channel friction is only 0.23 kPa. A 10 um film adds 0.12 kPa (3.4 %), inside the +/-5 % factory bin. A clustered 4 mm blockage, the die-killer at +17 K per fouling-filtration.md, changes global dP by roughly nothing.

The warm-water value (+13.1 K / +19.2 K supply, US$10.5-38 M per 100 MW) and the 'LoopCore-Ready CDU, inlet to 55 C at 1.0 LPM/kW' spec break the proposal's own 65 C return limit and the CPC Everis UQD 5-65 C rating. At 1.2 LPM/kW the coolant rises 12.7 K, so the return reaches 66.6 C (Tier 1) and 72.7 C (Tier 2); at 1.0 LPM/kW with a 55 C inlet it reaches 70 C.

The manifold as drawn does not hold up. Its 21 mm stack has a 2.5 mm Cu cover spanning troughs 29 mm and 43 mm wide, giving sigma = 0.5p(b/t)^2 = 101/222 MPa at 1.5 MPa proof against 70 MPa annealed yield. That fails the proof and 4.5 MPa burst qualification unless posts or a ~4.5 mm cover are added. Its side-by-side centre-collected topology is never re-verified for uniformity: the 1.06-1.15 max/min and the 1.5 K hot spot are borrowed from design H, a different geometry with 10x15/14x20 mm headers and a ~25 mm block.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Dual-end-fed centreline headers, each end with its own coupling pair. This halves the header and port flow (plate 3.7 vs 5.0 kPa), makes 2x flow feasible within ~100 kPa on standard 1/2-in couplings, and makes the plate symmetric for reverse flow.
Explicit dP accounting at named boundaries: plate port-to-port, plate plus TFM, and tray including the couplings by Cv, published as an OCP v1.0 data pack at three boundaries.

Rack-manifold network analysis with momentum coefficients. Low-dP plates need a 63 mm header or a branch orifice, and U (direct return) beats Z when momentum dominates; this is a design rule for any low-dP plate.
The equal-dP rule with keyed per-class orifices so that GPU, CPU, power-shelf and VPD branches share one manifold. Without it a 2 kW power-shelf branch draws 2.6x its rated flow.

A commissioning protocol in which plates stay jumpered out of the flush loop until an ISO 4406 target is met, together with a staged filtration ladder: CDU 25 um plus 5 um side-stream, TFM 50 um cartridge, captive plate screens laser-welded after braze so they never see the furnace.

Keeping the plate passive and sealed for 10 years and putting the serviceable sensors in a tray module. This avoids in-plate sensing IP; recast the module as flow and calorimetry, not fouling detection.
Fair-comparison framing through flow equivalence (Tier 1 matches CoolIT's average at 0.72 LPM/kW) and equal hydraulic power (34.5 LPM gives 23.8/26.8 K).
A cheap E1 rig that buys and tests incumbent plates and named UQD08/UQDB08 pairs at 5-40 LPM to pin the benchmark dP and coupling Cv.
VR skirt and backside VPD plate for full heat capture, with the flow allocation corrected.
numbers_disputed: Tray-loop headline 'CoolIT ~65-80 kPa (1x UQD08) vs LoopCore 26-29 kPa (2x UQDB08)'. On the same couplings the comparator is 36-40 kPa (the proposal's own table), so the real advantage is ~10 kPa with the metering orifice and ~20 kPa without it, not ~40-50 kPa.

'Cv 3-4 is conservative' for UQDB08. CPC lists Cv ~4.75 as a maximum, and the gap report gives 2.5-4.0 for blind-mate valving. At Cv 2.5 each 9 LPM path carries 12.6 kPa of couplings rather than 4.9-8.7, putting the standard loop at ~30-33 kPa.

CoolIT 4 kW point 'LoopCore Tier 1 31.0/34.4 K vs measured <36 K'. That holds only at 25 cm2. At the ~20 cm2 (~200 W/cm2) heated area inferred in coolit-briefs-numbers.md my model run gives Tier 1 PCM 37.1/40.9 K and paste 40.1/47.1 K, a loss of ~5-11 K. Thin-BLT paste at 25 cm2 gives 36.1 K, a tie.

Footprint robustness is not shown. At the 100 cm2 photogrammetric lower bound the model gives LoopCore same-paste 33.5/39.1 K, only 0.9 K under 34.4 K on the average, and Tier 1 PCM 31.3/34.5 K rather than 28.0/31.1 K.

Warm-water headroom of 53.9 C (Tier 1) and 60.0 C (Tier 2) inlet. With a 65 C return cap the maximum inlet is 52.3 C at 1.2 LPM/kW and 49.8 C at 1.0 LPM/kW. Usable headroom over CoolIT's 40.8 C is therefore about +11.5 K, not +13.1/+19.2 K, and the US$15-38 M Tier 2 value is void.

The fouling alarm '+2 kPa = screen at ~3x clean' is wrong on its own numbers. The screens are 0.30 kPa clean, so 3x clean is only +0.6 kPa, and a +2 kPa alarm trips at ~7.7x. A 10 um channel film adds 0.12 kPa, which is undetectable.

Metering accuracy of +/-3 % flow and +/-4 % heat. That needs a dedicated differential transducer: two 0-1 MPa gauge sensors at +/-0.25 % FS give +/-3.5 kPa on a 10 kPa signal, about +/-18 % flow. At 0.75 LPM/kW the signal falls to 3.9 kPa, and PG25 concentration drift moves Cd and density.
VR skirt on 3-5 % of the flow (0.54-0.9 LPM) for 1.1-1.5 kW gives a 19-42 K coolant rise in the skirt. A rise of 10 K or less needs ~11 % of 18 LPM (~2 LPM).

Plate height 21 mm. The proposal's own stack sums to 22.3 mm with 8.4 mm slots (2+1+0.5+1.5+0.4+8.4+6+2.5) before trough posts or a thicker (~4.5 mm) cover, so ~24-26 mm is realistic. That is consistent with the synthesis's ~25-30 mm.

Comb jets 'decay in a 1.5 mm plenum, no impingement'. The jets are 0.5 mm at 1.2 m/s, Re ~480, so the plenum is only L/d = 3, inside the potential core (~5-6 d). The jets reach the grate and fin tips. The synthesis rule puts the comb at the slot top for ~16 d of decay.

42/32 CDUs per 100 MW. This assumes the CDUs are pump-flow limited. Each unit's heat exchanger would have to carry 2.4-3.1 MW instead of ~2 MW, a 19-56 % rise in per-unit duty, so the CDU reduction is unproven.
Plate-to-plate spread of 2-3 K. Nothing supports it: the model's TIM scatter terms are max-of-8-TC hot-spot terms, not assembly-to-assembly spread.

system-platform.lens: strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: Tier 1 at 28.0/31.1 K (P90 31/35 K) against 34.4/44.2 K is a real win, mostly on maximum dT and Tcase headroom (76 vs 89 C). About 2 K of the average gain comes from choosing PCM over paste. With the same paste, the Monte Carlo P90 is 37 K, which is above CoolIT's 34.4 K, so the average-dT claim is not secure in an OCP head-to-head where the TIM is fixed. Only the maximum-dT claim (P90 42 vs 44.2 K) holds, and narrowly.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: At the hot die it is 28-40 K better than split-flow, but the drop-in robust core misses 85 C even with liquid metal (93 C). The 84.5 C figure needs 25 um loop filtration and has zero margin. On the volume GPU class (B300/Rubin/Rubin Ultra uniform lids) the PCM average is 1.3-3.2 K worse than the CoolIT-like reconstruction. The win there is 2-4 K on maximum plus function, which is a weak pitch into a price-capped Group-A channel.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: A 3.7 kPa plate (claimed <= 8 kPa) and the rack-balancing study (63 mm U-type manifold, the 2.6x overflow of power-shelf branches, the equal-dP orifice) are the best system-level hydraulics in the panel. Marked down because the headline tray-loop comparison is a straw man against a single UQD08. Dual-end ports also double the coupling count per plate, 10 kPa of the advantage is deliberately spent on the metering orifice, and theta_c uniformity is still unmeasured.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: The constant 4 mm flow length tiles to any field size, and dual-end 16 mm ports with dual UQDB08 carry 2x flow at 99-115 kPa. Q capacity is 21.6/29.7/37 kW by tier. Above ~22 kW it needs liquid metal or 25 um loops. A 2.2 kg, 148x152 mm body on a 120x150 mm Rubin-Ultra-class substrate raises retention, shock and ISTA questions that are not addressed.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: All processes are conventional, but the plate is a 5-layer vacuum-brazed stack. It needs fin-tip bonding next to 0.15 mm gaps (Ag wicking risk), captive screens laser-welded after braze, and 100 % 3-flow dP binning. That puts LoopCore-15 at ~US$165 vs ~US$100-115 at 100k. The claimed +US$5-10 for LoopCore-G conflicts with the cost report (+US$10-25 for 1-2 etched layers, +US$40-80 for a full laminate), and the TFM adds US$120-200 per tray. The US$3-5 M line sized for 100k/yr is two orders below Group-A scale (>= 100k/month).

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Pressure integrity is strong: no polymer, zero pressure bow, burst >= 4.5 MPa, leak-before-break. However, fouling life is parity at best (0.6-1.2x), and the captive screens cannot be serviced on a 'sealed 10-year' plate. The warranty is conditional on a commissioning protocol, and the 15 kW plate at 21 mm / 2.2 kg is not drop-in. The TFM adds two coupling pairs per tray, even though connections dominate field leaks, and MGX trays have no slot for it.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: FTO practice is sound: chart Split-Flow, use a rigid pedestal, sense leaks in the drip tray, keep the plate passive. But a continuous skived fin field with centre-fed slots that split flow each way is the closest literal reading of '330/'284/'513. The proposal also leaves out the zero-cost design-around the FTO report recommended (segment the fins at the outlet slots). The TFM sits among NVIDIA tray-sensor patents (US 12,089,378 B2, US 12,174,602, US 11,895,809) and a smart-manifold patent of unconfirmed assignee (US 12,720,714). Defensibility is weak: the core is expired art by design, and the provisionals are hydronic balancing and metering ideas with deep prior art, so there is little exclusive to license.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: Alpha plates in 10-12 weeks and qualification in 12-18 months on known processes are credible. But the Rubin Ultra (2H 2027) design freeze has passed, and Feynman needs a Group-A partner that has no IP reason to license. The TFM needs per-ODM BMC firmware and tray redesign on every platform. Plate, TFM, loop spec and CDU certification together are too much scope for a challenger. The 1-5k/month pilot is far from the volume gate.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: This is the widest family in the panel (G, 15, X, VPD, P, EV licence). The equal-dP keyed-orifice rule genuinely lets 800 VDC shelves share the GPU TCS. The power-electronics fit is still thin: 5-30 W/cm2 shelves gain little from an HMMC core, EV and industrial are licence-only into a pin-fin baseplate market owned by module vendors, and no WEG / aluminium-loop / -40 C qualification path is defined.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: The proposal is unusually candid: a 'where we lose' list, the 13 % same-paste figure, the GPU-class average loss, P10-P90 bands and five named experiments. Marked down for selective boundaries: the single-UQD08 straw man, plate-vs-TFM telemetry, and US$/kW without the TFM. The conservative same-paste '<= 34 K' contradicts the physics P90 of 37 K, and 21 mm vs the physics synthesis' ~30 mm plate is not reconciled. The per-100 MW dollar values rest on KB-L coefficients.

fatal_flaws: The mission claim 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' cannot be made, and the proposal admits it. The 15 kW plate is worse on height and mass (21 mm / 2.2 kg vs ~10-13 mm est.) and costs more (US$165 vs ~US$100-115 at 100k, plus US$120-200 TFM per tray). Fouling life is 0.6-1.2x. On GPU-class uniform lids the average dT loses (Rubin 2.3 kW: 18.4 vs 16.1 K with PCM). The architecture wins a subset of metrics, not all.

The average-dT claim is not defensible under the OCP v1.0 method, a spec CoolIT authored that uses a recommended TIM. With the same paste the HMMC-R Monte Carlo band is 26-37 K, so P90 sits above CoolIT's measured 34.4 K. The scorecard's 'conservative <= 34 K' misstates the physics of record. An OEM running a fixed-TIM head-to-head may see no significant average win, only a max-dT win (P90 42 vs 44.2 K).

The headline system numbers are framed against boundaries CoolIT never published. The '26-29 vs 65-80 kPa' tray loop puts dual UQDB08 against a single UQD08, yet CoolIT's 15 kW TTV used barbed fittings and the coupling is the tray designer's choice. On the same coupling the honest saving is ~21 kPa (the plate dP difference). With the standard 10 kPa orifice it is ~10 kPa (26-29 vs 36-40 kPa on 2x UQD08). 'Per-plate telemetry: none' compares an external module with a plate; the TFM bolts onto anyone's plate, including CoolIT's, so it differentiates nothing.

The platform pillar has no route into the largest channel and sits in a patent thicket. NVIDIA owns the MGX tray, bulkhead and QD layout and buys Rubin plates centrally from Group-A, so a third-party TFM cannot be inserted without NVIDIA/ODM adoption. NVIDIA US 12,089,378 B2 (server-tray flow-through fixture with state sensor), US 12,174,602 (server-level testing) and US 11,895,809 (leak sensing) cover the same functions. US 12,720,714 (smart rack manifold with server-level liquid telemetry) does too; its assignee was not confirmed. 'Read-only, no actuator' is a hope, not a clearance.

There is no moat behind the licence business model. The thermal core rests deliberately on expired Harpole/Cooligy art. The six provisionals are system-integration ideas with abundant prior art: orifice balancing plus measurement (IMI TA-type valves, Belimo-type energy valves, EN 1434 heat meters), Tichelmann/U-return, and commissioning bypass flushing. 'Licence core + comb tooling to a Group-A house' therefore offers nothing exclusive. Once the OCP report is public, AVC, Cooler Master, Delta or Jentech can build the same HMMC on the same skive/etch/braze supply base.

There is unmitigated US Split-Flow exposure through 2028-2031. A continuous skived fin field fed by centre slots that split flow in opposing directions is the closest literal reading of an open-ended '330/'284/'513 claim. The proposal keeps continuous fins and omits the zero-cost design-in that gap-splitflow-continuation-claims-fto.md recommends (fins segmented at each outlet slot), while targeting US hyperscaler samples in 2027-28. That is before the window closes, against an Ecolab-funded patentee with a record of IPRs and litigation.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Equal-dP keyed-orifice rule for mixed racks. It is quantified: an unorificed 2 kW power-shelf branch draws 2.6x its rated flow, and ten such branches take 6 % of GPU flow. Low-dP plates also need a 63 mm U-type rack manifold (direct return beats reverse return when momentum dominates). This is the clearest system-level enabler for putting 800 VDC shelves, VPD plates and GPUs on one TCS.

Dual-end centreline-fed headers with a port pair at each header end. This halves header flow, cuts the plate from the physics synthesis' ~30 mm toward ~21 mm, and makes the plate reverse-flow tolerant and back-flushable.

Publish OCP v1.0 data at three named dP boundaries (port-to-port, with named UQDB08, tray loop), with 3x3 builds at an independent lab. This beats CoolIT on transparency inside its own spec at negligible cost.

A factory 3-flow dP signature, serialised per plate and compared in the field against it, to infer screen loading, channel fouling and TIM drift. It works even without a TFM if rack or CDU dP data are available.

A deployability package: commissioning flush with plate bypass jumpers plus a filtration ladder (25 um full-flow and 5 um side-stream at the CDU, 50 um at the tray, 50 um absolute captive screens welded after braze so they never see the furnace). The 5 % slot dead-end bleed against settling is part of it.

Flow-equivalence and facility-lever framing. Tier 1 matches CoolIT's average at 0.72 LPM/kW, and the flow and supply-temperature levers spend the same margin and are explicitly not additive. That is an honest TCO pitch hyperscalers will accept.
Keep sensors off the plate so the plate stays a sealed, passive 10-year part and avoids in-plate sensing IP (CoolIT 9,052,252, NVIDIA intelligent-plate filings), while the sensors stay serviceable.
VR skirt (a Cu flange with milled channels over the VRM ring) for ~100 % heat capture, and a stepped Cu pedestal for HBM with <= 0.1 mm compliant TIM.
The 'where we do not win' table and P10-P90 scorecard as house style for any external claim.
numbers_disputed: Tray loop '26-29 kPa vs ~65-80 kPa'. Corrected: about 21 kPa less on the same coupling (44-59 vs 65-80 kPa with 1x UQD08, or 16-19 vs 36-40 kPa with 2x UQD08). With the standard 10 kPa metering orifice the saving is only ~10 kPa (26-29 vs 36-40 kPa). Basis: the proposal's own tray-loop table, plus gap-coolit-dp-flow-curves (the CoolIT 15 kW TTV used barbed fittings, not UQDs).
Scorecard 'same-paste average, conservative <= 34 K'. Corrected: P90 = 37 K (P10-P90 26-37 K), above CoolIT's 34.4 K. Basis: SYNTHESIS-physics.md Monte Carlo row 'HMMC-R robust, same paste 0.07'.

'US$7.6 per kW of Tcase-limited capacity vs ~US$9'. Corrected: about US$13/kW once the TFM that delivers the claimed telemetry and balancing is included ((165 + ~120) / 21.6 kW at 100k). That is worse than the ~US$9/kW CoolIT-like plate. The plate-only figure cannot be paired with platform claims.

LoopCore-G premium '+US$5-10 at 100k'. Corrected: +US$15-40. Basis: manufacturing-cost.md and gap-cost-volume put a 1-2 layer etched manifold at +US$10-25 and a multilayer laminate at +US$40-80. LoopCore-G adds grate, plenum, comb, CNC block, a vacuum braze of fin tips, welded captive screens and 100 % 3-flow dP binning.

Plate height '21 mm'. Corrected: plan for 24-30 mm until CFD and a water table confirm it. Basis: SYNTHESIS-physics says the manifold adds ~25 mm and the plate is ~30 mm. The 21 mm stack meets the branch/header-head rule at 6.1 against a >= 6 requirement, which leaves no margin.

Plate dP '3.7 kPa'. Read it as 5.0 kPa (3.9-6.6) for a single port pair, per SYNTHESIS-physics design H. The 3.7 kPa depends on dual-end ports, i.e. two coupling pairs per plate. The <= 8 kPa claim is fine, but quote it with the port configuration stated.

'Comb jets decay in a 1.5 mm plenum, no impingement'. Disputed: 0.5 mm holes at 1.2 m/s in PG25 at 45 C (nu ~1.24e-6 m2/s) give Re ~480. A laminar potential core runs ~5-8 d, i.e. 2.5-4 mm, which is more than the 1.5 mm plenum, so the jets reach the grate and fin tips. SYNTHESIS-physics put the comb at the slot top for 8 mm of decay. Move it there or get a JetCool/Frore claim review before relying on the distinction.

'8 fewer CDUs per 100 MW' credited to LoopCore. Disputed: by the proposal's own table, a CoolIT-like plate at 1.0 LPM/kW is only 1.4 K worse (35.8/45.6 vs 34.5/44.3 K). The flow lever is largely available to incumbents, and the attributable value is the thermal margin, not the CDU count. The US$2.5-38 M warm-water capex figures rest on KB-L dry-cooler US$/kW coefficients.

GPU-tray claim 'in the same budget we add hot-swap, metering and telemetry'. Corrected: the tray is 28-45 kPa with UQD04-class service pairs vs 26-31 kPa for a vendor-plate tray (sysplat_run.out). That is the same budget only with UQD06-class couplings (21-28 kPa), which cost more and take more space.

Tier 2 interface 'Ga-In liquid metal on an Au/Ni lid'. This contradicts the physics rule of record ('liquid metal on 3-5 um electrolytic Ni, no Au'), because gallium alloys with gold. Specify Ni-finished lids or a qualified barrier.

system-platform.lens: Manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility. Judged on the process chain and whether it can be inspected at volume, the cost basis, fouling and filtration, materials and OCP/ASHRAE/NVIDIA fit, burst and proof, service life, height and mass in MGX/NVL trays, and qualification burden. Checks were made against physics/SYNTHESIS-physics.md, base-stress-stiffness.md, fouling-filtration.md, design/sysplat/sysplat_run.py and .out, research/standards-reliability.md, manufacturing-cost.md, gap-cost-volume-and-market-anchors.md, gap-tim2-interface-impedance-and-reliability.md and gap-nvidia-rubin-plate-envelope-and-package-geometry.md.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: Tier 1 is 28.0 / 31.1 K (P90 <= 32 / <= 35 K) against 34.4 / 44.2 K. That is a robust 30 % win on maximum and 19 % on average, and it comes from the shared calibrated Monte Carlo. With the same paste the gain is only 30.0 vs 34.4 K (-13 %). The PCM 0.055 figure assumes 20-30 psi on 117 cm2 (1.6-2.4 kN of clamp), which a TTV can apply but production retention may not.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The robust core misses 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with liquid metal (93 C). Reaching 84.5 C needs the 0.10 mm die-zone core behind 25 um loop filtration, which is not drop-in. On GPU-class lids the average is 1.3-3.2 K worse than the CoolIT-like paste plate with PCM; it wins only on maximum, by 2-4 K.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: This is the best part. The plate is 3.7 kPa (claimed <= 8), loops are costed from catalogue coupling Cv, and the rack balancing and mixed-load orifice analysis is real. Deductions: the new single-layer 29 x 6 / 43 x 6 mm trough topology (branch/head 6.1 against a rule of 6, outlet slots apparently not centre-collected) was never re-run for maldistribution. The headline tray comparison (65-80 vs 26-29 kPa) also mixes coupling configurations.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: The field scales at a constant 4 mm flow length, and dual-end ports hold 36 LPM at 13.9 kPa. Q capacity is 21.6 kW (Tier 1) and 29.7 kW (Tier 2) at 45 C. Beyond 30 kW it needs liquid metal or more area. Plate height and mass grow (21-23 mm, more than 2.2 kg), and a 0.2 mm post-braze finish allowance over 150 mm or more limits laminate size.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Each step exists at volume: skive, PCE, CNC, vacuum braze, laser. Brazing the tips of 0.10 mm skived fins at 0.15 mm gaps into a five-layer laminate does not. The tie bonds that carry burst and the zero-bow claim cannot be inspected 100 % (C-scan cannot see through the fin field or the trough cavities), and the dP-signature QC is blind to fin-gap bridging. The 2.5 mm cover over 29-43 mm troughs breaks the project's own span rule. The cost adders (+US$5-10 per GPU plate; TFM US$120) are understated.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Strengths: a good filtration ladder, a Cu/316L/EPDM/PTFE wetted path, and MAWP 1.0 / proof 1.5 / burst 4.5 MPa aligned with OCP. Against that, dual-end 4-port plates, dual UQDB08 pairs and per-GPU UQD04 couplings multiply field joints, which are the dominant DLC leak source. The TFM with BMC wiring, a 63 mm manifold, a 25 um 'LoopCore-Ready' CDU and a warranty-gated commissioning protocol are not drop-in to MGX/NVL racks. The fouling prognostic cannot see channel blockage, fouling life is 0.6-1.2x at best, and the TFM qualification plan is thin.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: Building on expired Harpole, Cooligy and Tuckerman art and keeping the plate passive is sound. However, 14 centre-fed slots splitting flow 4 mm each way sit squarely within reach of CoolIT's Split-Flow family (expiring 2028-2031), and the claims are not yet charted. The TFM faces an NVIDIA 'intelligent cold plate' FTO gate. The proposed provisionals (dP signature, keyed orifices, dual-end headers) are system-level and close to the HVAC metering and balancing prior art the proposal cites itself, so defensibility is low.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: Qualification takes 12-18 months, giving a pilot in 2H 2027-2028. That misses Rubin, and Rubin Ultra is moving to micro-channel lids owned by the lid vendor. The platform couples four deliverables (plate, TFM with firmware, loop spec, CDU certification) to ODMs, BMC owners, CDU partners and operators, which multiplies schedule risk. The plate-only fallback is the saving grace, but it drops the platform differentiators.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: It covers GPU and ASIC plates, CPU/NVSwitch/CPO, VPD backside plates and 800 VDC shelves. The equal-dP orifice rule genuinely matters for mixed racks. LoopCore-P is effectively a different core (0.3-0.5 mm gaps, no screen), the EV case is licence-only, and laminate cost is high for US$50-150 power-electronics plates.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: The losses table, the conservative/nominal/stretch split and dP quoted with couplings are commendably honest. Against that: the tray headline is apples-to-oranges, and the CDU savings use a 1.2 LPM/kW baseline instead of NVIDIA's ~1.0. The proposal breaks its own base-stress cover rule, contradicts the fouling report on what dP can detect, and gives sensor accuracy (+/-3 % flow) without the instrumentation to support it. It calls B300 lidded although the corpus leans bare-die, and the manifold topology change was not re-modelled.

fatal_flaws: The mission claim fails on the proposal's own scorecard. It loses to the benchmark on 15 kW height and mass (21 mm / 2.2 kg against about 10-13 mm), bare-plate cost (+US$5-60), GPU-class average dT with PCM (+1.3-3.2 K) and fouling life (0.6-1.2x, parity at best). 'Beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' is therefore indefensible as written, and adding a TFM makes system cost and joint count worse.

The pressure boundary as drawn does not pass its own proof test. A 2.5 mm annealed Cu cover spans a 29 mm inlet trough and a 43 mm outlet trough. base-stress-stiffness.md rule 3 caps a 2.5 mm cover at 6 mm span (24 MPa yield-based burst). Scaling by (6/b)^2 gives yield at about 1.0 MPa and 0.47 MPa, so the 1.5 MPa 100 % proof ('no deformation') and 'burst >= 3.0 MPa by design' both fail. The fix is ribs or posts at <= 6 mm pitch, or a cover of 4.5 mm or more (+2 mm, +0.4 kg), and it is not in the height, mass or dP budgets.

The platform's fouling and QC differentiator is physically blind to the failure that kills dies. Channel friction is 0.23 of 3.69 kPa (6 %), and the inertial comb sets per-slot flow. fouling-filtration.md shows 10 % of channels blocked gives +0 % plate dP, while a single 4 mm blocked cluster costs +17 K. The 'factory dP signature' therefore cannot catch Ag-braze wicking (claimed '>5 % dP shift'), and the TFM cannot infer channel fouling or TIM drift. Provisional #1 and differentiator #3 rest on this. A 100 % thermal (IR or transient) screen is needed and is neither planned nor costed.

The platform is not drop-in to NVIDIA's channel. The standard loop needs two UQDB08 pairs per tray (double the rack-manifold ports), a 63 mm rack manifold, a tray-mounted sensor module integrated into the ODM's BMC firmware (PLDM/Redfish), a 25 um 'LoopCore-Ready' CDU and a commissioning protocol written into the warranty. NVIDIA buys Rubin plates centrally from Group-A and defines the MGX tray and manifold, so a component supplier cannot impose any of these. Sold as a plate alone it is drop-in, but then the system value proposition, which is the reason for this proposal, disappears.

The 'drop-in' Tier 1 numbers on real packages are not defensible. They assume PCM at 20-30 psi and a hot gap of 50 um or less under a plate made 24x stiffer so it does not conform. Per the TIM2 report, NVIDIA-class retention of 300-1,000 N gives only 4-12 psi on about 100 cm2, and CoWoS-L packages bow 100-300 um. The proposal also rules out compliant members to avoid CoolIT's patents. At about 0.08 cm2K/W and 100 um of bow, the TIM term alone adds roughly 3-5 K average and up to 15 K at the corners.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Quote dP only at named boundaries: plate port-to-port, tray with a named UQDB08 pair at catalogue Cv, and rack. Publish OCP v1.0 data at all three, with 3 plates x 3 assemblies tested by an independent lab and a plate-to-plate spread KPI of <= 2 K.

The equal-dP keyed-orifice rule for mixed-load racks. Without it a 2 kW power-shelf branch draws 2.6x its rated flow and ten such branches take 6 % of GPU flow. Pair it with the finding that a low-dP plate needs either a 63 mm manifold or about 10 kPa of metering, and that direct return (U) beats reverse return (Z) when momentum dominates.

A filtration ladder with commissioning bypass jumpers and an ISO 4406 acceptance gate before plates connect, which targets the incomplete-flush failure Ecolab cites. Add a serviceable 50 um cartridge at the tray, permanent plate screens laser-installed after braze so they never see the furnace, and corrugated 316L or PTFE-lined hoses to cut elastomer shedding.

Keep the plate passive and sealed and put sensors in a serviceable tray-level module. This avoids in-plate sensing IP and keeps the 10-year plate free of electronics. Offer it as an optional hyperscaler SKU, not a requirement.

Dual-end-fed centreline headers. They halve header flow, cut manifold height from about 30 mm to about 21-23 mm and make the plate reverse-flow tolerant for back-flush. Graft only where the extra port pair is acceptable.
A VR skirt fed from the comb to capture the 1.1-1.5 kW of VRM loss, giving close to 100 % heat capture.

Frame value as 'benchmark Tcase at 0.72 LPM/kW' and as LPM saved per MW (CDU, manifold and QD sizing), not as pump energy, while being explicit that flow and supply-temperature levers are not additive.
E1: for under US$40k in 8 weeks, buy 2-3 incumbent plates and named UQD08/UQDB08 pairs and measure the benchmark dP and coupling Cv before any external claim.
numbers_disputed: Tray loop 'CoolIT ~65-80 kPa vs LoopCore 26-29 kPa'. Corrected like-for-like from the proposal's own sysplat_run.out: with dual couplings, CoolIT-like 36-40 kPa vs LoopCore 26-29 kPa with the orifice (16-19 kPa without); with a single UQD08, 65-80 vs 44-59 kPa. The real tray advantage is about 10-21 kPa, i.e. the plate difference, not 40-50 kPa.

'Burst >= 3.0 MPa by design', 'proof 1.5 MPa, no deformation'. Corrected: the 2.5 mm cover over the 29 mm and 43 mm troughs yields at about 1.0 MPa and 0.47 MPa (24 MPa x (6/b)^2, base-stress-stiffness.md rule 3). It needs ribs at <= 6 mm pitch or a cover of about 4.5 mm or more. Stack height becomes about 23 mm and mass about 2.6 kg if the cover is thickened.

'Ag wicking caught as a >5 % dP shift' and 'fouling measurable from the dP signature'. Corrected: channel friction is 6 % of plate dP and 10 % blocked channels give about 0 % dP change (fouling-filtration.md). Roughly 45 % uniform blockage is needed to move plate dP by 5 %, and clustered blockage (+17 K per 4 mm) is invisible to dP.

Post-braze distortion '1.0 mm finish allowance'. Corrected: the base is 1.0 mm as bonded and 0.8 mm finished, and that budget also covers a 0.1 mm erosion allowance and skive tolerance. The real flatness allowance is about 0.1-0.2 mm, so any post-braze bow beyond about 0.1-0.15 mm over 150 mm scraps the plate.

Tie grate 'bonds >= 50 % of every fin tip' with a '50 % open grate'. Corrected: 50 % is the geometric ceiling, so the target requires void-free bonding on every web; a realistic figure is 35-45 %. Tie stress SF at 3 MPa falls from 4.7 to about 3-3.5. That is still above the physics floor (>= 30 % bonded, SF 2.8), but the acceptance spec is inconsistent.

Diffusion bonding as the 'premium route'. Corrected: not viable for this core. Cu DB at 5-20 MPa applied over about 20 % fin-tip contact area means 25-100 MPa at 800-900 C, above the hot yield of annealed Cu, so 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins would upset or buckle. Light-load vacuum braze is the only route.

LoopCore-G 'adds only US$5-10 at 100k'. Corrected: about +US$20-40 at 100k. It has three etched layers, a CNC block, a cover, Ag plating, vacuum braze, a laser seam, two dissimilar Cu-to-316L stub welds and captive screens, and it needs a 100 % thermal screen; first-two-year yield of 85-92 % versus the 12 % overhead assumed. The cost report's base design with 1-2 laminate layers is already US$110-125 at 100k. The 15 kW plate is realistically US$190-230 at 100k, not US$165.

TFM 'US$120 at 100k' (dual UQDB08). Corrected: about US$200-300. Four tray-side UQDB08 halves alone are about US$100-200, extrapolating US$15-40 per UQD04/06 half (gap-cost report) to the larger blind-mate size; no UQDB08 price was found online. A high-line-pressure differential transducer is also needed.

Flow +/-3 % and heat +/-4 %. Corrected: this requires a true differential sensor (about +/-0.3 kPa on 10 kPa) plus matched, calibrated RTDs. With three gauge sensors at about 1 MPa full scale and +/-0.25 %, the dP error is +/-2.5-3.5 kPa on 10 kPa, which gives about +/-15-18 % flow. Inlet-outlet conduction inside a single 316L body also biases delta-T by about 0.1-0.3 K.

Tier 1 PCM at 0.055 cm2K/W, 'drop-in at 20-30 psi'. Corrected: NVIDIA-class retention of 300-1,000 N gives 4-12 psi on about 100 cm2 (TIM2 report), which puts PCM at about 0.07-0.08. That is +2-3 K average at 128 W/cm2, so drop-in Tier 1 is about 30-31 K before any package-warpage penalty.

CDUs per 100 MW '50 -> 42 / 32'. Corrected: NVIDIA's rack envelope is about 1.0 LPM/kW nominal with a 0.75 floor, and 1.2 is a CDU rating point (gap-nvidia envelope report), so the baseline is 42 CDUs. A saving exists only at 0.75 LPM/kW and only for the 15 kW class (42 -> 32). By the proposal's own admission it is about zero for GPU-class plates.

Height '21 mm' against the physics synthesis's '~30 mm plate, ~25 mm manifold'. The reduction comes from a single 6 mm trough layer that was never re-checked for maldistribution (branch/head 6.1 against a rule of 6 with no margin; outlet collection apparently not centre-collected, and Z-type needs 2-3x the margin). The 1.06-1.15 uniformity is carried over from design H, not recomputed. With the cover fix the height is about 23 mm.

TFM qualification '500 mate cycles'. Corrected: the OCP/RVL expectation for QD mating is at least 1,000 cycles (standards-reliability.md). The plan also lacks EMC and IEC 62368 safety for the TFM electronics and operational vibration and shock for the plate; ISTA 3A covers packaging only.

'B300 flat lid' in the Tier 1 list. The corpus (gap-nvidia envelope and TIM2 reports) leans toward B300 being a bare-die SXM puck with a stiffener ring, which needs a two-height contact, not a flat PCM interface.

advanced-manufacturing.lens: manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: Tier 1 (PCM) gives 28.0 K avg / 31.1 K max against CoolIT's 34.4 / 44.2 K. These numbers trace to the calibrated model and reproduce am_run.out exactly. The max-dT win is robust (flow-driven hot spot 1.5 K vs 8.8 K). The avg win is thin: only 4.4 K with CoolIT's paste, the same-paste P90 (36.9 K) actually loses to the measured 34.4 K, and AM itself contributes 0-0.3 K.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The drop-in R core misses Tcase 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with liquid metal (93 C). Getting to 84 C needs either the P core behind non-standard <=33 um loop filtration or the X lid, which is not a product this company can ship. On Rubin-class lidded 2.3-3.6 kW plates the Tier 1 average is 1.2-2.3 K worse than split-flow; it wins only on max dT and dP.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 5.7 kPa / 1.7 W with an inertial comb is internally consistent: I checked comb velocity 1.18 m/s, branch-to-head ratio 17, slot entry <=0.5 m/s and port 1.49 m/s. The coupling accounting is honest (UQD08 ~25 kPa dominates the loop; specify UQD12-class). However, the 18 mm interleaved four-segment tree is not the maldistribution-verified design H (~25 mm manifold). The 1.10 uniformity is unverified, and photo-etch tolerance on the metering comb threatens long-wave uniformity.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Tier 1 PCM caps at 21.6 kW (27.5 kW on 150 cm2). 30 kW+ needs liquid metal, 20 mm ports (16 mm ports reach 2.98 m/s at 36 LPM) and 16-22 kPa. The artwork laminate tiles naturally to multi-chip and wafer-scale manifolds, but bond-press platen size, uniform bond pressure and laminate yield all scale badly with area.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: The core process is undemonstrated: a one-shot 9-11 layer vacuum diffusion bond, including a 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fin field, at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa. The slot sheet is only ~15% solid (3.3 mm slots at ~3.9 mm pitch leave 0.56-0.7 mm ribs) and the fins offer ~20% tip contact, so local stress is 30-65 MPa against a hot copper flow stress of roughly 10-20 MPa: ribs crush and fins creep-buckle. Alloy Enterprises solves this with inhibitor-coated support fill, which this proposal deliberately avoids. The cost (US$189 / 343) is plausible KB-M arithmetic, but it assumes ~88% yield and omits a per-unit thermal screen. The route screen that rejects L-PBF and ECAM for the volume core is excellent.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale:
Strengths: the 0.15 mm gap plus 50 um screen obeys the project fouling rule; the all-Cu/316L/EPDM wetted path is on the OCP/ASHRAE lists; the tied sandwich is vacuum-tolerant with zero pressure bow. Against that:
- About 6 m of internal bond line, with inlet-outlet cross-leaks that He and dP tests cannot see.
- Post-bond yield is ~35-50 MPa, not 70, which halves the safety factors.
- It is incompatible with Ni-plated wetted paths.
- A 12 cm2 screen loads in weeks, and the tray has no per-plate dP alarm to flag it.
- The PCM retention load (1.6-2.4 kN) is 5-8x the load the bow analysis assumed.
- Diffusion bonding is itself a new process needing 12-24 months of qualification, which the plan applies only to printed parts.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The foundations are expired (Harpole, Valenzuela/Creare, Cooligy, Heatric). But a full etched and diffusion-bonded laminate core walks into live Mikros/Jabil families; the project IP report recommends the skive plus single etched layer route specifically to avoid them. Alloy Enterprises art is adjacent. The proposed claims (segmented centre-fed slots, metering comb, stepped pedestal) are thin against Cooligy/IBM/Purdue HMMC work and CoolIT's compliant-member family.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The clear-SLA and printed-manifold loop is a real accelerator for manifold uniformity. But the bolted printed-manifold TTV cannot run a 1.0 mm untied base, which bows mm-scale at 0.3 MPa per the base-stress report. So month-3 data cannot calibrate the base, bond-line or bow terms that carry the PCM advantage. Bond-recipe development, furnace lead time and qualification of a new joining process push an Nvidia socket to 24-30 months, not 15-18.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family is credible from CPU/NVSwitch through 15-30 kW and tiled wafer-scale, and the niches are sensible: L-PBF AlSi10Mg conformal housings for aerospace and eVTOL, CVD-diamond inserts of 2 cm2 or less for laser/RF. Power-electronics coverage is thin. A diffusion-bonded Cu laminate is overpriced against US$15-40 forged pin-fin baseplates, and SiC traction in aluminium loops is handed off to licensed inserts.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: Unusually candid: AM adds 0-0.3 K, the 21 mm / 2.3 kg fallback is no better than the benchmark, X only ties bare-die LM, and the same-paste P90 is disclosed. The numbers match the model outputs. But several things are asserted rather than checked: process feasibility, the C-scan bond acceptance, the 70 MPa allowable, the 1.8 kg mass, the X cost and the Alloy precedent. The S slot also contradicts the proposal's own AM contamination rule.

fatal_flaws:
The one-shot vacuum diffusion bond is not buildable as specified (850-950 C, 5-10 MPa, 1-4 h, 9-11 OFE sheets plus the skived 0.10/0.15 x 2.0 mm fin field).
- Load path: the slot sheet is ~15% solid (0.56-0.7 mm ribs between 3.3 mm slots at ~3.9 mm pitch), the plenum is mostly open, and the 40%-solid fins are only 50% tied. Local stress reaches 30-65 MPa against a copper flow stress of roughly 10-20 MPa at 900 C (T/Tm ~0.86), so ribs crush, fins creep-buckle and channels collapse.
- Precedent: Oregon State microlamination work (Paul/Kwon/Subramanian) shows the bond-versus-deformation window closes exactly in this regime, and requires compressive stress everywhere for a leak-free bond. Alloy Enterprises gets round it with inhibitor-coated support fill, which the proposal explicitly avoids.
- The 2.5-D CNC fallback still needs the same fin-tip tie, so the fallback does not remove the risk.
- Until a recipe is demonstrated on full-size coupons (rib-aligned columns, <=800 C, <=2-3 MPa, or sub-stack bonding), the product's construction is unproven.

No viable non-destructive acceptance test exists for the defects that kill dies.
- Ultrasonic C-scan cannot image fin-tip bonds beneath a 2 mm fin field or through the internal plenum and tree cavities.
- CT cannot see kissing (zero-volume) bonds.
- An unbonded rib between inlet and outlet slots is an internal short. He leak cannot detect it, and the +/-0.6 kPa dP signature masks a few percent of bypass.
- Yet each starved 2 mm segment costs about +6.8 K, and a 4 mm cluster about +17 K, at 128 W/cm2 (project fouling report).
- A 100% thermal or IR screen per unit is required; it is neither in the plan nor in the cost.

The 350 W/cm2 claim is not deliverable as a product.
- The drop-in R core runs 93 C even with liquid metal.
- The P core needs <=33 um absolute loop filtration, which is not a drop-in condition.
- The 82 C X module puts 0.10 mm fouling-limited channels permanently inside a US$30-50k GPU package lid. Project fouling table: ~4 y relative life behind 33 um, against a 5-7 y server life. It is unserviceable and needs the chip vendor or OSAT to adopt a liquid-filled lid; a thermal-plate company cannot sell it.

Conditional: drop-in fails if the customer mandates a Ni-plated wetted path. GB200-class plates are described as Ni-plated in the project research (secondary sources; not confirmed against an Nvidia document). Electroless Ni-P cannot be pre-plated, because its ~880 C eutectic melts in an 850-950 C bond. Post-bond plating of 0.15 x 2 mm channels behind a 10-layer manifold has no throwing power.

The mission claim 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' is not defensible.
- The same-paste P90 average (36.9 K, the proposal's own number) is worse than the measured 34.4 K.
- On Rubin-class lidded plates the Tier 1 average is worse than split-flow.
- Mass at the 18 mm target is likely 2.1-2.4 kg, matching the self-admitted 'no better' 2.3 kg fallback.
- The S slot (L-PBF Cu manifold shells for wafer-scale) contradicts the proposal's own rule of no L-PBF wetted part upstream of a fin core. A manifold shell is by definition upstream of the fins.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Use AM only as a development accelerator. A clear-SLA water table (1-2 weeks) and printed manifolds can measure momentum coefficients and slot uniformity before any bond tooling. Use a thick-base or tied test article so the base and bond-line terms stay valid.

The fin-conduction-ceiling argument. Once fouling fixes the gap at 0.15 mm, no copper fin geometry exceeds ~138 kW/m2K, and skiving already reaches 92% of that. This cleanly kills ECAM, L-PBF and binder-jet for the volume core and belongs in any decision memo.

The route screen with throughput and capex. Supporting 100k/yr would take 35-117 L-PBF machines (US$35-175M) against 2-3 bond furnaces, and L-PBF, gyroid and binder-jet cores land at 40-63 K. Strong evidence for keeping the volume core conventional.

Four-segment centre-fed slots with an interleaved, both-end-fed tree to compress the manifold from ~25-30 mm toward ~18 mm. Worth a CFD and water-table check before any architecture adopts the 30 mm design-H stack.

The power-map comb as a separate metering and zoning layer, with a 2-week artwork turnaround per new heat map. Laser-drill it to +/-5-10 um rather than photo-etching, and pair it with a production dP signature.

The CTE-matched die-module analysis. Indium TIM1 bond line scales with lid CTE (Cu lid ~259 um vs 79-88 um for 7 ppm/K lids), and segmented <=2 mm strip fins eliminate long-range bow on composite bases. Diamond belongs only at <=2 cm2 sub-die hot spots and in laser/RF/CPO niches, not in a 117 cm2 plate.

AM contamination and cleanliness rules: no printed wetted parts upstream of fine cores, ISO 16232 flush, an ion-chromatography residue limit, and every stage more than 2x the width of the next so nothing sieves upstream of the channels.
An explicit coupling spec: UQD12-class or 3/4 in at 15 kW, report dP at three boundaries, and use 20 mm bores or 316L stubs above 25 kW to respect the 1.5 m/s copper erosion limit.
L-PBF AlSi10Mg conformal cooler-housings as a low-volume aerospace, eVTOL and motorsport inverter niche, where integration and mass justify printing.
numbers_disputed:
Diffusion-bond recipe of 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa nominal, with bond cost US$32 at 100k/yr and 50-200 plates per 8-12 h cycle on 2-3 furnaces.
- Why it fails: with ~15% rib solidity and ~20% fin-tip contact, local stress is 30-65 MPa, above the ~10-20 MPa hot flow stress of copper.
- Corrected: <=2-3 MPa nominal at <=800 C with rib-aligned load columns, roughly 2x longer holds. That means bond cost of ~US$45-60 at 100k/yr and ~4-6 presses.
- Basis: Oregon State microlamination bond/deformation window; copper hot strength (KB-M).

Design allowable for annealed OFHC copper: 70 MPa yield. Corrected: ~35-50 MPa after 850-950 C for 1-4 h, because of grain growth to 100-300 um (Hall-Petch, KB-M; verify on bonded coupons).
- Tie safety factor at burst falls from 4.7 to ~2.3-3.3.
- Land safety factor falls from 5.8 to ~2.9-4.1.
- A 2.0 mm cover over the 15 mm outlet branches first yields at ~1.4-1.8 MPa instead of 2.5 MPa, at or below the 1.5 MPa proof pressure, unless posts are spaced <=15 mm.
- This also breaks the sibling rule of cover spans <=6 mm for a 2.5 mm cover.

Mass of ~1.8 kg for the 15 kW class. Corrected: ~2.1-2.4 kg. A layer-by-layer solid-fraction estimate gives ~235-250 cm3 of copper (base 30, fins and land 31, grate and plenum 19, comb 8, slots 27, window 11, tree 67, cover 45) plus the bosses. That equals the 2.3 kg fallback.

Factory cost of US$189 at 100k/yr and US$343 at 10k/yr, with 12% for yield and overhead. Corrected: ~US$220-260 and ~US$400-460. Basis: 75-90% ramp yield on a 10-layer tied bond, plus a 100% thermal/IR screen (~US$5-10) that the plan omits.
Service life of 1.0x a skived plate (nominal). Corrected: ~0.7x. The project fouling table gives 7 y for 0.15 mm behind a 50 um absolute screen, against the 10 y reference.

Integrated 50 um absolute screen of >=12 cm2 with an alarm at +2 kPa, sized for a 10-year life.
- The project loading model gives ~13 days to 50% blockage for a 5 cm2 cartridge at 1e-4 particles/mL, so roughly a month at 12 cm2.
- Corrected: full-plate area (~100 cm2), or move <=50 um absolute filtration to the CDU.
- A per-plate dP alarm cannot be observed without pressure taps, which MGX/NVL trays do not have.

X module 'lasts the life of the package'. Corrected: 0.10 mm gaps behind 33 um absolute give ~4 y relative life (0.4x, project fouling table), shorter than a 5-7 y server life, inside a non-serviceable lid.

Acceptance criterion 'C-scan tip bond >=50%'. Not measurable through a 2 mm fin field and internal cavities. Corrected: destructive sectioning of witness plates per bond lot, a pressure-bow or flatness-under-pressure test, and 100% thermal/IR screening.

Photo-etch tolerance of +/-25 um on 0.4-1.0 mm OFE sheets. Corrected: ~+/-10% of sheet thickness, i.e. +/-40-100 um (research gives +/-25-50 um only for 100-200 um foils). On 0.5 mm comb holes that means ~+/-16% per-hole flow. Laser-drill the comb.

PCM retention of 20-30 psi over the 117 cm2 footprint implies 1.6-2.4 kN. The stiffness and bow analysis behind '15-25 um flat, PCM holds datasheet value' assumed 130-450 N. Mount bow scales with load (4-25 um at 300 N), so the flatness claim is unverified at the stated retention, and package load limits must be checked.

Tier 1/2 qualified by month 15 and customer-qualified at 15-18 months. Corrected: 24-30 months to an Nvidia socket. The proposal's own 12-24 month new-process qualification applies to diffusion-bonded laminates too, and bond-recipe development plus press lead time come first.

'The printed-manifold TTV-A article calibrates every model term at month 3.' Corrected: base and bond-line terms cannot be calibrated this way. A bolted, untied 1.0 mm base bows ~4.7 mm at 0.3 MPa (base-stress report), so the article needs a 2-3 mm base or a tie, and only manifold and convection terms transfer.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: I re-ran am_run.ev and got the same Tier-1 numbers as SYNTHESIS-physics: 28.0/31.1 K, built from h 13.2 kW/m2K (Nu 7.1 at Re 19, not optimistic), eta 0.56, h_eff 127, isothermal caloric 7.6 K at NTU 1.25, base 3.3, TIM 7.1, convection 10.1. The same-paste result of 30/35 K is shown honestly. Two gaps keep it from 8+: footprint uncertainty is left out of the Monte Carlo (at the 100 cm2 photogrammetry lower bound, Tier 1 is 31.3/34.5 K and same-paste is 33.5/39.1 K), and the 1.5 K flow hot spot is borrowed from design H, not derived for this laminate geometry.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The drop-in R core misses Tcase 85 C at 350 W/cm2 (93 C with LM, 107 C with PCM). Only the P core or the X module get there, and both need <=33 um loops or a lid partner. At Rubin-class lids the Tier-1 average loses by 0.5-2.3 K: the isothermal caloric term reaches 12.2 K at NTU 4.9. At the 4 kW point, 34.4 K max is parity with CoolIT's measured <36 K plate, not a win; the 40.0/50.7 'CoolIT-like' column is a reconstruction that is >14 K pessimistic at that scale.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: Strong points: head ratios are computed (branch 17, outlet 39, slot ~26), velocity caps and the 36 LPM erosion check are applied, the screen is in the budget, and UQD08 (~25 kPa per pair) is called out as 4x the plate. Weak points: the 'tree 0.50 kPa' is the design-H model term (K=1 at 1.0 m/s), copied rather than computed for perimeter loops with tees, bends, windows and combining flow. The perimeter-loop head ratio is ~5, below the >=6 rule. The comb sits over a 1.5 mm plenum (3 jet diameters), not at the slot top as the synthesis rule says. Zoned die-block slots run ~1.2 m/s against the <=0.5 m/s cap. UQD12-class is not confirmed to exist in OCP UQD v2.0.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length is independent of package size, so the manifold tiles: a wafer-scale plate with 4 port pairs, 36 LPM with 20 mm bores, and 30 kW on 150 cm2 at 30.8/33.2 K with LM. Tier 1 with PCM tops out at a 27.5 kW Q cap on 150 cm2, so 30 kW+ needs LM or the P/X cores. Plate dP of 22 kPa at 30 kW, plus couplings, starts to matter.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Rejecting AM for the volume core is correct and well argued. The stated process is not: a 'one-shot vacuum diffusion bond at 5-10 MPa' through a stack whose fin-tip load path is ~20% of plan area (0.10/0.25 fin fraction x 50% grate) puts 25-50 MPa on 0.1 mm fins at 850-950 C, well above hot annealed-Cu flow stress. The 2 mm cover also spans 7.5 mm-tall branch cavities. Separately, 100% C-scan of fin-tip bonds under ~15 mm of cavitied copper is not a credible production inspection. The US$189 cost and 9-12 month furnace ramp inherit this risk.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Fouling compliance is good: 0.15 mm gaps behind a 50 um absolute screen, each stage >2x the next, 5% slot-end bleed, no printed wetted parts upstream of the cores. The tied-sandwich pressure case (MAWP 1.0 / burst >=3.0 MPa) and the OCP-plus test plan are solid. Drop-in fit is weakened by three things: the 18 mm height does not close, the coupling recommendation may be non-standard, the plate screen has no service path, and diffusion-bonded laminate field reliability at volume is unproven (Mikros/Jabil only).

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: FTO targets are identified correctly: CoolIT split-flow, Fabric8 ECAM, Alloy Enterprises, Mikros/Jabil, JetCool, Corintis, with a budgeted search. The proposed claims (segmented centre-fed laminate slots, comb artwork, CTE-matched micro-channel lid) sit on dense prior art (Cooligy, Mikros normal-flow, IBM, Heatric), so defensibility is modest. Avoiding Alloy's sacrificial-support know-how is what creates the bonding problem.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The printed-manifold-on-skived-core TTV at month 3 is a real schedule accelerator and the best idea in the proposal. But bonded-laminate yield, the fin-tip bond process, furnace capacity, Nvidia's centralised Group-A plate purchasing, and a 12-24 month hyperscaler qualification make a 15-18 month qualified product optimistic. The X module depends on a lid/OSAT partner the company does not control.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family is broad and sensibly mapped. The 800 VDC derated chassis (20.9 K vs a credible 41.7 K pin-fin baseline, 0.835 cm2K/W, within the 0.4-1.0 range in power-electronics.md) is a fair comparison. The Al-loop traction market is honestly treated as licence-only, and L-PBF AlSi10Mg housings and CVD inserts are placed in aerospace and laser niches. Power electronics is mostly separate SKUs rather than one architecture.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: Unusually candid: AM adds 0-0.3 K at the TTV, a 'where it does not win' section, an admission that on the fallback it is probably no better than the benchmark in height and mass, Monte Carlo bands, and the model reproduces the synthesis exactly. Deductions: dP and height are asserted for a geometry that was never modelled (design-H terms reused), footprint uncertainty is missing from the bands, the X indium bond line is sized for 100 K although the proposal's own qualification is -40/+125 C, and the 4 kW reconstruction column misleads.

fatal_flaws: Bonding process conflicts with the physics. The specified one-shot vacuum diffusion bond (850-950 C, 5-10 MPa) of skived 0.10 x 2.0 mm fins tied to a 50%-contact grate loads the fin tips at ~25-50 MPa nominal, because tips are only ~20% of plan area. Hot annealed OFE Cu flows at ~10-20 MPa, so the fins creep or upset during a 1-4 h hold. The 2.0 mm cover over 10-15 mm-wide, 7.5 mm-tall branch cavities also sags unless supports are used, and the proposal rules out Alloy-style sacrificial supports for IP reasons. Without a >=50% tied fin-tip bond, the 1.0 mm base, zero pressure bow and PCM/LM flatness claims (and so the 28/31 K) fail. It needs a staged process: bond the laminate manifold first, then vacuum-braze or low-pressure bond the fin tips, managing braze wicking into 0.15 mm gaps. That must be proven by coupons before the cost or yield figures stand.

The 18 mm core height, AM's claimed main value, is not geometrically closed. Interleaved inlet and outlet branches, each fed from both ends, need two perimeter loops that cross at every branch-end edge. The stack-up has a single 7.5 mm tree layer and no crossing level. The stated loop sections (10x15 inlet, 10x22 outlet) cannot sit side by side in the ~20-22 mm per side that a 148 x 152 mm body leaves around a 108 mm core. A realistic height is ~22-25 mm, consistent with SYNTHESIS (manifold adds ~25 mm). On the 21 mm fallback the proposal itself concedes it is probably no better than the benchmark in height and mass.

The mission ('beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect') is not met by the drop-in tier, though this is disclosed. On Rubin-class lids the Tier-1 average is 0.5-2.3 K worse (isothermal caloric 12.2 K at NTU 4.9). At the 4 kW point, 34.4 K max is parity with CoolIT's measured <36 K plate (Monte Carlo P90 ~38 K). At 350 W/cm2 the drop-in R core runs at 93 C with LM and 107 C with PCM, missing 85 C. Only filtration-gated or lid-partner variants reach the target.

The X module's thermal case collapses at its own qualification range. Sized at dT_cyc = 100 K, the indium bond line is 79 um. At the stated -40/+125 C qualification (165 K, same 45 mm DNP) it becomes ~130 um, adding ~2.1 K at 350 W/cm2. Die top goes from 82 C to ~84 C, which ties or loses to conventional bare-die LM (83 C) and leaves a +US$117-277, ECAM single-source part with no thermal advantage.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Fin-conduction ceiling at a fouling-fixed gap: h_eff,max = (sqrt(2hkt)+hb)/(b+t) gives ~138 kW/m2K at 0.15 mm and ~207 at 0.10 mm, against 127 and 187 achieved by skiving. It is a clean, defensible argument that fabrication resolution buys nothing once filtration sets the gap, which kills AM, ECAM pins and offset strips for the volume core in one table.

Printed development loop: a clear-SLA water-table manifold (1-2 weeks) and an L-PBF Cu manifold bolted to a skived core with a metal C-seal (2-3 weeks) give calibrated TTV data at month 3, before any bond tooling. Tip-gap bypass is negligible because the channels are 2 mm deep. This is the cheapest risk retirement of any proposal.
Power-map comb as a replaceable etched artwork layer: zoning becomes a 2-week artwork change, and the plate's dP signature (5.7 +/-0.6 kPa) doubles as a screen and fouling health monitor.

Segmented centre-fed slot segments (27 mm) fed by interleaved, both-end-fed branches, with explicit head-ratio checks (branch 17, outlet 39, slot ~26). This is a useful way to flatten an HMMC manifold, provided the loop crossing is solved.

CTE-matched die-module analysis: indium bond line scales with lid CTE mismatch (Cu lid ~3x thicker bond line than a 7 ppm/K lid). Long continuous Cu features on Cu-diamond bow 130-215 um, so segmented <=2 mm strips and a MoCu cap joined at <=300 C are required. A useful rule set for any micro-channel-lid or direct-to-die partner programme.

Axisymmetric sub-die hot-spot result: a 2x2 mm patch at +650 W/cm2 gives a 27.7 K excess on Cu; Cu-diamond saves 5.3 K, CVD diamond 11.9 K, and CuW adds 14.6 K. Diamond belongs only in <=2 cm2 hot-spot inserts or laser/RF niches, not across a 117 cm2 plate.
Quantified rejections to reuse: a vapor-chamber base costs +9 K at 128 W/cm2; L-PBF fins at their 0.4 mm limit land at 48.9 K; L-PBF gyroid at 40-41 K; binder-jet at 62.6 K.
AM contamination rule: no L-PBF or binder-jet wetted part upstream of a fin core (15-45 um satellites, Ra 3-50 um), plus ISO 16232 flush and ion-chromatography acceptance for ECAM parts.
numbers_disputed: Core height 18 mm (17-19): I estimate ~22-25 mm. The two perimeter loops that serve interleaved, both-end-fed branches must cross, the 148 x 152 body has no room to place them side by side, and SYNTHESIS gives ~25 mm for the manifold and ~30 mm for the plate.

Plate dP 5.7 kPa (tree term 0.50 kPa): I estimate the tree at ~1.0-1.8 kPa and the plate at ~6.5-7.5 kPa. The 0.50 kPa is the model's single K=1 at 1.0 m/s from design H. It omits port-to-loop tee splits, loop corner bends (K 0.3-1 at 1.0 m/s), branch take-offs, window turns, and combining tees at 0.68 m/s on the outlet. The 3-4x plate-level advantage over the ~24.6 kPa reconstruction survives.

Loop-level advantage: the 24.6 -> 5.7 kPa headline is plate-only. With the UQD08 pair most racks use (~20-35 kPa), the loop comparison is ~50 vs ~31 kPa (about -38%), not 4x. 'UQD12-class ~5 kPa' is not confirmed as an OCP UQD v2.0 size; dual UQD08 (5-9 kPa) is the standards-compliant route.

Tier-1 avg/max 28.0/31.1 K (P10-P90 25.7-31.4 / 28.7-34.5): the Monte Carlo leaves out the 100-145 cm2 footprint band from photogrammetry. Re-run, Tier 1 is 31.3/34.5 K at 100 cm2 and 24.4/27.1 K at 145 cm2. Same-paste is 33.5/39.1 K at 100 cm2, which shrinks the like-for-like average margin to 0.9 K. The claim should read -9% to -29% on average, not -19%.

Q cap 21.6 kW: I get 21.1-21.5 kW. The script holds the hot-spot terms at their 15 kW values. A self-consistent solve with TIM scatter scaling with flux gives 21.5 kW, and 21.1 kW if the flow-maldistribution term also scales with Q.

CoolIT-like 4 kW point, 40.0/50.7 K: CoolIT's measured 4 kW plate is <36 K max-case-to-inlet including TIM, so the reconstruction is >=14.7 K pessimistic. The comparison should read Tier-1 34.4 K vs <36 K measured (parity within the Monte Carlo band), not a 16 K win.

X module In bond line 79-88 um / 0.011 cm2K/W / die top 82 C: I estimate ~130 um, ~0.017 cm2K/W, ~84 C. The proposal's own X qualification is -40/+125 C (165 K), while the bond line was sized for 100 K at the same 45 mm DNP and gamma 0.25. The Cu-lid reference bond line rises from 259 um to ~430 um on the same basis.

Mass 1.8 kg: I estimate ~2.1-2.3 kg. Summing solid fractions layer by layer (1 mm base, 40% fins, 50% grate and plenum, ~60% slot, ~85% window, ~40% tree, 2 mm cover over 148 x 152 mm) gives ~235 cm3 of Cu before bosses.

Diffusion bond 5-10 MPa: I estimate <=1-2 MPa is admissible on the fin field. The tip contact fraction is ~0.20, so stack pressure is amplified ~5x at the fin tips, to 25-50 MPa at 850-950 C, above the hot flow stress of annealed OFE Cu. That forces staged bonding or brazing, and changes the US$32/plate bond cost and cycle time.

Zoned real package (die block ~90% of flow through the same 3.3 x 2.0 mm slot segments): die-zone slot velocity is ~1.0-1.2 m/s (head ~0.6-0.7 kPa). That breaks the proposal's own <=0.5 m/s cap and gives a comb-to-slot head ratio of ~3 against the >=15 rule. The fix is a die-zone comb of >=8-10 kPa or deeper slots, which means more height. The 48.3 K hot-die figure assumes the uniformity this geometry does not show.
Rubin-class plate dP 0.1 kPa (section 6.4) vs 0.33 kPa (am_points.out with 12 mm ports): the proposal's two figures disagree. It does not matter in practice because couplings dominate.

advanced-manufacturing.lens: strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims (differentiation vs CoolIT and Nvidia Group-A; FTO vs Split-Flow, JetCool, Frore, Mikros, Asetek, Alloy, Fabric8; OCP-spec convincingness; business-model realism)

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: Tier 1 (R core, PCM) gives 28.0/31.1 K nominal and 31.4/34.5 K at P90, against CoolIT's measured 34.4/44.2 K. These numbers are identical to the SYNTHESIS HMMC-R row, so additive manufacturing adds nothing; the proposal itself says 0-0.3 K. With the same TIM the margin is only -4.4 K average, and the same-paste P90 (36.9 K) is worse than CoolIT's measured average.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: At 350 W/cm2 the deployable R core misses 85 C even with liquid metal (93 C). Getting to 82-84 C needs the 0.10 mm P core or the X module, and both need <=33 um loop filtration that no rack provides today. At 2-4 kW, Tier 1 average dT is 2.3 K worse than split-flow on Rubin 2.3 kW, and at CoolIT's measured 4 kW point (<=36 K max) Tier 1 reaches 34.4 K, essentially parity.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 5.7 kPa including the screen, a branch-to-head ratio of 17, honest UQD08-vs-UQD12 treatment, and a 2x-flow rating with 20 mm ports and an erosion check are all strong. Uniformity is unverified for a 112-segment centre-fed tree. The 18 mm stack shortens the comb-jet decay length to about 4 hole diameters, against the 8 mm slot depth the SYNTHESIS rule assumed.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: 30 kW on 150 cm2 works with liquid metal (cap 38.7 kW) but not with Tier 1 PCM (27.5 kW cap). A tiled wafer-scale manifold with low-volume L-PBF shells is a sensible use of AM, and the 36 LPM port and erosion rules are stated. Above 30 kW the only scaling beyond the baseline HMMC is the gated X module.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: The one-shot 850-950 C, 5-10 MPa diffusion bond of a skived 0.10 x 2.0 mm fin field to a 50 % tie grate loads about 25-50 MPa onto the fin tips. That is several times the hot strength of OFE copper, so it invites fin creep and buckling, or unbonded tips if pressure is reduced. The risk is not analysed. The laminate cost is borrowed from the 2.5-D route, the plate costs US$30-85 more than a skived plate, and the bond process moves away from the skive/braze/weld base that Group-A houses run.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Good points: a 0.15 mm floor behind an integrated 50 um screen, a dP signature, all-copper leak-before-break construction, 100 % He test, and printed parts kept off the wetted volume BOM. Against that: internal bypass leaks between laminate layers cannot be caught by an external He test, a 1-4 h anneal at 900 C grows grains through 0.10 mm fins, the 15 kW plate needs non-standard UQD12-class couplings, and the proposal itself admits 12-24 months to qualify a new process.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: FTO is reasonable because the core sits on expired Harpole and Cooligy art, but that same fact leaves almost nothing to claim. Provisionals 1, 3 and 4 (<=19 mm stack, replaceable comb artwork with a dP-signature screen monitor, stepped pedestal) look obvious over Cooligy '159/'312/'382 and PCHE practice, and only the X-lid claim is narrow but real. Alloy Enterprises already ships diffusion-bonded copper DLC plates, Mikros/Jabil hold live laminate families, Purdue HMMC is omitted, IBM Zurich distributed feed is wrongly filed as expired, and Split-Flow expiry is understated.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The printed-manifold development loop (TTV data at month 3, 1-3-week iterations before bond tooling) is a real schedule advantage. However, Tier 1 qualification at month 15 depends on a fin-field diffusion bond that has never been done in volume. The X gate at month 9 misses the Rubin Ultra micro-channel-lid window (2H 2027 decisions), and US launch in Jan-Apr 2028 falls before the earliest Split-Flow expiry.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The family is broad (GPU, CPU/NVSwitch, 15-30 kW, wafer-scale, 800 VDC, SiC, aerospace L-PBF AlSi10Mg, laser/RF with diamond inserts) and puts AM only in real niches. The power-electronics entries are one-liners. The 20.9 vs 41.7 K SiC comparison is plate-only and leaves out the TIM2 penalty against TIM-free direct-cooled pin-fin baseplates, and the automotive Al-loop route ('licensed forged/MIM Cu insert') is hand-waved.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: This is unusually honest work: it says AM adds 0-0.3 K, lists where it does not win, publishes P10-P90 bands, and its numbers reproduce from am_run.out, am_extra.out and am_xseg.out (checked). Points come off for a scorecard that leads with a TIM swap (PCM against CoolIT's paste), a 4 kW comparison made against a reconstruction rather than CoolIT's measured <=36 K, an unmodelled laminate cost and 18 mm height, and an unsupported claim that grease caused CoolIT's plate-to-plate spread.

fatal_flaws: No defensible differentiation. The volume product is the SYNTHESIS HMMC-R core with PCM (same 28.0/31.1 K, about 5 kPa), so the 'advanced-manufacturing' architecture ships no AM and adds 0-0.3 K. Its only unique volume feature, the diffusion-bonded etched/laser-cut copper laminate, is already sold by Alloy Enterprises: Stack Forging copper DLC plates shipping since Jun 2025, with claims of 10x lower dP, 50 um features and work with 'all the big names' (techcrunch.com/2025/11/05/this-startups-metal-stacks-could-help-solve-ais-massive-heat-problem; 3dnatives.com Alloy copper DLC). It also overlaps the live Mikros/Jabil laminate families. The pitch 'AM-style freedom from PCB capacity, no powder' is Alloy's own pitch.

Bonding mechanics dilemma is not addressed. A one-shot vacuum diffusion bond (850-950 C, 5-10 MPa) of a skived 0.10 mm x 2.0 mm fin field (H/t 20) to a 50 %-open tie grate concentrates 25-50 MPa on about 20 % contact area (40 % fin solidity x 50 % grate). That is several times the hot strength of annealed OFE near 900 C (order 10 MPa, KB-M), so the fins creep and buckle; dropping the pressure leaves tips unbonded given skive height scatter. The tied sandwich is what allows the 1.0 mm base (3.3 K) and zero bow. If it fails, the plate falls back to a thicker, bowing base (+3-6 K), and most of the same-TIM margin over CoolIT disappears. Experiment 3 bonds laminate coupons, not a fin field.

The headline claim does not survive the OCP v1.0.0 protocol that CoolIT authored. OCP measures with a recommended TIM, most likely a PCM (the OAI precedent), so both plates would carry the same interface. The defensible delta is the same-TIM 30.0 vs 34.4 K average (-13 %) and 35.0 vs 44.2 K max. Our same-paste P90 (36.9 K) is worse than CoolIT's measured average. The scorecard's -19 % / -30 % Tier 1 headline is largely a TIM swap; an OEM would see it as such.

Against CoolIT's measured data the advantage disappears on the product the market buys in volume. CoolIT's 4 kW plate was measured at <=36 K max including TIM (0.009 C/W x 4 kW). Tier 1 gives 34.4 K, about 1.6 K better. On Rubin 2.3 kW at 1.0 LPM/kW, Tier 1 average dT is 2.3 K worse than split-flow, and unit cost is US$30-85 above a skived plate. So 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' is false on cost and on low-flux average dT; only Tier 2 liquid metal, an OEM co-design, wins broadly.

There is no go-to-market or business model. Nvidia now buys Rubin plates centrally from Group-A (Jentech, AVC, Cooler Master, Delta). The proposal names no channel: licence to a Group-A house, a hyperscaler ASIC programme, or a CM (Jabil and Flex own Mikros and JetCool). Its diffusion-bond route also moves off the skive/braze/weld supply base Group-A runs, which hurts the 'partner, don't go direct' route the market research says is the only realistic Nvidia path. The X module depends on a lid or package partner (the lid incumbent, Jentech, is a Group-A competitor), on Fabric8 as single source (Fabric8 partners with Wiwynn and GIGABYTE), on Cu-diamond at an unpublished price, and on <=33 um loop filtration. It buys only 1 K over bare-die liquid metal (82 vs 83 C), so as a differentiator it is strategically dead.

The IP posture has errors that make the FTO claim indefensible as written. (a) Purdue HMMC families (2015-19 filings, live to 2035-39 if granted) are not listed, although the proposal uses Purdue's 'HMMC' name. (b) 'IBM distributed feed' is filed under expired foundations, but IBM Zurich's 2008-11 MMC filings may be live to 2028-31. (c) Split-Flow is given as 'about 2028'; with patent-term adjustment the window is Aug 2028 to about mid-2031, and the roadmap reaches customer qualification in Jan-Apr 2028, so a claim chart is needed before US sales. (d) The fins are continuous rather than segmented at the outlet slots, the design-around the FTO report recommends, so every inlet slot literally sits 'between the ends' and splits the flow. (e) The 0.5 mm comb jets at 1.2 m/s have only about 2 mm (4 diameters) to reach the fin tips. That is a jet-onto-microchannel arrangement, which ip-landscape flags for JetCool claim review, and the proposal does not flag it.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Printed-manifold development loop. An L-PBF Cu manifold bolted to a skived core with a metal C-seal, plus a clear-SLA water table, gives calibrated TTV data at month 3 and 1-3-week iterations before any bond tooling exists. Any HMMC programme should adopt it; it is the best schedule de-risker in the proposal.

Fin-conduction ceiling argument. At the 0.15 mm fouling floor no straight copper fin can exceed about 138 kW/m2K (207 at 0.10 mm), and skiving already reaches 92 %. This is a ready, quantitative rebuttal to competitors' AM marketing (Fabric8/Wiwynn '48 % better than skived') and to internal pressure to '3D print it'.

Quantified AM route screen. L-PBF fins, gyroid, binder jet and vapor-chamber bases come out at +9 to +35 K. Use it as sales and design-review ammunition, and keep diamond confined to <=2 cm2 hot-spot inserts (Cu-diamond -5.3 K, CVD -11.9 K on a 2x2 mm +650 W/cm2 patch).

Indium TIM1 bond line scaled to lid CTE. A Cu lid needs about 259 um (11.2 K at 350 W/cm2) against 79-88 um for 7-8 ppm/K lids. Pair this with fins segmented into <=2 mm strips on CTE-mismatched substrates to remove long-range bow. This is the right physics for any micro-channel-lid or direct-to-die co-design bid.

Comb as replaceable artwork. A new power map becomes a 2-week phototool change, with a factory and in-service dP signature (5.7 +/- 0.6 kPa) doubling as screen-health monitoring. It is cheap SKU agility, well suited to the many-SKU hyperscaler-ASIC channel.

AM contamination rules. No L-PBF or binder-jet wetted part upstream of a fin core; ISO 16232 flush; ion-chromatography residue limit; 25 um filter behind printed rig parts. Add these to every proposal's qualification plan.
