Four-segment centre-fed slots fed from an interleaved in-laminate tree to cut the manifold stack from about 25-30 mm to about 18 mm. Graft it once a CFD or water-table test confirms max/min flow <=1.10 and the comb-jet decay length is restored.

Niche-only AM product slots: tiled L-PBF Cu manifold shells for wafer-scale or non-planar SKUs below about 2k/yr, and L-PBF AlSi10Mg conformal cooler-housings for aerospace and motorsport inverters, where integration and mass, not resistance, are the value.
numbers_disputed: 4 kW comparison 'CoolIT-like 40.0 / 50.7 K' against Tier 1 31.0 / 34.4 K: use CoolIT's measured <=36 K max including TIM (<0.009 C/W x 4 kW at 1.5 LPM/kW, coolit-briefs-numbers). The max-dT advantage is then about 1.6 K (~4 %), not about 16 K. The reconstruction is 15 K pessimistic for CoolIT away from its 15 kW calibration point.

Scorecard headline -19 % average / -30 % max (Tier 1 PCM against CoolIT's paste): under OCP v1.0.0, with the recommended TIM on both plates, it is -4.4 K average (-13 %). If CoolIT also ran PCM, its TIM term drops about 9.0 to 7.1 K, giving roughly 32.5 K average, a margin of about 4.5 K (-14 %), and our P90 (31.4 K) is within about 1 K of CoolIT's nominal.

Max-dT benchmark 44.2 K: this is the single highest of 24 readings over 3 plates (per-plate maxima 41.5 / 44.2 / 44.0; three-plate mean at TC5 43.2 K). It should be compared with our P90 of 34.5 K, not the nominal single-plate 31.1 K. The defensible max margin is about 9-10 K (-22 %), not 13 K (-30 %).

Split-Flow 'about 2028': the expiry window is 11 Aug 2028 to about mid-2031, because patent-term adjustment of up to 1,034 days is possible on the 2,129-day pendency of '330 (gap-splitflow-continuation-claims-fto.md). The roadmap reaches customer qualification in Jan-Apr 2028, so budget a US$25-60k claim chart and opinion before US sales.

Laminate set 'US$45-60 at 100k' and factory cost US$189: the laminate figure is not modelled. am_run.out section 9 reuses the 2.5-D route (3 laminates US$16 + CNC block US$34). 9-11 etched sheets at US$2-5 per layer (gap-cost) plus a 7.5 mm tree plate at US$10-25 gives US$30-80. The 12 % yield/overhead is also optimistic for a 10-20-layer bond onto fin tips; 70-85 % first-year yield is more realistic. Expect about US$210-240 at 100k in years 1-2.

Comb-to-fin jet decay '1.5 mm plenum + 0.5 mm grate': that is about 4 hole diameters for 0.5 mm jets at 1.2 m/s, whose potential core is about 5-6 d (2.5-3 mm). The SYNTHESIS rule placed the comb at the slot top so jets decay over an 8 mm slot depth. Expect +1-2 mm of plenum or a diffuser sheet, giving a stack of about 19-20 mm (top of or above the 17-19 mm target), or a non-uniform feed across the about 9 gaps served by each hole.

Diffusion-bond '5-10 MPa, one shot' on the fin field: the local tip stress is 5-10 / (0.4 solidity x 0.5 grate) = 25-50 MPa at 850-950 C, against a hot strength of order 10 MPa for OFE copper (KB-M). The fin field needs <=2 MPa with lands carrying the load, or a lower-temperature interlayer or TLP bond at 600-700 C. As specified the process is not credible without a fin-field trial.

Power electronics '20.9 K vs 41.7 K pin-fin at 50 W/cm2': this is plate-only. Direct-cooled pin-fin baseplates have no TIM2, while our plate under a flat baseplate adds 0.05-0.2 cm2K/W (+2.5-10 K at 50 W/cm2). The like-for-like advantage is about 10-18 K, and only if the module maker gives up its pin-fin. The 0.30 mm gaps in unfiltered automotive WEG loops also need a fouling case.

X module at 350 W/cm2 '82 C, a decisive differentiator': the proposal's own table gives 83 C for Tier 3A bare-die liquid metal on the P core (and 84 C for the P core plate with liquid metal). That is a 1-2 K gain for +US$117-277 at 100k. Its only value is TIM1 reliability (soldered indium against bare-die gallium); it is not a thermal win.

'Grease bow and ageing produced CoolIT's 10 K plate-to-plate spread': this causal claim is unsupported. The spread is one TC8 outlier (37.7 on plate 1 against 27.6 / 27.7), which fits TC placement or heater variation equally well. Withdraw it, or present it as a hypothesis.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: I re-ran risk_run.py with the unmodified model and synthesis copies and got the same term budget: isothermal caloric 7.6 K at NTU 1.20, 0.15 mm gap (deployable), PCM result 28.4/31.4 K. My own 2-D Hele-Shaw conjugate model of the top-fed 4 mm x 2 mm cell, plus PCM run at 15 psi (below its 20-40 psi window), add about 1.5-4 K, which puts the realistic PCM result near 30/33-34 K. It still beats 34.4/44.2 on both. The like-for-like paste average margin is thin (P 0.79, and a coin flip if CoolIT's heated area was 100 cm2).

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: By its own numbers it misses 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with liquid metal (95 C), and it loses on average on uniform low-flux GPU test vehicles by 0.5-2 K because the isothermal-cell caloric penalty dominates there. It never evaluated CoolIT's own 4 kW / 50x50 mm / 6 LPM point. My model run gives 0.0087 C/W with PCM and 0.0099 with paste against CoolIT's <0.009 C/W, i.e. parity at best. The Rubin-class wins rest on a 1-D die-zone model labelled 'indicative'.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: The plate has about 4x lower dP than the reconstructed benchmark. The meter is inertial (89 % of branch dP), so uniformity holds as flow rises. My 1-D dividing/combining plenum check of the off-centre feed (-14/+14 mm) gives 1.07-1.08 max/min along each plenum, which supports the claimed global figure of 1.10. Couplings are treated honestly (UQD08 pair 20-35 kPa, three published dP boundaries). Against that: separator-window losses are missing, the fin-entry jet runs at 1.32 m/s against the synthesis cap of 0.5 m/s, the meter sits exactly at the braze fillet and fly-cut burr zone, and the topology was never run through the network solver.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Q capacity is 21 kW with PCM at 117 cm2, so 30 kW needs liquid metal or more area. Running 30 kW at 1.2 LPM/kW (36 LPM) exceeds the plate's own continuous rating (2.6 m/s jets) and is beyond what a UQD08 pair can pass. Tiling the plenums with a fixed 4 mm flow length is sound in principle, and the proposal sensibly declines per-package kW claims.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Skive plus one-cycle vacuum braze is an incumbent route, and the costing is itemised: US$148 at 100k/yr against about US$105 for the incumbent. Several risks are not acknowledged: the 0.30 mm x 108 mm through-slits gang-sawn from below into 9 mm plenums leave saw run-out arcs at the slit ends that encroach on the frame seal land, with burrs that cannot be removed inside the plenums; fly-cutting the fin tips raises burrs over the metering windows; and filler wicks into 0.15 mm gaps. 'Every kept feature exists in volume production' overstates both the distributor and the 89 % fin-tip tie.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: It follows the synthesis fouling rule: 0.15 mm channels behind an integrated 50 um absolute screen, every stage more than 2x the next, dead-end bleeds. The tied base and leak-before-break logic are sound, and the qualification matrix is complete. But metering at the fin entry creates the impaction and erosion risk the plate otherwise avoids (Stokes number about 5 at the window, 2.0 m/s at the 27 LPM rating). Design life is only 7 years, and 29.5 mm height plus 1.8 kg are worse for drop-in.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The expired Harpole and Cooligy art gives a sound invalidity shield, and the Split-Flow design-arounds (interior outlets, separate distributor, segmented fins) are reasoned. But US sales at M18 (about May 2028) fall before the earliest Split-Flow expiry (Aug 2028, possibly mid-2031), so 'lines up with expiry' is optimistic. The proposal's own claims are narrow process and structure claims, so they defend little.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: This is the proposal's strongest area: five risk-retiring experiments with numeric pass criteria, gates at M3, M6 and M9, two fallbacks (F1/F2) already modelled, a decision to commit publicly only after internal measurement, two suppliers per process, and a credible 14 FTE / US$6.1M envelope. The schedule to OCP in October 2027 is tight but achievable.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: It covers AI data-centre plates, an 800 VDC power-shelf variant with 0.3-0.5 mm channels on the same braze line, EV SiC as licence-only, and DI-water niches. Weak GPU-class average performance and the 350 W/cm2 miss narrow the breadth of the core AI claim.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It is unusually candid: it lists where it does not win and which claims it will not make, labels the Monte Carlo as model-uncertainty-only, and its numbers trace to scripts I reproduced exactly. Deductions: the 3.0 mm-fin 'upside' is physically wrong for a top-fed 4 mm cell, the PCM headline runs below the evidence's clamp window, the cost-per-kW comparison sets a PCM plate against paste, the test-vehicle area choice favours the result, and 18 kW exceeds what the heater tiles are rated for.

fatal_flaws: I found no flaw that would make the architecture fail physically. What follows would make specific claims indefensible.

The mission requires beating CoolIT in every measurable aspect, and by its own scorecard the proposal does not. It loses on body height (29.5 vs about 22-28 mm), mass (1.8 vs 1.2-1.6 kg), average dT on uniform 1.4-3.6 kW GPU test vehicles (+0.5-2 K), the 85 C case at 350 W/cm2 (95 C even with liquid metal) and field record, and it reaches only parity at CoolIT's own 4 kW / 50 mm / 6 LPM point.

The headline average win comes from the TIM, not the plate. With CoolIT's paste the average win is only P 0.79 at 117 cm2. At the evidence's lower-bound footprint of 100 cm2 it becomes a tie in per-area resistance: R'' 0.227 against CoolIT's implied 0.229 cm2K/W, average win P 0.52. Because the test-vehicle area is self-chosen at 117 cm2, a reviewer can attribute the plate-to-plate win to the choice of footprint.

The only flow-metering element (a 0.30 mm slit over 0.15 mm fin gaps, a 0.045 mm2 window per channel) sits exactly where braze fillets, filler wicking and fly-cut burrs form. Variation in fillet or burr size across the plate becomes long-wave flow maldistribution, which is the lever that sets the hot spot. Until E1 and E2 pass, the maximum-dT uniformity basis (global max/min 1.10, 1.5 K) is unproven. The fallback (Rev B orifice comb) is in effect the synthesis design the proposal departed from.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: A gated 12-month programme: E1-E5 experiments with numeric pass criteria (C-SAM land bond at least 80 % overall and at least 50 % in any 10 mm cell, global flow max/min at most 1.15 on a water rig, test-vehicle proxy within 3 K), a public commitment only after internal measurement at G2, and fallbacks (1.5 mm and 2.0 mm base) modelled in advance.

Size the base by unbonded-patch tolerance (about 12 / 18 / 25 mm for 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 mm bases) and enforce it with C-SAM and a 100 % three-point dP-versus-flow test that catches blockage and slit cross-leaks.
Qualify two braze filler routes in parallel to limit wicking into 0.15 mm gaps: 25 um BAg-8 preforms matching the land pattern, and 5 um Ag electroplate forming the Ag-Cu eutectic.

An inertial-dominated branch meter (at least 85-90 % of branch dP inertial), so the uniformity ratios hold from 0.5x to 2x flow. Graft it with the meter placed away from the fin tips and braze joint, for example the synthesis orifice comb at the top of the slot.

Publish pressure drop at three boundaries (port-to-port with bore stated; with CoolIT-style barbs and hose; with a named UQD08 pair), plus 6-point R and dP curves, 3 plates x 3 assemblies at k = 2 uncertainty, R'' per area, plate-to-plate spread as a KPI, and a named independent-lab repeat.
Write explicit 'claims we will not make' and 'where it does not win' sections. Lead GPU-class marketing with real-package and maximum-dT data rather than uniform-TTV averages.
Report extra metrics: flow needed to match the benchmark, equal pumping power, inlet headroom for Tcase,max = 85 C, and Q capacity at fixed LPM/kW.
An integrated, serviceable 50 um absolute screen with dP taps, a passage hierarchy where each stage is more than 2x the next (16 > 10 > 3 > 0.3 > 0.15 mm), and 0.6 mm bleeds at plenum dead-ends.
Build a same-lot hedge core (RF-10, 0.10 mm fins) alongside the baseline, and calibrate the rig with purchased incumbent plates.
numbers_disputed: h_eff 122 kW/m2K and convection 10.5 K are optimistic for a top-fed 4 mm x 2 mm cell. My 2-D Hele-Shaw conjugate cell (0.15 mm inlet and 0.30 mm outlet half-slits, h 13.3 kW/m2K) gives an effective NTU of 0.85 against 1.24 in 1-D. That is a heat-transfer ratio of 0.81, or 0.85 after removing the z-unmixed effect that every microchannel plate shares; 44 % of the flow passes through the lower half and the near-base velocity is 0.83 of the mean. Inertia of the 1.32 m/s window jet recovers part of this, so caloric plus convection rises from 18.1 K to about 18.9-19.8 K: +0.8 to 1.7 K on both average and maximum, a one-sided bias not covered by the symmetric Monte Carlo.

U1 (3.0 mm fins, -0.8 K) is likely a penalty, not an upside. The same 2-D model gives a heat-transfer ratio of 0.70 at H = 3 mm, and the cell's outlet effectiveness falls from 0.57 at H = 2 mm to 0.52 at H = 3 mm. Expect +1 to 2 K.

Plate dP of 5.6 kPa (port-to-port, 18 LPM) leaves out entry and exit losses at the 28 separator windows (unsized, about 0.7-0.9 m/s) and understates the K for a 16 mm vertical port into a tee (about 3-4 rather than 2.3 combined). My estimate is 6.5-8 kPa nominal, still within the claim of 10 kPa or less and still about 3x better than the benchmark.

PCM R'' of 0.055 cm2K/W at 15 psi is optimistic. The evidence (gap-tim2) puts the PCM clamp window at 20-40 psi and gives 0.079 at 50 um bond line. At 15 psi expect 0.06-0.08, a TIM drop of 7.7-10.2 K instead of 7.1 K (+0.6 to 3 K). Run the headline at 25 psi or quote 15 psi as the conservative case.

Adding the h_eff bias and the 15 psi PCM penalty, realistic PCM performance is about 29.5-31 K average and 33-34.5 K maximum. P(decisive: average at most 31 K and maximum at most 35.4 K) falls from 0.84 to about 0.6. P(beats CoolIT on both) stays at about 0.95.

The ripple is wrongly cited. With a 4 mm flow length the sawtooth period is 8 mm, not the 4 mm modelled in hotspot-smoothing. The lumped attenuation 1/(cosh kt + (k_cu k/h_eff) sinh kt), with k = 2pi/8 mm and t = 3 mm, is 0.054, giving about 0.7 K peak-to-peak. The finite-volume model ran 2-5x above the lumped value, so expect about 1-1.5 K peak-to-peak rather than under 0.7 K (+0.3-0.5 K at an unlucky thermocouple).
The heated area is 112.4 cm2, not 117. Four 53 x 53 mm tiles cover 112.4 cm2, so 15 kW is 133 W/cm2 (86 % of the 155 W/cm2 rating), and the tiles' rated limit is 17.4 kW, not 18 kW.
Cost per kW of 7.0 against 8.3 $/kW compares a PCM plate's capacity (21.1 kW) with a pasted CoolIT plate. Like-for-like with paste, capacity is 18.0 kW, giving 8.2 $/kW: parity, not 17 % lower.

The per-area resistance advantage depends on CoolIT's undisclosed footprint. At the 100 cm2 lower bound CoolIT's R'' is 0.229 cm2K/W against 0.227 for this plate with paste (a tie) and 0.211 with PCM (-8 %). The claimed -17 % holds only at 117 cm2.

CoolIT's 4 kW benchmark (25 cm2, 4 kW, 6 LPM, <0.009 C/W) was not evaluated. My scoping-model run gives 0.0087 C/W with PCM, 0.0099 with paste and 0.0068 with liquid metal: parity with PCM, a loss with paste.

Fin-entry jet of 1.32 m/s at 18 LPM (2.0 m/s at the 27 LPM rating) breaks the synthesis cap of 0.5 m/s or less between fins. It raises the Stokes number for 50 um Cu oxide from about 0.2 (fouling report, 0.05 m/s) to about 5. It also sits at or above the roughly 1.5-2 m/s erosion-corrosion guideline for warm water in copper (my recollection, not checked against a source), so derate continuous flow to about 20-24 LPM.

Annealed yield of 70 MPa is too high after a 790 C vacuum braze with grain growth: expect 35-50 MPa for OFE copper. Margins still hold (25 MPa at Kt 2.5 under the 4.5 MPa test), but the safety factors shrink by about 1.5-2x.
Inlet headroom of 53.6 C implies a 66.3 C outlet at 15 kW, which exceeds the 65 C return envelope the proposal itself cites.

risk-first-12mo.lens: manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The PCM headline of 28.4/31.4 K matches the physics synthesis (28.0/31.1 K) and clearly beats CoolIT on max dT (-29%) and on the hot-spot spread. With the same paste the average margin shrinks to 30.4 vs 34.4 K (P(win) only 0.79 with uncontrolled BLT). The headline also assumes PCM at 0.055 cm2K/W while clamped at 15 psi, which is below the 20-40 psi PCM window in our own TIM report, so the average margin is softer than shown.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The proposal admits it does not reach 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with LM (95 C), and that it loses on average by 0.5-2 K on uniform 1.4-3.6 kW GPU TTVs because of the isothermal caloric penalty. It wins on Rubin-class die-concentrated maps and on max dT, but those results are indicative 1-D numbers with no TTV-B data before M12.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 5.6 kPa port-to-port with an inertial 0.30 mm slit meter (branch/plenum ratio 20, branch/header ratio 8.8) follows the synthesis rules. The UQD08 (+20-35 kPa) is honestly booked and dP is published at three boundaries. One risk: braze fillets and kerf scatter at the slit edges directly perturb the meter, and uniformity cannot be checked on production parts beyond a gross 3-point dP test.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length stays at 4 mm at any size, and plenums tile, so area scaling is credible. Q capacity is 21 kW nominal (18 kW at P10) with PCM, and 30 kW needs LM or more area. Port and header velocity forces 20 mm ports at about 36 LPM, so height and mass grow with power.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Every individual tool exists. The enabling step does not exist at volume: area vacuum-brazing about 10,000 fin-tip segments of a 0.15/0.15 x 2 mm skived field to slit lands at 80% or more bond, with 2% or fewer channels blocked. It sits inside a narrow filler window (25 um foil risks fillets of about 0.13 mm radius, comparable to the 0.15 mm gap; 5 um Ag needs flatness of about 10-20 um over 108 mm), and there is no practical 100% NDT. Cost is understated: copper at US$10-12/kg against about US$14.5/kg LME plus the OFE premium, and 100-300 plates per braze load at 1.6-3.1 kN of fixture clamp each. The real figure is about US$170-185 at 100k against the programme target of US$125 or less.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Strengths: all-Cu/Ag-Cu/316L/EPDM wetted path, OCP-consistent MAWP/proof/burst, He at 1e-6, zero pressure bow, leak-before-break, vacuum-tolerant, and an honest 7-year life with no 10-year claim. Weaknesses: the 29.5 mm centre bar with vertical 16 mm ports and screen boss will not fit a 1U MGX/NVL tray, and the low-profile Rev C is roadmap only. The per-plate screen becomes the loop filter with no field telemetry, which adds a silent flow-starvation mode. Slit jets impinge on 0.15 mm fin edges (up to 2.0 m/s at the 27 LPM rating) with no full-flow erosion test, and 7 years falls short of the 10-year plate norm.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: Good awareness: the Split-Flow expiry window (2028 to about mid-2031), the 'comprising an inlet' reading, the expired Harpole/Cooligy shield and a month-1 FTO budget. However, the optional fin segmentation under the outlet slits would create 8 mm channels with a central inlet and outlets at both ends, which moves toward the literal '330 claim rather than away from it. The proposed own claims (slit-metered tied sandwich, gang-slit process) are narrow, hard to police as process claims, and likely obvious over Cooligy plus brazed skived plates.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: Best-in-class gating: E1-E5 retire the key risks by M3-M11, G2 says commit publicly only on measured data, RF-10 hedge cores sit in the same lots, there are dual filler routes, and a 14 FTE / US$6.1M budget is realistic. An M12 demo is plausible. The tie braze is on the critical path, and F1/F2 still depend on it, so a failed E1 has no clean fallback. Revenue timing is weak: the M18-qualified PSM-15 has no shipping 15 kW socket, and PSM-R at M15-24 arrives after Rubin Ultra plate awards.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The SKU table covers ASICs, Rubin, Rubin Ultra, CPO/switch, wafer-scale, 800 VDC shelves, EV (licence only) and SST/RF. The power-electronics variants are effectively different designs (0.3-0.5 mm channels, Al CAB for EV), and a 30 mm, 1.8 kg copper stack is overkill for 5-30 W/cm2 shelves. AI-DC breadth is limited by the height issue until Rev C exists.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: Unusually honest: explicit will-not-claim list, conceded losses (GPU-class average, height, mass, fouling parity, filler-free), three dP boundaries, independent-lab repeat, and footprint hard-mode results. Points off for: P(win)=0.98 that counts model uncertainty only; an unverified 'expected OCP reference TIM'; PCM 0.055 assumed at 15 psi; stale copper price; the 'every kept feature exists in volume production' framing; and a cost-per-kW claim chosen at nominal capacity.

fatal_flaws: The mission's 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect' claim cannot be defended for this architecture, and the proposal itself concedes losses: height (29.5 vs about 22-28 mm), mass (1.8 vs 1.2-1.6 kg), factory cost per plate (+41% as stated, about +60-75% corrected), average dT on uniform low-flux 2-4 kW GPU TTVs (0.5-2 K worse), fouling life (parity at best, 7-year design life against the 10-year norm), filler-free construction and field record. As written, the deliverable can only claim 'beats on thermal, dP and transparency'.

Drop-in failure for the primary AI-DC socket. A 29.5 mm centre bar with vertical 16 mm ports, a screen cartridge boss and stubs puts the installed height at roughly 45-55 mm above the lid. A 1U NVL72/MGX compute tray has roughly 25-30 mm above a lidded package (my estimate, as tray CAD is NDA). The in-plane-header Rev C (21 mm) that might fit is unmodelled roadmap and sits outside the M18 qualification, so the 'qualified product' has no Nvidia-tray home.

The enabling process has no volume precedent and no inline NDT, and all fallbacks depend on it. Area vacuum-brazing of 0.15/0.15 x 2 mm skived fin tips to slit lands (at least 80% bond, at most 2% blocked channels) must land in a narrow filler window. C-SAM cannot resolve 0.15 mm fin-tip joints through a 10 mm coarse-grained annealed Cu distributor or through the fin layer. F1 and F2 (1.5 and 2.0 mm base) still need ties, because an untied base over a 108 mm cavity needs about 8.8 mm per base-stress-stiffness.md. The diffusion-bond fallback carries the fin-creep risk the proposal itself cites. If E1 fails, the architecture has no modelled fallback (a thick lid with posts) that keeps the 1.0-1.5 mm base win.

The cost case does not survive correction. With 2026 copper (LME cash about US$14.4-14.7k/t in Sept 2026, plus the OFE plate/bar premium) and realistic braze-furnace loading under 1.6-3.1 kN of fixture clamp per plate, factory cost is about US$170-185 at 100k, against the programme's own target of US$125 or less and an incumbent at about US$105-110. The claimed '17% lower $/kW' turns into roughly parity at nominal and about 10% worse at P10 capacity. Under Nvidia-centralised purchasing, with Group-A houses at roughly 17-20% gross margin, a 60%+ premium is close to disqualifying for licensing.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: A window-slit meter cut through the distributor floor (0.30 mm inertial slit, at least 0.3 mm so it obeys the L2 fouling rule) in place of a 1,300-hole orifice comb. It has far fewer features, keeps uniformity flow-independent, and can be made with gang saws.
A two-sided gang-slit distributor machined from one Cu plate (plenums from the top, slits from below): a conventional horizontal-mill process that any Taiwanese or Vietnamese house can second-source.

A feature triage table (keep / roadmap / reject) with each feature tied to maturity evidence, plus a gate structure G1-G5 with pre-modelled fallbacks and the rule 'commit publicly only if measured' at G2.

Dual filler-route qualification in E1: 25 um BAg-8 laser-cut preforms vs 5 um Ag electroplate forming the Ag-Cu eutectic, run explicitly to bound the trade-off between voids and wicking. Add a 100% proof test followed by base flatness/profilometry as the production tie screen, since C-SAM cannot do it.
Hedge cores (RF-10, 0.10 mm fins) built in the same skiving lots, giving a free performance option without schedule cost.

A transparency package: three dP boundaries (port-to-port with bore, barbs plus hose, a named UQD08 pair), 3 plates x 3 re-mounts, k = 2 uncertainty, an on-rig benchmark proxy, purchased incumbent plates for TTV-G calibration, a named independent-lab repeat, R'' per area, and a TTV no smaller than the benchmark's footprint.

Fouling hygiene by hierarchy: each passage more than 2x the next (16 > 10 > 3.0 > 0.30 > 0.15 mm), dead-end bleeds, slot ends kept outside the die, a 100% three-flow dP signature, and an ISO 16232 flush.

Comparisons at equal pumping power and at equal dT ('flow to match 34.4 K'), plus inlet-headroom framing (53.6 vs 40.7 C at Tcase,max = 85 C), which converts thermal margin into facility dollars better than 'kW per plate'.
Fully tied construction (zero pressure bow, vacuum-stable to -0.9 barg). It gives a genuine advantage in negative-pressure (Chilldyne-class) loops and for holding TIM bond lines.
numbers_disputed: Copper at US$10-12/kg. Corrected: LME cash was about US$14.4-14.7k/t in early Sept 2026 (Westmetall 8 Sept 2026: 14,737 US$/t; Cochilco 1 Sept 2026: 14,395.5 US$/t; 2026 YTD about 6.03 US$/lb, roughly 13.3k/t). OFE C10100 plate and bar adds a further premium, giving about US$17-20/kg. On about 3.2 kg of blanks with about 1.5 kg of swarf credit, the copper line is about US$37-43 at 100k, not US$26. Sources: https://www.westmetall.com/de/markdaten.php ; https://www.reporteminero.cl/noticia/noticias/2026/09/precio-cobre-cochilco-lme-promedio-alza-inventarios-2026

Factory cost US$148 at 100k/yr (US$235 at 10k). Corrected: about US$170-185 at 100k. Basis: copper +US$11-17; braze +US$6-16 because 0.1-0.2 MPa on a 156 cm2 stack is 1.6-3.1 kN per plate, so 100-300 plates per load means 160-930 kN of fixture clamp in one furnace and 30-80 per load is realistic; internal deburr/electropolish of saw burrs inside 3 x 9 mm plenums and at 0.30 mm slit edges +US$3-6. The premium over the incumbent becomes about +60-75%, not +41%, and the plate misses the programme's US$125 target.

Cost per kW of capacity: 7.0 vs 8.3 $/kW (17% lower). Corrected: about US$175 / 21.1 kW = 8.3 $/kW at nominal, and US$175 / 18.1 kW (P10) = 9.7 $/kW, against about US$110 / 12.7 kW = 8.7 $/kW for the incumbent with corrected copper. That is parity to about 10% worse.
Braze furnace throughput of 100-300 plates per load. Corrected: about 30-80 per load, given the 1.6-3.1 kN per-plate clamp, which needs differential-expansion fixtures with large thermal mass.

PCM pad R'' = 0.055 cm2K/W at 15 psi (headline TIM term 7.1 K). Corrected: the PTM7950 clamp window in gap-tim2 is 20-40 psi, and at 15 psi a BLT of 40-50 um is likely, giving 0.065-0.08 cm2K/W. That makes TIM 8.3-10.2 K, the average 29.6-31.5 K and the max about 32.6-35 K, so P(decisive: avg 31 K or less) falls well below 0.84. Run the headline at 25-30 psi (2.0-2.4 kN on 117 cm2) and verify by D5470 at that pressure.

'15 psi (1.2 kN) is within module-class loads'. Corrected: gap-tim2 gives SXM/OAM-class retention of about 0.3-1.0 kN (KB-L), so 1.2 kN is above that range, and the 20-30 psi a PCM wants is 1.6-2.4 kN.

Monte Carlo P(beats on both average and max) = 0.98, and programme P(decisive at M12) of about 0.7. Corrected: 0.98 is model-term uncertainty only. It excludes TIM clamp pressure, footprint ambiguity (at 100 cm2 the proposal's own number is 0.81) and the probability that the tie braze passes E1. I judge P(decisive public result at M12) at about 0.5-0.6, and P(beats on average, max and published dP at M12) at about 0.8.

'Every kept feature already exists in volume production; only one feature (the 1.0 mm base) is a development item'. Corrected: at least three are development items with no volume precedent. They are fin-tip area brazing of a 0.15/0.15 skived field to slit lands at 80% or more bond; gang-sawn 0.30 +/- 0.02 mm slits used as the production flow meter, with braze-fillet intrusion at their edges; and an integrated 50 um absolute per-plate screen as a field-service item.

Installed height '29.5 mm at the bar'. Corrected: about 45-55 mm above the lid once the vertical 16 mm port stubs, the screen cartridge boss and hose fittings are included (estimate from the stated geometry). The comparable 1U tray budget is about 25-30 mm (estimate; tray CAD is NDA).

Per-lot C-SAM verification of fin-tip bonds. Corrected: this is not feasible on production parts. Resolving 0.15 mm joints needs roughly 50 MHz or more, and that cannot pass through a 10 mm coarse-grained annealed Cu distributor or along the fin layer. Use CT and sectioning on 60 x 60 mm coupons plus 100% proof with post-proof flatness mapping as the production screen.

'EN-plated variant skived at 0.16 mm gap so it still has 0.15 mm after 5 um'. Corrected: EN Ni-P cannot be applied uniformly after braze inside closed 0.15 x 2 mm channels behind 0.30 mm slits. Pre-braze EN followed by a 790 C BAg cycle is an unqualified combination (P diffusion, embrittlement, wetting). Treat the EN variant as unproven, not as a 1-line option.

Design life of 7 years. Not a calculation error, but the standards baseline (standards-reliability.md) is a 10-year plate design life, so this is a drop-in shortfall to list in the scorecard rather than omit.

risk-first-12mo.lens: strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: With PCM the plate reaches 28.4/31.4 K (model P10-P90 26-32 / 29-35 K) against 34.4/44.2 K, so the max-dT win is large and robust. The average win depends on the TIM. With the same paste it is 30.4 K, and P(avg<34.4) is only 0.79 when the bond line is uncontrolled. Swapping the paste for PCM on the CoolIT-like plate brings it to about 32.6/40.4 K, so the architecture alone is worth about 4 K on average and 9 K at the max.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: It wins clearly on die-concentrated Rubin and Rubin-Ultra-class packages (28.1/31.1 vs 33.9/43.6 K). It does not reach 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with LM (95 C), and it loses 0.5-2 K on average on uniform 2-4 kW TTVs, which is the volume market. The proposal is honest about this, but a hyperscaler TTV that is closer to uniform would show the loss.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: Plate dP is 5.6 kPa (P90 7.2) against a reconstructed ~22-25 kPa. The inertial slit meter keeps uniformity ratios of 20 and 8.8 up to 2x flow. dP is published at three boundaries, including a named UQD08 pair, and the proposal openly says the couplings dominate the loop. The 1.3 m/s fin-entry jet carries an untested impaction risk, and uniformity stays an assumption until E2.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Q capacity is 21 kW with PCM at 117 cm2. Reaching 30 kW needs LM or more area, and the plenums tile with the 4 mm flow length unchanged, so the scaling logic is sound. Claiming W/cm2 at a stated R'' instead of 'N kW per package' is the defensible framing. Height, mass and port size grow with size, and nothing at wafer scale is demonstrated.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Every process is incumbent (skive, gang-slit, stamp, one vacuum braze) and can be second-sourced. However, fin-tip brazing across 0.15 mm gaps without wicking, and 0.30±0.02 mm slits gang-sawn through 1 mm of OFE copper, are both unproven at yield. Factory cost is US$148 against US$105 at 100k/yr (+41%), with 1.8 kg of copper per plate.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The integrated 50 um screen, the 0.15 mm channel floor, an all-Cu wetted path, a tied pressure vessel that leaks before it breaks, and a credible OCP-style qualification matrix are all strong. Drop-in is weak: 29.5 mm at the bar and 1.8 kg, against an estimated 22-28 mm and 1.2-1.6 kg. Design life is 7 years, not 10, fouling life is at best at parity, and Ag-Cu fillets sit in the wetted path.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The Split-Flow design-arounds (interior outlets, a separate distributor, solid ribs, segmented fins) and the memo mapping features to expired Harpole/Cooligy art are good practice. But the FTO window is wrong: the 2012 CIP branch runs to about Feb 2032. The FTO list also omits a live 2022 interleaved-nozzle manifold application and the Toyota MMC patents that matter for the PE SKUs. The proposed own claims are narrow, largely anticipated by Cooligy '312 or plate-fin practice, or are process claims that cannot be enforced against offshore makers, so the licensing model has little leverage.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: This is the best part of the proposal: one development item gated at M3, pre-modelled fallbacks, a public-commitment gate at M6 that requires measured data, five risk-retiring experiments, and a realistic 14-FTE, US$6.1M budget. Getting an independent-lab repeat plus 1,000-cycle data by OCP Summit (M11 from a Nov-2026 start) is tight. The design freezes for Rubin Ultra are already past, so the first real volume socket is Feynman or a hyperscaler ASIC.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: The proposal names a family across AI, switch/CPO, 800 VDC shelves, EV under licence only, and DI-water SST/RF niches. However, at 5-30 W/cm2 power electronics do not need a short-flow-length fine core, and the PE SKU is mostly a coarse-channel re-badge. There is no 15 kW package customer, so the flagship PSM-15 is a demo vehicle, not a product.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It has an explicit list of claims it will and will not make, discloses where it loses (height, mass, low-flux average, 350 W/cm2), publishes the paste result regardless, and states probabilities with fallbacks. Points are lost for presenting PCM as 'the OCP reference TIM' when the evidence base marks the v1.0.0 TIM as unverified, and for quoting P(win)=0.98 from model uncertainty alone. The on-rig proxy is also tuned to match the average only (max 47.5 K, dP 70 kPa).

fatal_flaws: The literal mission claim, 'beats CoolIT in every measurable aspect', cannot be made. The proposal itself concedes losses on height (29.5 vs ~22-28 mm at the bar), mass (1.8 vs ~1.2-1.6 kg), average dT on uniform 2-4 kW GPU TTVs (+0.5-2 K), filler-free construction, field track record and fouling life (parity at best). An OEM measuring a sample would find each of these. The defensible claim is narrower: better on every metric CoolIT disclosed, plus dP.

The 'decisive' headline depends on a TIM swap. The proposal calls PCM 'the OCP reference TIM', but the evidence base (gap-ocp-test-spec) records the v1.0.0 recommended TIM as unverified. That spec's primary author is CoolIT's Ben Sutton. If the spec names a grease, the like-for-like average win is only P=0.79 with uncontrolled bond line, and CoolIT can re-test its own plate with PCM to about 32.6/40.4 K. That cuts the average margin to about 4 K (-13%) and leaves max dT and dP as the only decisive wins.

The FTO timing is wrong. The proposal says the Split-Flow exposure ends between Aug 2028 and mid-2031 and that US volume from mid-2028 'lines up with the expiry window'. In fact US 9,453,691 (app 13/401,618, filed 21 Feb 2012, a CIP of 12/189,476, described by CoolIT as its Split-Flow invention) and its continuations US 11,994,350 and US 12,460,878 (issued 4 Nov 2025) carry 2011-12 CIP matter, so they run to about Feb 2032 plus PTA. CoolIT also won a 2024 Federal Circuit appeal (CoolIT v. Vidal, on US 9,057,567, reversing the PTAB) in this 2012 family, so it enforces these patents competently. These patents need a claim chart before any US sale, and they are absent from the proposal's IP section.

The licensing business model has no moat. The proposal says 'no proprietary process, any Taiwanese or Vietnamese skive-and-braze house can second-source'. Its planned claims are narrow or likely anticipated: zoning by slit pitch reads on Cooligy '312, integrated strainers are old, fin-tip ties are plate-fin practice, and process claims cannot be enforced against offshore makers. After a full OCP disclosure at OCP Summit 2027, the Nvidia Group-A houses (AVC, Delta, Cooler Master, Jentech) can build an equivalent plate without a licence. The route to revenue through licensing a Group-A or CM partner is therefore unsupported.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Transparency as a competitive weapon: a full OCP v1.0.0 report with 6-point R and dP curves, dP at three stated boundaries (port-to-port, plate plus barbs and hose, plate plus a named UQD08 pair), 3 plates x 3 re-mounts, k=2 uncertainty, a named independent-lab repeat, and an explicit list of claims it will not make. This beats CoolIT, which published one flow point and no dP, on the axis that CoolIT, as the spec author, cannot dismiss.

Publishing paste and PCM results separately, with measured post-test bond line, while also reporting the architecture-only delta. Making the like-for-like number public first pre-empts the 'TIM swap' rebuttal.

A continuous 0.30 mm window slit as an inertial flow meter, replacing a ~1,300-hole orifice comb. Uniformity holds at 2x flow, every passage stays at least 6x the 50 um screen rating, and the slit is machinable on a gang arbor.

Programme gating: a single development item (the 1.0 mm tied base) gated at M3 with pre-modelled fallbacks F1 and F2 that still win, and a G2 rule to commit publicly only if measured PCM results are at or below 31/35.4 K. RF-10 hedge cores are built in the same lots.

Monetisable comparison metrics in place of a single dT: the flow needed to match 34.4 K (11.1 LPM, 0.74 LPM/kW, comparable to Frore's 0.87 LPM/kW claim), comparison at equal pumping power, and inlet temperature headroom at Tcase,max=85 C (53.6 vs 40.7 C).

An FTO shield memo mapping each feature to expired Harpole US 5,088,005 and Cooligy US 6,986,382 / 7,156,159 / 7,104,312, plus Split-Flow differentiators designed in up front: interior-only outlets, a separate distributor layer, solid zone ribs, and optional fin segmentation under outlet slits.

A TTV built no smaller than the benchmark's estimated footprint (117 cm2), with R'' per area published, a 100 cm2 'hard mode' sensitivity case, and a standing offer to test any CoolIT plate on the same rig.
An integrated, serviceable 50 um absolute screen with dP taps, dead-end bleeds, and port-adjacent slits kept outside the die.
numbers_disputed: Split-Flow family US expiry 'Aug 2028 to ~mid-2031': the CIP branch US 9,453,691 (filed 21 Feb 2012 as a CIP of 12/189,476) and its continuations US 11,994,350 and US 12,460,878 run to about 21 Feb 2032 plus PTA for claims that rely on the CIP matter. Basis: the USPTO Official Gazette lineage for US 12,460,878 (provisionals 61/512,379 of Jul 2011 and 60/954,987 of Aug 2007) and the 9,453,691 gazette entry.

Headline '-17 % average / -29 % maximum vs CoolIT': this mixes a TIM change with the architecture. Applying the physics-synthesis rules (TIM term 9.0 to 7.1 K, scatter 3.5 to 1.5 K), the CoolIT-like plate with PCM is about 32.6/40.4 K. The architecture-only margin is therefore about -4.2 K (-13 %) average and -9 K (-22 %) maximum; with paste on both plates it is -4.0 K / -8.8 K.

'P(beats on both average and maximum) = 0.98': this figure is model uncertainty only. It leaves out the benchmark footprint uncertainty (100-145 cm2, where at 100 cm2 the proposal's own result is P(avg)=0.81 with PCM and 0.52 with paste), the AlN TC bias, and the risk on TIM identity. A realistic figure is about 0.85-0.9 for the PCM headline and 0.6-0.8 for paste like-for-like.

'About 0.7 probability of the decisive result on schedule at M12': about 0.5 is more realistic. The schedule needs a new fin-tip braze process proven by M3, heater commissioning at 128-155 W/cm2, two builds, and an independent-lab repeat, all before OCP Summit, which falls at M11 from a Nov-2026 start. The proposal itself names a 1-3 month slip as the dominant failure mode.
'PCM pad = OCP reference TIM': this is unverified. research/gap-ocp-test-spec lists the v1.0.0 TIM as ASSUMED. Only the 2023 OCP OAI guideline names a phase-change TIM.

'Cost per kW of Tcase-limited capacity 17 % lower (7.0 vs 8.3 $/kW)': procurement buys a plate per package at a fixed spec, so the relevant figure is +41 % factory cost (US$148 vs US$105 at 100k/yr). Group-A houses compete on that number within a ~US$300-400 ASP that Nvidia controls.

On-rig benchmark proxy 'predicted at 34.5 K average, the same as CoolIT': it matches only the average. The same run gives max ~47.5 K (vs 44.2 K measured) and dP 70 kPa (vs a reconstructed ~22-25 kPa), so it cannot stand in for the max-dT or dP comparisons.

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: I re-ran pe_ai_run.py on the corrected model (Darcy friction, isothermal-cell caloric). It reproduces SYNTHESIS-physics exactly: Tier 1 is 28.0/31.1 K (P90 <=32/<=35 K) against 34.4/44.2 K. The isothermal caloric term (7.6 K, NTU 1.25), the 0.15 mm fouling floor and the measured-to-modelled TIM tiers are all respected. Two things hold it back. With the same paste the margin is only 30.0/35.0 K (-13 % on the mean), and the 1.5 K flow-driven hot spot rests on an untested +/-10 % uniformity assumption.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The proposal says so itself: the robust core with liquid metal reaches 93 C at 350 W/cm2 and misses 85 C. Only C-P behind <=33 um filtration (84 C) or direct-to-die gets there. At Rubin flux (2.3 kW, 60 cm2, 1.0 LPM/kW) the isothermal-cell caloric penalty makes the average worse than split-flow: 18.4 K with PCM and 16.9 K with liquid metal, against 16.1 K for CoolIT-like with paste. So the plate does not beat CoolIT on every measurable metric at GPU scale; it wins only on max dT, dP and uniformity.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: The AI side is sound. 5.7 kPa breaks down as ports 2.57 + headers 0.5 + comb 2.0 + channel 0.23 + screen 0.4. The inertial comb branch meets the >=6x/15x header-head rule, and UQD08 (~25 kPa) is correctly called out as the loop-dominant term. The power-electronics dP headlines are housing artefacts. At 65 C the C-A core (comb 1.50 + channel 0.01 + header 0.03 = 1.54 kPa) is no better than the pin field (1.4 kPa); the 2.9 vs 7.6 kPa gap comes from crediting the cartridge with 14 mm ports while the baseline carries Infineon's 6.2 kPa reference housing. The interdigitated feed/collect manifold that C-A needs is not in the 7.8 mm cartridge, so its loss and uniformity are not specified. The 24 mm envelope with 'in-plane headers' contradicts the centre-fed/centre-collected design-H stack (~25 mm manifold, ~30 mm plate). UQD12 is not confirmed as an OCP size.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length stays 4 mm whatever the area, and tiled headers scale to wafer-scale and multi-chip packages. Q capacity is 21.6 kW (PCM), 29.7 kW (liquid metal) and 37 kW (C-P), and 36 LPM costs 22.4 kPa at the plate. But 30 kW on the same 117 cm2 doubles flux to ~56 K average with PCM (>100 C case), so scaling works by area, not flux. Mass (2.2 kg) and coupling dP at 36 LPM (3/4-in class 13-35 kPa) grow, and nothing in the power-electronics-first framing adds AI scaling capability beyond HMMC-R.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Skiving, photo-etching, diffusion bonding in batches of 100-300, CNC and He leak testing are all conventional. US$330/180 at 10k/100k sits under the ~US$400 Group-A ASP, though cost basis is [KB-M] and unconfirmed by RFQ. The 'one part family, one supply chain' claim is overstated. C-R (diffusion-bonded 0.15/0.10 mm), C-A (stamped comb, fin tips brazed with stop-off in 0.4 mm gaps, ENi in 12.5:1 slots) and C-Al (CAB) share no tooling or process. C-A tip brazing and ENi uniformity are real yield risks at automotive cost points (US$19-28 vs pin-fin at US$15-25).

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: AI and data-centre power follow the synthesis rules (0.15 mm behind a 50 um absolute screen, all-Cu wetted path, leak-before-break, a sensible OCP matrix). Automotive is weaker on four counts. The 125 um screen has a 20 kPa bypass that sends unfiltered casting sand to the 0.6 mm comb holes and 0.4 mm gaps exactly when it opens. The Cu cartridge wets twice the cathode area against Al housings. Si-OAT silicate drop-out near fine passages is unaddressed. Sintering onto a 24x-stiffer Cu sandwich raises ceramic and sinter stress. 'PE-A1 drop-in' is not a drop-in, because the jacket must supply alternating feed/collect slots, and the AI plate at ~24-30 mm / 2.2 kg is not drop-in into 12-20 mm envelopes.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: Avoiding the Split-Flow central-slot claims and the ShowerPower-3D meander/swirl claims is credible, and the expired foundations (Harpole/TRW, Tuckerman) are correctly identified. Several claimed novelties look anticipated or weak. Parallel-fed double-sided cards are standard in Denso/Toyota stacked coolers. Comb density mapped to the heat map overlaps EPFL/Corintis heat-map manifolds and Mikros normal-flow art. Keyed balancing orifices are common rack practice. The defensible core is narrow: the tied cartridge as a sintered power-module baseplate.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: The AI core is the same HMMC-R, so the AI path (TTV parity M6-9, qualification M15-18) is unchanged, and the five experiments target the right unknowns (theta_c water table, sinter-on-cartridge cycling, fouling rigs). Running AI, 800 VDC power and automotive (24-36 month PPAP through a licensee) at once dilutes a small team. The automotive value case also rests on SiC savings that the proposal itself rates highly likely to erode.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: This is the widest and best-reasoned coverage among the proposals. It spans AI plates, 800 VDC shelves, SST and solid-state breakers, filtered premium EV loops, double-sided cooling, dielectrics (PAO) and laser/RF niches. It handles the 'SSD' ambiguity correctly and states plainly what to avoid (rail, PCS, SSD) and where to license only (volume EV traction).

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: There is a lot of real modelling: the Fourier spreading model agrees with 3-D finite volume within 2 %, the pin-fin calibration has a Zukauskas cross-check, die-area sensitivity is reported, there is a 'where it does not win' list, and the 10.9 LPM match-flow figure is correct (better than the synthesis's 7 LPM). Against that, the headline power-electronics comparisons use straw men. The 'skived plate' comparator is given h_eff 40 kW/m2K when the project's own coolit_like model gives 99 at the same flow. dP is compared across different housings. Cold-viscosity arguments use -40 C, which is below the ~-37 C freeze point of 50/50 WEG. The 24 mm height and the +0.9 K for an 18 mm variant have no shown basis.

fatal_flaws: The power-electronics dP differentiator does not hold up. At 65 C the C-A core costs 1.54 kPa (comb 1.50 + channel 0.01 + header 0.03; pe_run2 C2), against 1.4 kPa for the pin field (pe_run B5). The quoted 2.9 vs 7.6 kPa simply swaps Infineon's 6.2 kPa reference housing for an idealised pair of 14 mm ports. In the same housing the two are at parity (~7.7 vs 7.6 kPa). The same artefact drives PE-DSC's 0.7 kPa per side vs Boyd's 12.5 kPa.

The automotive -18/-22 % comes from skived fin area, not from the manifold architecture. The proposal's own D1 run shows a straight-through 0.40/0.30x5 skived baseplate reaching the same h_eff of 41 kW/m2K at 8.4 kPa (65 C), about the baseline's 7.6 kPa. The manifold buys only the hottest-switch caloric (8.1 -> 5.3 K, ~3 % of the Tj rise) and ~5 kPa (~1 W of pumping). The cold-start case for the manifold rests on -40 C, which is below the freeze point of 50/50 WEG (~-37 C) and is not a thermal design point: cold coolant carries ~100 K of extra Tj headroom.

The data-centre power headline ('1.8x loss per cm2 of SiC', 1.71 vs 0.94 kW) compares against a straw-man skived plate at h_eff 40 kW/m2K. The project model's coolit_like at the same 2.4 kW / 60 cm2 / 2.9 L/min point gives 99 kW/m2K. Against a fair comparator, skived + PCM carries 1.17 kW, which beats the proposal's own PE-DC + PCM product (C-D core, 1.09 kW). Ag-sinter directly on a skived fin field carries 1.52-1.57 kW, so the cartridge's own contribution is ~9-12 %, not 80 %; most of the gain is sinter-vs-TIM, which is prior-art direct-substrate cooling.

'Drop-in' claims are undermined twice. The C-A cartridge (base 2.0 + fins 5.0 + comb 0.8 = 7.8 mm) has no interdigitated inlet/outlet slot layer, so the customer's jacket must be redesigned to provide one; its header loss and the 'branch/header ratio 18' uniformity rest on hardware nobody has specified. The AI plate's 24 mm envelope with in-plane headers conflicts with the design-H rule (centre-fed, centre-collected stacked headers, ~25 mm manifold, ~30 mm plate). Edge-fed in-plane headers would need 2-3x the branch dP.

Against the mission (beat CoolIT on every measurable metric), the plate loses on average dT at GPU-class flux: 18.4 K with PCM and 16.9 K even with liquid metal, vs 16.1 K at Rubin 2.3 kW / 1.0 LPM/kW. This is an intrinsic isothermal-cell caloric effect, not a tuning problem. The plate also loses on height and mass, and the robust core misses 85 C at 350 W/cm2 (93 C).
strongest_ideas_to_graft: Standard tied-sandwich cartridge (base / skived fins / etched tie grate / etched metering comb) as a self-contained, pressure-rated, separately testable element that drops into different bodies. It decouples the qualified thermal core from envelope-specific manifolds and lets comb artwork be changed per heat map at the cost of a phototool (US$0.5-3k).
Keyed inlet orifice on low-dP power plates (0.28 kPa plate on a ~27 kPa rack header would draw ~2.6x its flow) so 800 VDC shelf plates cannot steal GPU branch head in mixed racks.

Sell the sintered direct-substrate module rather than a better plate under a pad. With a gap pad, the plate choice moves Tj by only 6-7 K (64.8 vs 58.1 K at 400 W). The interface dominates, which is the right strategic insight for data-centre power electronics.

Filtration-class grading of channel width (gap >= 3x the last screen's absolute rating: 0.15 mm behind 50 um for PG25; 0.40 mm behind 125 um for unfiltered automotive), with each passage > 2x the next.

Galvanic rule for Cu cores in Al/WEG loops: ENi all over after braze, an electrically floating cartridge (insulating O-ring, isolated screws), and Si-OAT inhibitor. It acknowledges the ~2x cathode area of finned vs pin-fin cores.

Matched-flow metric: CoolIT's 34.4 K average is matched at 10.9 LPM (0.72 LPM/kW, 2.1 kPa, 0.39 W). This is the correct value from the model sweep and should replace the synthesis's inconsistent '7 LPM / 0.2 W'.
Honest 'where it does not win' table, plus SiC-area sensitivity of the relative gain (-9/-18/-25 % at 1.22/1.62/2.03 cm2), as a template for defensible claims.
numbers_disputed: Power-electronics module dP '2.9 kPa vs 7.6 kPa at 10 L/min, 65 C'. In the same housing: C-A core 1.54 kPa + 6.2 kPa housing = ~7.7 kPa vs pin-fin 7.6 kPa, i.e. parity. Basis: pe_run.out B5 (pin field 1.4 kPa, housing 6.2 kPa held inertial) and pe_run2.out C2 (comb 1.50, channel 0.01, header 0.03, ports 1.41).
PE-DSC '0.7 kPa per side' vs Boyd's 12.5 kPa. This leaves out the shared header, stack manifold and housing; the like-for-like figure is several kPa, set by the housing as in the item above.

Data-centre power '1.71 vs 0.94 kW per switch, 1.8x W/cm2 SiC'. The comparator skived plate should be h_eff ~99 kW/m2K (coolit_like at 2.4 kW / 60 cm2 / 1.2 LPM/kW per the project model), not 40. I re-ran pe_fourier with the proposal's stack: skived + PCM 0.08 gives 1.17 kW (1.46x, not 1.8x); Ag-sinter on a skived 2 mm base gives 1.52-1.57 kW, so the cartridge adds ~1.09-1.12x.

PE-DC + PCM '1.09 kW, 674 W/cm2, better than a skived plate'. It is actually below a CoolIT-class skived + PCM (1.17 kW, ~722 W/cm2), because the de-rated C-D core (h_eff 72) is worse than a 0.2 mm skived fin (h_eff ~99) in the same PG25 loop, where the AI plates already run 0.15 mm gaps.

Automotive '-18 % Rth from the HMMC-X architecture'. A straight-through skived 0.40/0.30x5 baseplate has the same h_eff of 41 kW/m2K (pe_run3 D1), so the architecture-specific gain at 65 C is caloric only: hottest switch 8.1 -> 5.3 K, about -2.8 K on a ~157 C Tj (~-3 %).

'Straight skived fins ~370 kPa at -40 C' (and the C-R/C-A -40 C rows). 50/50 WEG freezes at about -37 C, so the 80 mPa.s viscosity is a supercooled extrapolation. At -30 C (~35-40 mPa.s) the straight-fin figure is ~170-200 kPa, and the cold case is not the thermal design point.

AI plate envelope '~24 mm'. Should be ~30 mm: the 5.4 mm cartridge plus the ~25 mm design-H manifold (8 mm slots + 15-20 mm centre-line headers + walls; manifold-maldistribution rule 7, SYNTHESIS section 3.3). Otherwise the headers are edge-fed, which needs 2-3x the branch dP (comb ~4-6 kPa, plate ~8-10 kPa).
'18 mm low-profile variant costs only +0.9 K'. No calculation supports it; header area falls by ~2x, so header head and maldistribution rise unless the comb dP is raised.

'UQD12-class ~5 kPa at 18 LPM'. Should be 3-9 kPa by Cv 6-10 [KB-L], and a UQD12 size is not confirmed in OCP UQD v2.0.0. The standards-compliant route is dual UQD08 ports (tray 19-28 kPa) per gap-hydraulic-model-reconciliation section 4.

Statement that C-A channels have 'fully developed Nu, h barely depends on velocity'. The thermal entry length is 0.05 Re Pr Dh = 0.05 x 16 x 12.3 x 0.74 mm, about 7 mm, longer than the 4 mm flow length. h is entrance-affected (the model is conservative here), so the statement is wrong even though the number is not optimistic.

power-electronics.lens: Manufacturability, cost, reliability and drop-in compatibility (process chain at volume, yields and tolerances, cost basis, fouling and filtration, OCP/ASHRAE/Nvidia materials, burst and proof, service life, height and mass in MGX/NVL trays, qualification burden)

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The AI core is HMMC-R unchanged, so 28.0/31.1 K with a PCM pad (30.0/35.0 K with the same paste) is reproduced from the calibrated model with honest P10-P90 bands. The like-for-like gain is only -13 % on the average; most of the headline comes from changing the TIM. Flow uniformity (theta_c) has not been measured yet.

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The robust core misses T_case 85 C at 350 W/cm2 even with liquid metal (93 C). Getting under 85 C needs the C-P core behind <=33 um loops (not drop-in) or direct-to-die. On Rubin-class GPU plates at 1.0 LPM/kW the average dT is 2.3 K worse than split-flow (18.4 vs 16.1 K), even with PCM against paste.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: The 5.7 kPa clean plate dP and the inertial comb metering are well argued, and the keyed orifice on power plates is a real system fix. But the dP spec leaves out the 2-5 kPa screen-loading budget the fouling research requires. The ~5 kPa coupling figure relies on a 3/4 in 'UQD12-class' part that may not exist in OCP UQD v2.0.0.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length stays at 4 mm and headers tile, so 21.6 kW (PCM), 29.7 kW (liquid metal) and 37 kW (C-P) are credible, with 22 kPa at 36 LPM. Ports, header height and copper mass all grow with size (already 2.2 kg at 148 x 152 mm), and 30 kW on a drop-in TIM is not reached.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Skiving and photochemical etching are mature. Diffusion-bonding the tips of 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa is not a proven volume process: the fins carry 2.5-5x the nominal stress, well above copper's flow stress at bond temperature; skived tip coplanarity is about +/-20-50 um against the <10 um needed; and production C-scan cannot resolve 0.1 mm tip bonds. The route then needs a second furnace cycle to braze the cartridge into the body. The US$180 figure at 100k counts finished copper weight, not buy weight, and is dearer than the research's skive + etch + laser-weld route, which needs no diffusion bond.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: Strengths: the tied sandwich, burst >= 30 bar, 100 % He leak test and a Cu/316L/EPDM wetted path all match OCP. Weaknesses: the in-plate 50 um screen (>=12 cm2) has no service path and is undersized against the research rule of >=30 cm2 as a removable cartridge. The plate is 24-30 mm and 2.2 kg against CoolIT's ~10-13 mm body. The automotive 'drop-in' needs a redesigned jacket plus module-vendor adoption, and PE-DS needs a new module qualification. That makes three separate qualification stacks.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: It builds sensibly on expired Harpole and Cooligy art. The research says multiple slots alone do not design around a broad Split-Flow claim (live to 2028-31), yet the proposal treats that claim as avoided. Danfoss SP3D, EPFL/Corintis and Purdue sit close to the PE claims. The new claims (cartridge as baseplate, comb mapped to dies, keyed orifice) are narrow and may be anticipated by integrated manifold-microchannel SiC modules.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: Data-centre qualification at M15-18 depends on standing up a diffusion-bond line (9-12 months, US$3-6M) whose yield is unknown. PE-DS depends on a module vendor whose product cycle is 2-3 years, and automotive revenue needs 24-36 months of PPAP through a licensee. Running three segments at once spreads one team across three qualification regimes.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: Few proposals cover this much: one core across AI, 800 VDC power, SST, DSC, PAO/RF and lasers, each with a stated grade and an honest 'where it does not win' list. Value in each segment is thinner than claimed: in 800 VDC shelves the TIM dominates unless vendors redesign around sintered direct-substrate modules, and automotive is licence-only.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It is unusually candid: concessions, P10-P90 bands, published anchors and sensitivity runs. Weak points: the PE baseline fits pin-fin h to a single datasheet Rth with the die area unknown (the gain swings -9 to -25 %). The C-A core's fin height to flow length ratio (5 mm / 4 mm = 1.25) breaks the 1-D duct assumption. The 24 mm height contradicts the programme's own ~30 mm, the SiC-saving economics ignore higher conduction loss, and the dP baseline comes from a different Infineon part number.

fatal_flaws: The mission asks to beat CoolIT in every measurable aspect, and the proposal admits three losses that sink that claim. (1) Height: 24 mm claimed; the programme's own synthesis puts the manifold block at ~25 mm plus a 5.4 mm cartridge, i.e. ~28-31 mm, against CoolIT's ~10-13 mm body. (2) Mass: 2.2-2.4 kg. (3) Average dT on Rubin-class GPU plates: 18.4 vs 16.1 K at 1.0 LPM/kW. In a 1U MGX/NVL tray, ~30 mm of plate plus 16 mm side ports is an unresolved packaging risk (SYNTHESIS item C19).

Plate-level filtration is undersized and cannot be serviced. The channels run at 0.083 m/s, so they never self-clean, and 10-year life rests on an integrated 50 um screen of only >=12 cm2 sitting in the CNC body's cavity, with no removal path. The research rule is >=30 cm2 as a removable cartridge in the inlet fitting or at the tray manifold. Per fouling-filtration, a 5 cm2 50 um screen half-blinds in 13 days at 1e-4 particles/mL, so a 12 cm2 one does so in about a month. Commissioning debris, which Ecolab itself cites as the field failure mode, would trip the 3x dP alarm and force replacement of US$180-330 plates. The 5.7 kPa plate dP also leaves out the 2-5 kPa screen-loading budget.

The core process chain is unproven at volume. The cartridge diffusion-bonds the tips of 0.10 x 2.0 mm skived fins at 850-950 C and 5-10 MPa. Fins are 40 % of the bond area, so they see 12.5-25 MPa, or 25-50 MPa at the 50 % tip contact the design assumes, against copper's ~10-20 MPa flow stress at temperature. DOE laminate-bonding practice uses a two-stage low-pressure bond precisely to prevent channel collapse. Skived tip coplanarity of +/-20-50 um cannot meet the <10 um per-layer flatness the proposal itself requires, and production C-scan through annealed Cu cannot resolve 0.1 mm tip bonds. The braze fallback risks wicking into 0.15 mm gaps. Yield, and with it the US$180 at 100k, is therefore unknown.

The automotive 'PE-A1 drop-in' is not drop-in. The cartridge is a fin field plus a 0.8 mm tie-comb with no header plate, so it needs interdigitated inlet and outlet plenums that a pin-fin jacket does not have. The Tier-1 would have to redesign its die-cast or PPS housing with a two-level manifold insert, and the module vendor (Infineon and others), who owns the baseplate, would have to adopt the cartridge and re-run AQG 324 and PPAP. The headline -18/-22 % cannot be realised by the party the claim implies.

The automotive economics are wrong. The US$70-105 per inverter assumes 18 % less SiC at equal Tj, but the proposal's own model scales loss as 1/area: the smaller die raises Rds(on) and conduction loss by ~22 % at equal current. That is an efficiency and range penalty no OEM accepts as a die-cost saving, so the net value is near zero once the customer's jacket-manifold cost is included. The defensible value is +11-14 % current or a lower Tj for life.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: A keyed inlet orifice on every low-dP power or auxiliary plate, sized to the rack branch dP. Without it a 0.28 kPa plate draws ~2.6x its rated flow and steals head from the GPU branches. It is cheap, and it is a real mixed-rack integration fix.

An inertial (orifice-dominated) metering comb as the flow regulator, so that uniformity holds across 2x flow, temperature and viscosity. Combined with the 4 mm flow length, this gives a strong cold-viscous-coolant argument (-40 C WEG: 3.7-10 kPa vs ~370 kPa for straight skived fins).

One standard pressure-rated tied cartridge reused across bodies (AI manifold body, module baseplate, double-sided card). The only per-SKU change is the comb artwork, a US$0.5-3k phototool mapped to the power map. Good for supply-chain leverage and qualification reuse.

A grade ladder tied explicitly to the last filter each market's loop has (C-R 0.15 mm behind 50 um abs, C-P behind <=33 um, C-D 0.25 mm, C-A 0.40 mm, C-Al). It turns the gap >= 3x filter rule into a product-line rule.

A sintered direct-substrate SiC module on the C-R core (PE-DS-R) for SST, 800 VDC and solid-state-breaker stages in already-filtered PG25 or DI loops. Benchmarking it as loss per cm2 of SiC at Tj 150 C (1,055 vs 582 W/cm2) is a sharp, sellable metric for the power business.

The honest 'where it does not win' table, plus the experiment set: a slot-pair water table with bonded coupons and burst >= 4.5 MPa; a direct-substrate demonstrator measured by Vsd(T) against an HPD G2 on Infineon's reference cooler; a dosed-fouling rig; and a mixed-rack branch test with the keyed orifice.
numbers_disputed: Plate height '~24 mm': I put it at ~28-31 mm. Basis: manifold-maldistribution.md gives the manifold block as ~25 mm (8 mm slots + 15-20 mm headers + walls), the cartridge adds 5.4 mm, and SYNTHESIS-physics says 'the plate is ~30 mm thick'. Design H headers are 10x15 and 14x20 mm. The '18 mm low-profile variant at +0.9 K' is unsupported without a maldistribution re-run.

Plate dP '5.7 kPa incl. screen': as a spec this should be 7.7-10.7 kPa. Basis: gap-fine-channel-fouling research sets a 2-5 kPa screen-loading budget (service alarm at 3x clean); 0.4 kPa is the clean value only.

Integrated screen '>=12 cm2, 50 um abs': it should be >=30 cm2 and removable, at the inlet fitting or tray manifold. Basis: gap-fine-channel rule (>=30 cm2 for 50 um), and fouling-filtration loading data (a 5 cm2 screen half-blinds in 13 d at 1e-4/mL, so ~30 d at 12 cm2).

Copper cost 'US$25/23 for 2.2 kg': about US$35-50 net. Basis: buy weight is ~5-6 kg of OFE C10100, since the CNC body comes from a ~3.6 kg billet plus skive stock; add the OFE premium and subtract scrap credit. That puts PX-15 at ~US$195-205 at 100k and ~US$345-360 at 10k, which leaves thin margin against a ~US$400 Group-A ASP at low volume.

Diffusion-bond loading '5-10 MPa, batches of 100-300 per cycle': fin stress is 12.5-25 MPa at full tip contact (fins are 40 % of the area) and 25-50 MPa at the 50 % contact the design assumes. That exceeds copper's ~10-20 MPa flow stress at 850-950 C, so expect fin creep and gap closure unless low-pressure two-stage bonding or support tooling is used. Yield is unproven.

Sinter compatibility 'fins carry <=10 MPa': for C-R (0.10/0.15 mm) fins this means 25 MPa at full bond and 50 MPa at 50 % tip bond, at 250-300 C where annealed OFHC yields at ~55-60 MPa. The safety factor is 1.1-2.3, not comfortable; specify pressureless sinter or comb-side support as the default.

PE-A1 Rth '-18 %': the realistic band is -9 to -25 %, likely at the low end. Basis: the proposal's own E2 run shows the gain depends on the unknown SiC area per switch. The C-A fin height to flow length ratio (5 mm / 4 mm = 1.25) breaks the 1-D duct model, because flow short-circuits near the comb and under-sweeps the base. The earlier B3 run with 3 mm fins gave -11 %.

Automotive value 'net US$70-105 per inverter': roughly US$0-40, or negative. Basis: 18 % less SiC means +22 % conduction loss at equal current (the model's own P ~ 1/s scaling), and the customer's jacket needs a new interdigitated manifold insert plus tooling (US$3-8 per unit plus NRE), which is not counted.

Coupling 'UQD12-class (~5 kPa) for 15 kW': this size is not confirmed to exist in OCP UQD v2.0.0 (gap-hydraulic report). The standards-compliant options are a UQD08 pair at 20-35 kPa (+/-50 %) or dual UQD08 at a 19-28 kPa loop. The plate's loop-level advantage still holds (45-65 vs 64-90 kPa tray).

Pin-fin baseline dP '7.6 kPa at 10 L/min' comes from FS980R08A7F32B (a 750 V G2 part), not from the SiC FS01MR12A8MA2B that sets the Rth baseline. It must be confirmed on the same part before the '2.9 vs 7.6 kPa' claim goes external.

Automotive screen '125 um with 20 kPa bypass relief': at -40 C, WEG viscosity rises ~57x (80 vs 1.4 mPa s), so the viscous screen dP of a partly loaded element exceeds 20 kPa. The relief would open at every cold start and send unfiltered debris to the 0.6 mm comb holes. In addition, the 0.40 mm C-A gaps are below the research's ~0.5 mm automotive reliability floor.

power-electronics.lens: strategy, market, IP and defensibility of claims (differentiation vs CoolIT and Nvidia Group-A; FTO vs Split-Flow, JetCool, Frore, Mikros, Asetek and power-electronics incumbents; application breadth; how convincing the win is under the OCP spec; business-model realism)

scores.criterion: thermal performance at the 15 kW benchmark (avg & max dT)
scores.rationale: The AI core is the same as HMMC-R: 28.0/31.1 K with PCM against 34.4/44.2 K, and 30.0/35.0 K on the same paste. The max win holds up because it comes from the short flow length. The average win depends on the TIM: the same-paste P90 is 37 K, and when CoolIT is also given the OCP-recommended PCM the margin shrinks to about 4.6 K (-14 %).

scores.criterion: performance at 2027-28 real packages (350 W/cm2 dies) and at 2-4 kW GPU plates
scores.rationale: The robust core misses 85 C at 350 W/cm2 (93 C). Meeting it needs C-P behind loop filtration of 33 um or finer, or direct-to-die. On Rubin-class 2.3-3.6 kW plates the average is 1-2 K worse than split-flow (18.4 vs 16.1 K). At CoolIT's own 4 kW point it wins only 34.4 vs <36 K, and only with a better TIM. The volume market is where the margin is thinnest.

scores.criterion: hydraulics: dP, pumping power, flow uniformity, coupling realism
scores.rationale: 5.7 kPa with an inertial, comb-dominated branch, 1.10 global max/min, an honest statement that UQDs dominate, and a keyed orifice on PE-DC plates to protect GPU branch head are all good systems work. Two weaknesses: the AI dP win is measured against a reconstruction, and the PE claim of 2.9 vs 7.6 kPa leaves the housing out of the cartridge figure. Like-for-like at 65 C it is roughly parity; the real gain appears only at -40 C.

scores.criterion: scalability to 30 kW+ and large/multi-chip packages
scores.rationale: Flow length stays at 4 mm as the manifold tiles. Q capacity is 21.6 kW (PCM), 29.7 kW (LM) and 37 kW (C-P, LM), and dP at 36 LPM is 22 kPa. The 24 mm, 2.2 kg plate and the need for 3/4 in couplings get worse at wafer scale.

scores.criterion: manufacturability at volume and cost
scores.rationale: Every process is conventional, but diffusion bonding in 2-3 furnaces is a capacity and yield bottleneck next to the Asian skiving incumbents. US$180 at 100k is roughly parity with the incumbents' bare-plate cost of US$100-180, not an advantage. The automotive C-A cartridge (US$19-28) costs more than forged pin-fin (US$15-25), and braze wicking and ENi plating in 0.4 x 5 mm slots are unproven.

scores.criterion: reliability, fouling tolerance, drop-in compatibility, qualification
scores.rationale: The filtration-gated grade ladder, the 50 um integrated screen, and the 125 um screen with a 20 kPa bypass are sound. Drop-in is overstated in both markets. On the AI side the plate is 24 mm and 2.2 kg and needs UQD12-class couplings. On the automotive side the 'drop-in' cartridge needs the module vendor to change its baseplate and the Tier-1 to supply interdigitated headers in the housing. A copper cartridge with twice the wetted area in Al/Si-OAT loops over 15 years is a real galvanic-corrosion fleet risk.

scores.criterion: IP freedom-to-operate and defensibility
scores.rationale: The proposed claims are largely anticipated. Claim 1, a cartridge sintered to the AMB as the baseplate, is anticipated by Dowa's Integrated Substrate (PCIM 2020), the EPFL sintered-MMC SiC module and the Wolfspeed/Wieland direct-cooled XM3. Claim 2, hole density mapped to dies, is anticipated by Cooligy US 7,104,312, Toyota US 11,149,937 and HUST US 12,178,022 (live). Claim 3, a double-sided parallel-fed card, runs into Toyota's live US 11,849,569 / 11,596,088. Claims 4-5 are obvious design rules. FTO also has to cover JetCool (heat-map-mapped orifice combs), Mikros (diffusion-bonded etched laminates) and CoolIT '513/'906. No claim text was read.

scores.criterion: time-to-market and programme risk
scores.rationale: AI qualification at M15-18 lands in mid-2028, after Rubin Ultra sockets are awarded and probably before the Split-Flow family expires (Aug 2028 to mid-2031), so a claim chart is needed. The roadmap runs six or more SKUs (PX-15, PX-GPU, PE-DC, PE-DS-R, PE-A, PE-Al, DSC) plus two qualification regimes in parallel. Automotive revenue arrives around 2030 or later, after 24-36 months of PPAP through a licensee and the vehicle SOP lag.

scores.criterion: application breadth (AI DC + power electronics + niches)
scores.rationale: This proposal has the broadest coverage: AI, 800 VDC shelves, SST, DC breakers, EV single- and double-sided, PAO/dielectric, lasers and RF. It also gives sensible avoid/licence-only calls and a good argument that the manifold is what makes fine fins usable in cold, viscous WEG and PAO. The catch is that the best-fit PE markets are small (in-rack 800 VDC plates US$4-90 M/yr) and the large market (EV traction) is licence-only.

scores.criterion: evidence quality and honesty of claims
scores.rationale: It has an exemplary 'where it does not win' list and discloses the SiC-area sensitivity. The pin-fin calibration is anchored to a datasheet value I verified (0.103 K/W). Three numbers conflate effects: the dP figure omits the housing, the 1.8x loss per cm2 SiC mixes the sinter-vs-PCM interface with the core, and the headline uses PCM against paste. 'Drop-in' is mislabelled. The PE results come only from the team's own Fourier model (+/-25 %), the ShowerPower-3D baseline is a KB-L guess, and the costs are KB-M.

fatal_flaws: The mission was to beat CoolIT in every measurable aspect, and this proposal does not, by its own numbers. It loses on height (24 mm) and mass (2.2 kg), and the average is worse on Rubin-class 2-4 kW plates (18.4 vs 16.1 K). At CoolIT's published 4 kW point it wins only 34.4 vs <36 K, and only with a better TIM. The 2-4 kW plate is the volume market, and that is where the win is weakest.

The win is not secure under the OCP spec that CoolIT authored. The spec uses one recommended TIM (most likely a PCM) for every plate. With the same TIM on both plates the average margin falls to about 4.6 K (-14 %), and the same-paste P90 (37 K) is above CoolIT's 34.4 K. A 3-plate OCP test therefore may not separate the averages, and CoolIT will attack the PCM/LM headline as TIM substitution. Only the max-dT and dP wins are robust.

The automotive 'drop-in' (PE-A1) is not drop-in. The cartridge replaces the pin-fin baseplate that the module vendor solders on in its own process. The interdigitated inlet/outlet headers it needs above the comb are not present in a standard HPD-style die-cast jacket, so the Tier-1 must change its housing too. Both Infineon/ST and the Tier-1 have to change before any royalty flows, and the realistic horizon is 2030 or later.

The PE pressure-drop headline (2.9 vs 7.6 kPa) compares unlike things. The 7.6 kPa includes about 6.2 kPa for Infineon's reference-cooler housing (pe_run.out B5), while the cartridge figure includes only idealised 14 mm ports. The pin-fin field alone is 1.4 kPa at 65 C, so in the same housing the two are at parity. The hydraulic advantage is real only at cold start.

The IP position is close to indefensible as written. Claim 1 (cartridge sintered/soldered to the AMB as module baseplate) is anticipated by Dowa's Integrated Substrate (PCIM 2020), the EPFL nanosilver-sintered manifold-microchannel SiC module, the Wolfspeed/Wieland direct-cooled XM3 baseplate and Infineon US 9,731,370. Claim 2 (die-mapped hole density) is anticipated by Cooligy US 7,104,312 (expired), Toyota US 11,149,937 (expired, fee-related) and HUST US 12,178,022 (live; hotspot-directed MMC for power modules). Claim 3 (double-sided card fed in parallel by manifold cartridges) sits inside Toyota's live US 11,849,569 B2 / US 11,596,088 B2, configurable double-sided MMC cold plates expiring around 2040-41; that is an FTO block for PE-DSC, not an asset. Claims 4-5 are obvious design rules. The moat is process know-how only.

There is a channel conflict. Delta and Flex, two of the named PE-DC channel partners, are direct competitors: Delta is a Rubin Group-A plate supplier and makes its own cold plates, and Flex owns JetCool. Jentech, the proposed automotive baseplate licensee, is also Group-A. Licensing the cartridge to them arms competitors in the primary AI market.

The business model is upside-down for a 'power-electronics-first' variant. On the programme's own estimate, in-rack 800 VDC plates are worth US$4-90 M/yr, and the automotive royalty is US$2-5 per module with a 4-5-year adoption chain. Meanwhile the AI core is identical to HMMC-R, so the PE emphasis adds sprawl (six or more SKUs, AQG 324 plus OCP qualification) without adding AI differentiation.
strongest_ideas_to_graft: A keyed inlet orifice on every low-power plate (800 VDC shelf, NVSwitch, CPO), sized to the rack branch dP so the plate cannot steal GPU head, verified with a mixed-rack branch test. This belongs in any architecture's rack kit.

One standard pressure-rated cartridge (fin field, tie grate and metering comb bonded into a single element) dropped into several bodies: a Cu manifold body, a module baseplate or a double-sided stack. One OCP qualification matrix then covers the GPU plates and the data-centre power plates.

A grade ladder gated by filtration: C-R at 0.15 mm behind a 50 um absolute screen, C-P at 0.10 mm only for loops at 33 um or finer, and coarse C-A/C-Al grades for Al/WEG loops. This makes fouling a published specification rather than a hidden risk.

The cold, viscous coolant argument. The short-flow-length manifold makes fine fins usable in WEG at -40 C and in PAO (C-A at about 3.7 to 10 kPa at -40 C against about 13-19 kPa for pins, and -39 % Rth against pin fins in PAO). This is a real differentiator for eVTOL, radar and defence niches, where it beats everything else.

Automotive practice worth reusing: a 125 um screen with a 20 kPa bypass relief so a clog never starves the inverter; ENi over the whole cartridge with an electrically floating cartridge and Si-OAT inhibitor to manage the larger copper cathode area; ASTM D1384/D2570 corrosion gates.
Sell power density (W per cm2 of SiC, current headroom, lower Tj for power-cycling life) rather than die-area savings, because that pitch survives SiC price deflation.
