A cheap, decisive demonstrator: a sintered direct-substrate cartridge measured by Vsd(T) at 10 L/min WEG at 65 C against an HPD G2 pin-fin module on Infineon's reference cooler, followed by 50k power cycles.
Report a 'flow to match' metric (CoolIT's 34.4 K reached at 10.9 LPM and 0.39 W) as a TCO and CDU-sizing lever for hyperscalers, and publish curves at 0.5-1.5 LPM/kW in OCP format.
The honest 'where it does not win' list and the SiC-area sensitivity disclosure, kept as a template for external claims.
numbers_disputed: PE pressure drop at 10 L/min, 65 C: '2.9 kPa vs 7.6 kPa (-62 %)'. Corrected: parity at about 7.6-7.7 kPa each in the same housing, or about 1.4-1.5 kPa core-for-core (pin-fin field 1.4 kPa against cartridge comb plus channel about 1.5 kPa). Basis: pe_run.out B5 attributes 6.2 of the 7.6 kPa to the reference-cooler housing, and C2 includes only 14 mm ports for the cartridge. The genuine dP advantage exists only at -40 C (pins about 13 kPa vs cartridge 3.7-10 kPa).

Data-centre PE: '1.8x the loss per cm2 of SiC (1.71 vs 0.94 kW)'. Corrected: about 1.38x for the core alone. Basis: pe_run.out B7 at equal Ag-sinter interface gives 31.4 K (skived split-flow) vs 22.8 K (PE-DC-R) per 400 W switch. The rest of the gain comes from swapping PCM for sinter, which any plate can do.

Headline AI average '-19 % (28.0 vs 34.4 K)' and max '-30 % (31.1 vs 44.2 K)'. Corrected: -14 % average (28.0 vs about 32.6 K) and -24 % max (31.1 vs about 40.9 K) when CoolIT is also run with the OCP-recommended PCM. Basis: SYNTHESIS-physics term structure, with CoolIT's TIM term going from 9.0 to 7.1 K and paste scatter from 3.5 to 1.5 K. CoolIT's Q capacity at 85 C correspondingly rises from about 12.7 to about 14 kW.

Cost comparator 'Group-A Rubin ASP ~US$400' next to PX-15 at US$330/180. Corrected: a bare-plate Rubin ASP of about US$200-280 and an incumbent bare-plate cost of US$100-180, because the US$300-400 line items probably include UQD halves and hoses (gap-cost-volume-and-market-anchors.md). The comparison also sets a 2.3 kW plate against a 15 kW plate. PX-GPU at US$130 vs GB200 skived at about US$105 (100k/yr) is a 24 % premium, not a saving.

PE-A1 '-18 % Rth, drop-in'. Corrected: -9 % to -25 % depending on SiC area per switch (1.22 to 2.03 cm2, pe_run2.out E2), because the FS01MR12A8MA2B die area is not public. It is also not drop-in, since it needs a module-vendor baseplate change plus a new housing manifold.

Automotive net value '~US$70-105 per inverter'. Corrected: about US$35-75 if SiC per switch is about 1.2-1.6 cm2 (PE-A2 gain -13 % to -22 %) and SiC deflates 30 %. Even that is realisable only if module vendors re-bin die area. Value capture by a licensor is far lower; the proposed US$2-5 royalty implies under US$5 M/yr before 2031 at realistic adoption.

Split-Flow expiry '~2028'. Corrected: 11 Aug 2028 to about mid-2031 depending on '330 PTA (gap-splitflow-continuation-claims-fto.md), with US 12,101,906 of unknown subject matter. A data-centre launch at M15-18 (around H1 2028) falls before the earliest expiry and needs a claim chart and opinion (US$25-60k) before US sales.

Automotive timeline 'PPAP through a licensee in 24-36 months'. Corrected: first royalty-bearing vehicles around 2030-31. PPAP after licence signature at about M18 gives M42-54, and inverter SOP follows the module PPAP by 1-2 years.

synth.architecture_name: PRISM (Proven-subset, Recessed-meter, Interdigitated, Skived Manifold) cold plate: an all-copper, single-vacuum-braze tied-sandwich manifold micro-channel plate. A skived RF-15 fin field (0.15/0.15 x 2.0 mm) is kerfed at every inlet and outlet line under stamped floor-grate windows. A stamped orifice meter sheet sits 1.0 mm above the braze plane. Plenums are laminated, with a stamped separator and a forged/CNC centre header bar. The 1.0 mm base is fly-cut after braze. Flow length is graded by local flux: 4-12 mm, 6 mm on the 15 kW TTV.
grafts: Base architecture, from risk-first-12mo (PSM-12): skived fin core, single vacuum-braze cycle, tied 1.0 mm base, centre header bar. Also its gated 12-month programme (E-series experiments, G1-G5 gates, commit publicly only if measured), two filler routes (BAg-8 preforms and 5 um Ag eutectic), transparency package (dP at three boundaries, 3x3 builds, k=2, independent repeat, R'' per area, TTV no smaller than CoolIT's), 'claims we will not make', edge-fed benchmark proxy and purchased incumbent plates.

Separately stamped orifice meter sheet with zoning by orifice pitch/size, from hmmc-elite and the synthesis comb, made by stamping or punching as conventional-cost's stamped selector floor. Advanced-manufacturing's judge rule applied: avoid photo-etch tolerance. The meter is placed off the braze plane, per the risk-first judge.

Interface tiers on one core (PCM drop-in / liquid metal on electrolytic Ni with no Au / stepped bare-die pedestal), 'never grease on >=100 mm lids', stepped HBM pedestal machined post-braze, heat-proportional zoning with HBM never downstream of a die, coupling class named in every dP claim, and conservative/nominal/stretch scorecard discipline: from hmmc-elite.

Narrow fin-level openings with land much larger than fin height, to kill the Hele-Shaw short-circuit (from the hmmc-elite judge's 2-D model). Extended here with full-height fin kerfs and 6 mm cells, which bring the 2-D differential versus CoolIT to 0 K.

Printed-manifold development rig (clear-SLA water table plus a printed or CNC manifold bolted on a thick-base skived core) for M2-3 calibration; fin-conduction-ceiling argument (h_eff <=138 kW/m2K at 0.15 mm); AM route screen and AM contamination rules; CTE-matched micro-channel-lid rules and diamond only in <=2 cm2 hot-spot inserts: from advanced-manufacturing.

Fly-cut-after-braze base (thick during processing, thin after); 100% three-flow dP test with CpK >= 1.33; dead-end bleeds; optional green-laser filler-free outer seam; second-sourceable skive/stamp/braze supply base; warm-water TCO pitch: from conventional-cost.

Filtration ladder (commissioning flush with plate bypass jumpers and ISO 4406 gate; CDU 25 um + 5 um side-stream; tray-level >=150 cm2 cartridge, required for the P-grade; plate keeps only a 50 um absolute guard; 316L/PTFE hoses). Also: equal-dP keyed-orifice rule, 63 mm U-type rack manifold for low-dP plates, non-additive flow/supply-temperature levers, E0 buy-and-measure incumbent plates and UQD pairs, VR skirt with ~11% of flow: from system-platform.

Keyed inlet orifice on low-dP power and auxiliary plates; filtration-class grade ladder (R / P / coarse automotive); sintered direct-substrate SiC module as the power-electronics product (with judge-corrected 1.38x claim); galvanic rules for Cu in Al/WEG loops; selling power density rather than die area; Vsd(T) demonstrator; 'SSD converters' interpretation: from power-electronics.

One engine with the tier set only by post-braze face finishing; liquid-metal containment as a designed subsystem (electrolytic Ni or W barrier, no Au, FKM dam, moat, conformal coat, Galinstan); load-limited kinematic float with stiffener hard stops; pedestal crowned to hot-state warpage; TTV-C real-silicon vehicle; separable manifold cap as the in-silicon end-state play: from direct-to-die.

Swappable-insert single-cell coupon as a cheap kill/confirm test (applied to meter and kerf variants in E1/E2), inertial branch rule (branch >= 6x header head), leak-before-break by construction (internal layers carry only internal dP and tie loads), artwork-based zoning: from jet-hybrid.

New in the consolidation (own 2-D calculations): flux-graded flow length (4-5 / 6 / 8 / 12 mm by zone flux). It turns the uniform low-flux GPU-lid average loss of every proposal (-1 to -3 K) into a narrow win (-0.3 to -1.0 K).

open_risks: R1 Fin-tip tie braze (voids, wicking into 0.15 mm gaps, kerf damage). This is the single make-or-break item, gated at M3 (E1). Fallbacks: Ag-eutectic, then Cu-Sn/Ag-Sn TLP, then low-pressure diffusion bond. If all fail, a 1.5 mm tied base still beats CoolIT on max, dP and capacity (PCM 30.0/34.9 K).

Tie-bond inspection: C-SAM cannot see the joints. The pressurised differential flatness scan detects a 12 mm (critical-size) unbonded patch only marginally (~3 um bulge against ~1 um resolution). It must be validated in E1, backed by coupon CT/sectioning and sample proofs at 2 MPa.

Uniformity and 2-D physics are model-based. The meter sheet (~1.8 kPa), centre-fed plenums (1-D max/min 1.065-1.085) and kerfed 6 mm cells (2-D differential 0 K versus CoolIT's own +6.9%) must be confirmed by the E2 water table and the printed-manifold rig at M2-3.

The average-dT win depends on footprint. If CoolIT's heaters were 100 cm2, the like-for-like paste average is parity (34.0 vs 34.4 K), and PCM is 31.7 vs ~32.1 K on CoolIT re-tested with PCM. Max, dP, capacity and headroom wins hold at all footprints.
The OCP v1.0.0 recommended TIM is unverified. If it is a paste, the headline average margin roughly halves. Read the PDF in month 1.
At CoolIT's small single-die 4 kW point the drop-in R-grade only ties (0.0093 vs <0.009 C/W, PCM) and loses with paste (0.0105). Small high-flux dies need Tier 2 or the P-grade.

Per-plate factory cost is about US$160 against about US$110 for the incumbent at 100k/yr (+45%), and 8-10% worse per kW. Copper is at ~US$14.4-14.7k/t (Sept 2026), braze is fixture-limited, and RFQs are pending. The economics close only where facility value is priced in.

IP. The Split-Flow family includes the 2012 CIP branch ('691, '350, '878), running to ~Feb 2032 plus PTA, and '567 was revived in CoolIT v. Vidal (2024). Microfabrica US 12,255,123 (hybrid microjet + microchannel) and JetCool/Frore need claim charts. The kerf design-in and the offset-orifice fallback must be confirmed by counsel before any US sale.

Fouling, impaction and erosion. There is no shear self-cleaning at 0.15 m/s. Particles may deposit on the kerf floor under the meter jets (St ~1-2). The 10-year life is not claimed until the E4 1,000 h dosed test and a field pilot; the drop-in life without a tray cartridge is set by loop cleanliness.
A mandated Ni-plated wetted path (reported practice on GB200-class plates) has no qualified route with a 790 C BAg braze. TLP with pre-plated Ni is the only candidate.
Tier 2/3 liquid metal has no public reliability data above ~10 cm2; for bare die there is TIM1 and die-warranty liability. These stay stretch tiers until our warped-package cycling data exist.

Channel and moat. The concept practises expired Harpole/Cooligy art and every process is second-sourceable, so after a full OCP disclosure Group-A houses can copy it. The moat must come from process know-how, inspection methods, the zoning tool, data and customer co-design.

Schedule. The dominant failure mode is a 1-3 month slip at E1 or TTV commissioning (AlN heaters at ~129 W/cm2). The judged probability of the decisive public result at M12 is ~0.6, and ~0.75 for beating CoolIT on average, maximum and dP with PCM.
decisions_for_manager: D1 Claim scope and lead grade. Approve the public claim: PRISM 'beats CoolIT's 15 kW plate on every metric the OCP Cold Plate Test Spec v1.0.0 measures and on every metric CoolIT disclosed; parity on height; slightly heavier; more expensive per plate'. This states the 4 kW single-die tie and the 100 cm2-footprint average parity openly. Decide whether to lead with the drop-in R-grade (recommended) and whether to fund the P-grade plus tray-filter kit as the decisive like-for-like product, with the decision taken at gate G2 (M6).

D2 Channel and moat. Choose build-and-partner: supply hyperscaler custom-ASIC programmes first through a contract manufacturer under our recipe, inspection and test cell; then NVIDIA volume through a know-how-plus-supply partnership with a Group-A/B house. The moat is process know-how and data, not patents. The alternative, licence-first, has no defensible moat and thin Group-A margins.

D3 Budget and gating. Approve US$6.6 M for 12 months (US$9.5-10 M to an M18 qualified product, 14-15 FTE). Kill/pivot gates are M3 (tie braze, E1) and M6 (measured parity: PCM <=31/36 K, paste <=33 K average). Public release is at OCP Global Summit Oct 2027. Any US sale is gated on the Split-Flow (incl. CIP branch), Microfabrica and JetCool claim chart and opinion (US$80-140k).
